## Session 31, continued (2026-10-04) -- the frame profiler (step 13b-2)

Each race frame's time is in the log now, phase by phase and the draw
stage by stage. Retail's own profiler is ported: MainLoop's ten ticks,
CalculateFrameRate, and the two times it reads from the display. The
port adds a line a second. `docs/formats/frame-profiler.md` has the
write-up.

### The port

- **`mainloop.c`**:
  - MainLoopTiming (`0x002f0058`, the mdebug's type 3247): ten ticks,
    StartTime to LimitFrameRate.
  - CalculateFrameRate (`0x0012f090`):
    - the CPU's time is the frame less the GPU wait, floored at 0.1 ms;
    - the GPU's time is the VIF's;
    - 1000 over each is its rate;
    - all four are kept when bit 3 of RealTimeFrames changes.
  - MaybePrintTiming, `jr ra` in both images.
  - Retail's DoScreenPrintf loop over the cars changes nothing. It is
    left out, like `carfinish.c`'s.
- **`edisplay.c`**: WaitBufferSwapTime and VifTime, milliseconds in
  16.16 from bGetFixTickerDifference. GetWaitForBufferSwapTime and
  GetVifTime scale them by 2^-16.
- **`hudrender.c`**: DisplayDebugInfo's "C: %dfps" and "G: %dfps" print
  PreviousCpuFrameRate and PreviousGpuFrameRate, in place of the two
  names nothing wrote.
- **`main.c`**:
  - stamps the ten ticks at the port's own phase ends;
  - splits C3D_FrameBegin(C3D_FRAME_SYNCDRAW) into C3D_FrameSync and
    C3D_FrameBegin(0), so the blank's wait and the GPU's are timed
    apart. The GPU's wait is WaitBufferSwapTime, and
    C3D_GetDrawingTime is VifTime.
  - `SHOW_FRAME_RATES` (0) turns on DisplayPlayerDebugInfo for the
    HUD's rates.
  - At boot, a `console:` line: the model, New 3DS or not, the
    speedup, the memory type, the grant, the heap, linear, and core 1's
    limit.
- **`frameprof.c`**, the port's own: a `frame:` line a second of a race.
  - The frame rate, the mean frame and the longest.
  - Each phase.
  - The draw's nine stages. `main.c` and `trackview.c` stamp their
    ends.
  - The two waits, citro3d's two times, and retail's two rates.

### The checks

- **`mainloop_check`** runs CalculateFrameRate and the two getters out
  of the image. The script covers:
  - frames at 30, 20 and 60 a second;
  - the floors;
  - bit 3 of the frame count;
  - each other field off the frame's end;
  - the counter's wrap;
  - long and backwards frames;
  - a 400-op walk.

  11 scenarios, 4195 ops, 5097 lines, 0 differ. 46 mutations, 46
  caught.
- `hudrender_check`, `hudanim_check`, `hudcop_check` and
  `hudscore_check` define the two kept rates in their harnesses. `hudrender_check`'s `debug-fps-rounded`
  is caught.

The whole chain: 100 checkers and the four table generators in 1444 s. 1 of 104 failed: hudscore_check's harness, which links hudrender.c, did not define the two rates it now reads. With them it gives 1608 ops, 6184 lines, 0 differ, so 0 of 104 fail (`out/chain_13b2.txt`).

### On Azahar

The race on track 12, holding the gas, at Speed 100%
(`out/azahar_13b2b`):

- `console: New 3DS XL (model 4), New 3DS, speedup asked, memory type

## Session 31, continued (2026-10-04) -- New 3DS mode in full (step 13b-3)

Each part of New 3DS mode is checked at runtime now, not assumed from
`app.rsf`. The CIA could not reach the speedup, and now can. The heap is
sized from the grant. The jukebox worker's time is in the log, and the
draw's stages have the right names. `docs/formats/new3ds-mode.md` has
the write-up.

Between 13b-2 and 13b-3, commit 2260d0e made the minimap bigger, as the
user asked: `hudsplit_map_place` fits the displayed mode's box into the
bottom screen's free lower left, 176 by 116 pixels in mode 0 against
retail's 70 by 46 (`hud-split.md`, "The minimap's place").

### The port

- **`app.rsf`** adds `ptm:sysm`. libctru's `osSetSpeedupEnable` is
  `ptmSysmInit` then `PTMSYSM_ConfigureNew3DSCPU`, and APT makes the
  same call each time the app wakes. Without the service the call
  failed silently: the CIA ran at the ExHeader's clock, and nothing put
  it back after the HOME menu.
- **`heapcfg.c`**:
  - the linear heap asks for what is left after the heap's 48 MB, up to
    80 MB (`LINEAR_WANT`);
  - the malloc heap takes the rest, up to its 96 MB window
    (`HEAP_AREA`), and never less than 48 MB.

  A New 3DS's CIA gets 80 and 96. The .3dsx (124 MB) and an Old 3DS
  divide as before.
- **`main.c`**:
  - `logClock`, after the `console:` line, times a 2,000,000-turn
    `subs`/`bne` loop three times by the system tick: as launched, with
    the speedup off, and with it back on. The `clock:` line has whether
    ptm:sysm opened, the three times, and the last two's ratio.
  - The jukebox worker's time each frame of a race goes to the `frame:`
    line. Out of a race it has a line of its own every five seconds
    while a tune streams.
- **`jbstream.c`**: the worker sums its decode and read ticks, and
  `jbstream_busy` reads them.
- **`frameprof.c` and `trackview.c`**: the draw's stages renamed.
  13b-2's "cull" ended at `scenery_stuff_scenery`, so it timed the

## Session 31, continued (2026-10-04) -- the draw's first cuts (steps 13b-4a to 13b-4d)

The race on Azahar went from 20 FPS to 28-30, and the draw from 39-46 ms
to 26, with the same picture. Four cuts, each measured on its own run.
`docs/formats/draw-cuts.md` has why each one leaves the picture as it
was.

### The port

- **13b-4a, georender's runs** (`georender.c`, `trackview.c`).
  `georender_run_begin` and `_run_end` bracket a run of draws with
  nothing else drawn between them: `scenery_stuff_scenery`, and each
  envmap face's. Within a run, these go only when they change:
  - the program, the attributes, and the frame's uniforms (the
    projection, the light, the ambient, the fog's row);
  - the cull mode;
  - the pass;
  - the combiner and the ST scale;
  - the texture.

  A lit batch, the fog, the light, the depth range and the Z writes
  make the run forget what it sent. A one-run dump of a redwood's
  commands (454 words, six batches) showed what was being sent again.
  A `models:` line after each `frame:` line counts `render_model`'s
  models, batches, lit and held batches, and words (`frameprof.c`).
- **13b-4b, a mesh's buffer as one register.** After the draw that
  sends citro3d's `BufInfo`, a mesh's buffer in a run is one write of
  `GPUREG_ATTRIBBUFFER0_OFFSET`, in place of 40 words. The model-view
  goes only when it changes. `georender_run_end` marks citro3d's
  `BufInfo` changed, so its copy and the GPU agree again.
- **13b-4c, `c3dwrap.c`.** Every `C3D_DrawArrays` ran
  `C3D_UpdateUniforms` twice, for the vertex and the geometry shader.
  Each call tests 96 dirty flags one by one: about 1,200 instructions a
  draw with nothing to send. The Makefile's `C3DWRAP` links with
  `--wrap`, and the wrapper calls citro3d's function only when a public
  dirty flag is set, or a shader's constants may be waiting.
  `C3Di_LoadShaderUniforms` and `C3Di_DirtyUniforms` are wrapped to
  note those.
- **13b-4d, the Flailer layers from one walk** (`uirender.c`, `bui.c`).
  The port walked every visible screen's objects once for each of the
  29 layers. Each time it unpacked the whole object to compare its Z.
  `draw_visible` now builds the layer lists in one walk, as retail's
  AddFlailerStrip fills LayerRenderInfoTable. It reads only the Visible
  and Z bytes (`bui_object_layer`), then draws the layers in
  `BUI_LAYER_ORDER`. The order within a layer is unchanged: bundle,
  then screen, then the file's order.

### The checks

13b-4a to 13b-4c have no retail function behind them. 13b-4d keeps
eDisplayFrame's layer order, which `BUI_LAYER_ORDER` already held, and
draws the same objects in the same order, so its checkers are the
chain's Flailer ones. The whole chain: 100 checkers and the four table generators in 1468 s, 0 of 104 failed (`out/chain_13b4.txt`), `bui_check`, `flailer_check` and the HUD's among them.

## Session 31, continued (2026-10-04) -- the strips' flushes (step 13b-4e)

The draw on Azahar went from 26.1 ms to 23.3, and the cars stage from
4.3 to 2.6, with the same picture. `docs/formats/draw-cuts.md` has the
section.

### The port

- **The strips and quads are not flushed one at a time**
  (`georender.c`). `georender_draw_strip` and `draw_screen_quad` called
  `GSPGPU_FlushDataCache` on each strip's or quad's few vertices: a
  request to the GSP service each time. `C3D_FrameEnd(0)` flushes the
  whole linear heap after it queues the frame and before the GPU runs
  it (citro3d's disassembly: `__ctru_linear_heap` and its size, then
  `gxCmdQueueRun`). Both rings are `linearAlloc`'d, and every
  `C3D_FrameEnd` in `main.c` passes 0.
- **The last runs** (`trackview.c`, `georender.c`). The sky, the
  scenery's solid list and the cars' chain are each a georender run.
  The screen quads, the strips, the lit batches and the envmap's fold
  forget the run first, since they set citro3d's state themselves.
  `georender_draw` clears the run's pass after its own depth test.

### How it was found

A probe build (not committed) timed the cars stage's parts with
`svcGetSystemTick`. RenderCars took 1.5 ms: the shadows 0.5, the body
0.65, the tyres 0.3. The solid list took 0.1 and the alpha list 2.7. In
the alpha list, 27 strips took 2.33 ms, 86 µs each, against about 20 µs
for each of 20-35 held batches. Without the flushes the strips take
0.68 ms.

### The checks

No retail function changed, and no checker builds `georender.c` or
`trackview.c`. The chain: 0 of 104 failed, 1483 s (out/chain_13b4e.txt).

- **The checker agrees with retail:** 7373 ops, 459051 lines, 0 differ.
  The mutation pass catches 264 of 273. Nine are equivalent: SC-1's
  five, and four of SC-2c's, each argued in EQUIVALENT:
  - `urcp-flip-y`: the identity's v0.y is 0, and eRotateZ's sums lose
    the sign of the -0;
  - `urcp-tire-roll`: eRotateY by 0 is an exact identity;
  - `urcp-wheel-w`: eIdentity already put 1 in the brake's v3.w;
  - `light-one-skin`: a one-skin car's index can only be 0.
- **Mutation passes are quicker: `tools/mutpar.py`.** The user asked
  for it: a two-hour pass doesn't fit in a session. carsel, selcam and
  fecar use it now:
  - The model's transcript is cached under a sha256 of the checker up
    to its mutations and of every source and header. A pass after an
    EQUIVALENT-only edit skips the model.
  - Once the model is done, a snapshot copies the sources and every
    header in `3DS Files/source` into a temporary directory and builds
    them once. That build has to give the base transcript, or the pass
    stops.
  - Each mutant is built from the snapshot, never the tree. A source
    mutant compiles one file and links with the snapshot's objects; a
    header mutant compiles a whole copy of the snapshot. So the tree
    may be edited and built while the mutants run.
  - Up to sixteen mutants build and run at once, and the lines print
    in the pass's order.
  - `hostbuild.build_objects` builds uncached objects with a chosen
    include path, and hostbuild's object cache key now covers every
    header, so a header edit can't reuse a stale object.
  carsel's pass took 11m42s, about 8 minutes of it the model (it was
  24 minutes); fecar's takes 25 s and selcam's 43 s.

Not ported: the system's destructor (0x0012a398) and the static fini
(0x0012a1e0). Both run only at exit.

**AddAutoEmitter (0x001274a0):**
1. If RandomSeed (+36) is 0, step AcidRandomSeed (gp-23504, 0x23985727
   at boot) by xorshift: `x^=x<<17; x^=x>>13; x^=x<<5`. Then
   RandomSeed = cvt.w.s(((float)(int)(x & 0x7fffffff) * 2^-31) * 2^31),
   which saturates.
2. Then by the data and State:
   - A NULL data, or State 2: set State to 2 and add to the tail.
   - State <u 2 (0 OFF, 1 ON): take the cycle and its variance from the
     data, On (32/36) for ON and Off (40/44) for OFF.
     - If the cycle is not zero (c.eq.s, so -0 counts as zero):
       w = var * cycle; xorshift the emitter's own seed;
       cycle = (cycle - w) + unit(seed) * w.
     - Add to the **head**, with RemainingCycleTime = cycle and
       EmissionCountdown = 0.
   - State 3 (LIBRARY): add to the tail.
   - Any other State: set it to 2 and add to the tail.
3. NumAutoEmitters (+80) goes up in every case.

**The disc's data:**
- GLOBALB has 111 datas (0x35021 at 0xa3480) and 112 emitters (0x35020
  at 0xb2080), all LIBRARY.
- Each of the 30 tracks, TRACKB11..16, 21..26, 31..36, 41..46 and
  61..66, has both packs: 1 to 20 datas and 10 to 40 emitters, all ON.
- Every Acid chunk is at the top level. On the disc, the pointers,
  RandomSeed and the cycle times are all 0.
- XE_SelectCarNebula is GLOBALB's one FE_EMITTER data.
- One thing to check in SC-3d: GLOBALB's group is
  CARFX_BREAK_LICENSE_PLATE_REAR, but carrenderinfo.c's kCarFxNames has
  CARFX_BREAK_LICENSE_PLATE_RIGHT. See whether retail's string table
  says RIGHT too.

**The harness (`afx_test.c SCRIPT RECORDS`):**
- RECORDS is two int32s, the data count and the emitter count, then
  the 544-byte datas and the 192-byte emitters.
- The harness rebuilds each record in the host's layout. A non-zero
  disc pointer becomes the pattern pointer, "pat".
- It defines its own slot pools: fixed arenas, the lowest free slot,
  zeroed if flags&2 and 0xa5 otherwise. They print "newpool", "omalloc
  pp|gp|ep -> name" (or null or full), "free pool name" and "delpool".
- Its GetTextureInfo prints "gti hash ud iu -> tN|null". Mode is
  hash%3, or set by TXM: 0 gives NULL, 1 a match, 2 NameHash^1.
- Names: D/E k.c.i for records, p/g/e n for slots, gN.pl, t N, L N,
  FE.act, FE.auto, WE.act, WE.auto and EDL. A list's i-th node is
  `list.i`, and "r" is the last CP, RA, GD or GE result.
- Ops:
  - B n
  - D (the full dump), DL k (list k in full), DE e (one emitter in full)
  - BR k (reset buffer k)
  - CH k type ver count mis kind(D/E/-) first
  - S, I, C
  - L k c, U k c, LA k, UA k (newest first)
  - T, TXM hash mode
  - GD name group after, GE name group after
  - CP e, NL k, GS k group, DS k
  - SD e d, SH e hash
  - AA sys e, RA sys e
  - K sys, MG sys e np (a group with np particles, on the head), GX g
    flags
  - ED e flags, ED2 e flags
  - CT sys
  - PE e field val, with fields st rc ec rs de nh dh d nm nmz
  - PD d field val, with fields on onv off offv nh gh th tex
  - SEED v, F pool n (the pool fails after n more)

  Every op but D, DL, DE, BR, CH, PE, PD, SEED and F ends with a short
  line, "s n .. seed .. edl .. FE a/b/c WE a/b/c".
- Names print with non-ASCII as '.'. Floats print as bits, with any NaN
  as "nan". Hashes passed to retail must be sign-extended (s32) in the
  model, because the image compares 64-bit registers.

**The model (afx_check.py):**
- **Memory:** fake pools at 0x01000000 + 64*i, with flags at +20 set to
  15. The arenas are at 0x01010000, 0x01020000 and 0x01030000 (32, 28
  and 192 bytes a slot). The lists are at 0x01080000, the textures at
  0x01090000 (164 bytes, NameHash at +32), and the buffers at
  0x01100000 + k*0x100000. The records are in the disc's layout, with
  the Node and any non-zero pointer set to 0xa5a5a5a5.
- **Stubs:** bNewSlotPool 0x00257c10, bDeleteSlotPool 0x00257c48,
  bOMalloc 0x00257c80, bFree(pool, p) 0x00257ca0, and GetTextureInfo
  0x001abf48. bFree(void*) 0x00257850 traps. bStringHash, bStrNCpy and
  bMemSet run as shipped. Assert that word 8 of the image is 0.
- **Scenarios:**
  - the boot over GLOBALB and TRACKB12, with lookups, GS over the 26
    CARFX names and FE_EMITTER, then the unloads and close;
  - all 30 tracks in turn over GLOBALB;
  - AddAutoEmitter's edges, over emitter records in a version-6 chunk
    so they don't load: every state, a NULL data, cycles of
    0/-0/NaN/inf/denormal, the variances, and seeds made by inverting
    the xorshift so that unit*2^31 rounds to 2^31;
  - versions, other types, count 0 and mis 0/4/8/12;
  - copies with the pool failing, 63-char names, and every delete
    flag;
  - MG/K/GX and close with groups;
  - TXM texture modes;
  - a fuzz that tracks what "r" holds, so it never adds a linked

  As written, s_tracks takes the 30 tracks six to a scenario, and the
  fuzz runs three times: 400 ops on TRACKB12, 1200 on TRACKB24 and 2500

### The hang's watchdog

The user's first race on a New 3DS XL stopped after frame 1, with HOME
dead (CONTINUE.md). `hangwatch.c` says where, into `nfshp2_debug.txt`;
it changes nothing that is drawn.

- The main loop and the draw are marked (`hangwatch_mark`, a pointer
  and a count). A watchdog thread, one priority above the main
  thread's and on its core, logs the last 16 marks when no frame has
  begun for 3 s, again at 10 s and every 30 s, and `frames again` if
  they come back. It also logs whether the marks still move, citro3d's
  GX queue (entries, sent, done, and what is left), and a few GPU
  registers through GSPGPU_ReadHWRegs. aptMainLoop's wait is HOME or
  sleep, and is not reported.
- The GPU check, for the first 3 frames of each race: at the end of
  each draw stage (the cull, each envmap view, the fold, the sky, the
  models, the scenery, the cars, the HUD, the bottom screen) the
  commands so far go to the GPU and are waited on for 2 s. The linear
  heap is flushed first, as C3D_FrameEnd flushes it, and the queue is
  stopped after, as the frame had it. A stage that does not finish is
  `NOT done`, with the queue and the registers.
- A frame's most GX entries is logged when it grows: citro3d's queue
  holds 32, and gxCmdQueueAdd's 33rd is svcBreak. The race has 9 at
  most, the car select 6.
- Read from libctru and citro3d's objects: gxCmdQueueWait's timeout is
  in ticks, though gx.h says nanoseconds, and it waits on
  gspWaitForAnyEvent, which the vertical blanks wake. gxCmdQueueStop
  with nothing running clears the bound queue; gxCmdQueueRun binds it
  again, as C3D_FrameEnd does.
- On Azahar the race keeps 30 FPS with 0 unmapped accesses, its 36
  stage checks finish, and the car select passes with no watchdog line.
  A build with a 5 s spin and then a sleep at world frames 200 and 400
  (taken out again) had the watchdog log both: `still moving` and
  `frames again after 5.1 s`, then `none moving` at 3 s and 10 s.

For the device: copy `NFSHP2-3DS.cia` (or the `.3dsx`), hold R at
boot, and give it 15 s after it stops before powering off.

**The device's answer (2026-10-05).** The New 3DS XL's log
(`3DS Files/Hang Test Build/nfshp2_debug_first_watchdog.txt`) has the
first race frame (21) pass the cull and stop in envmap view 0: the GX
queue's fill (the face's clear) done, and its command list (57 KB, from
the frame's start) never done. That is the first georender draw of the
boot, since R skips the car select. The watchdog's register read
through GSP never came back, nor did its 10 s line, so the GPU's
registers stopped answering too: the GPU is wedged, not just late.
Azahar's log has nothing for that run.

**The draw check** (`hangwatch.c`, the rest of it) says which draw.
`-Wl,--wrap` on C3D_DrawArrays, C3D_DrawElements (citro2d's),
C3D_FrameBegin and C3D_BindProgram reads citro3d's command buffer back
into a shadow of the PICA's registers, from boot to the end of the first
race's checked frames, then stops. At each draw it checks the vertex
buffers, the index buffer, the three texture units (and a cube's five
other faces), the colour and depth buffers, the viewport and the scissor
against the linear heap and VRAM, and the attribute counts against the
shader's inputs. In the first checked frame each draw is logged
(`draw N at <mark>: ...`) and then sent and waited on alone; a draw over
20 ms says so. Marks inside the stages name the sky, the scenery and the
lists of each envmap view and of the player's view.
- After each wait the GX queue is stopped and cleared, as citro3d's own
  sync transfer does within a frame: the draws one at a time are 1781
  entries in frame 21, and the queue's 33rd is svcBreak.
- HANGWRAP has to come before C3DWRAP in the Makefile: C3DWRAP's `:=`
  took it empty, and the first build linked no wrapper at all.
- On Azahar frame 21 takes 3.7 s, with 1781 draws (envmap views 0, 1 and
  5: 2 sky, 103 to 211 scenery, 22 to 24 list draws each; the fold, 3;
  the player's view, 2 sky, 1068 models, 58 sun, 99 cars), and 0 issues.
  The race goes on at 30 FPS after.

The build is in `3DS Files/Hang Test Build/`. In the device's log, the
last `draw N` line before `gpu check: draw N NOT done` is the draw that
stops the GPU.

## Session 34 (2026-10-05) -- the New 3DS XL's race hang; SC-3c's CPU half

The user ran each build on a New 3DS XL and put its `nfshp2_debug.txt`
in `3DS Files/Hang Test Build/`. Each log is kept there by name. Every
one stopped at the boot's first georender draw. That is the first 3D
the device ever drew: with R held at boot, the frontend's 3D never
draws.

### What each build found

- **The draw check** (`nfshp2_debug_draw_check.txt`, commit 25b31d3).
  It stopped at draw 1, the sky into envmap face 0, a 16-bit RGBA5551
  colour buffer over a 32-bit D24S8 depth buffer. Every address was in
  range.
- **RGBA8 faces** (`nfshp2_debug_rgba8_face.txt`, 1644100). Same stop,
  with the face now RGBA8. So the pair was not it. The faces stay RGBA8
  until a device run tries 5551 again.
- **The probe** (`nfshp2_debug_probe.txt`, 8f165d3). `georender_probe`
  draws one geosolid triangle at a time before the envmap, each with a
  feature more than the last. It stopped at the first one: onto the top
  screen, with no texture and no depth test.
- **The vertex stride** (`nfshp2_debug_stride_fix.txt`, 62924cd).
  3dbrew's GPU/Pitfalls: a loader's attributes must fill the stride
  CONFIG2 gives it. GeoRenderVertex's were float3, float2, ubyte4 and
  byte3, 27 bytes, against a stride of 28. The normal now loads as four
  bytes, the pad its w. The draw check now works out each loader's size
  by the PICA's alignment and logs it (`4/28=28`). The device still
  stopped at the probe's first triangle.
- **The check's flush order** (`nfshp2_debug_flush_fix.txt`, 04aa510).
  hangwatch's `gpu_wait` flushed the linear heap and then called
  C3D_FrameSplit, which writes the list's FINALIZE. On the New 3DS
  (2 MB L2) those words could stay in the cache. It now splits, flushes
  and runs, as C3D_FrameEnd does. The device still stopped at the same
  triangle.
- **The output components** (this session's last build, 02:30). With
  the stride, units, depth test and target ruled out, the shader is
  what is left. 3dbrew's GPU/Pitfalls: "Each configured output component
  has to be written exactly once or the PICA freezes."
  GPUREG_SH_OUTMAP_MASK enables output registers whole, so all four
  components of each count.
  - `.out outtex texcoord0` gets the mask xyzw from picasso. geosolid
    wrote only `.x` and `.y` of its `texcoord0` and `texcoord1`. geolit
    never wrote o1.w or o3.zw, and geofold never wrote o1.w.
  - The user pointed at NFSU2-3DS, which drew its world on hardware.
    Its three shaders (`car`, `scene`, `vshader`) and citro2d's
    `render2d` (dumped from libcitro2d.a) all write every component of
    every output. The rest of NFSU2's world path is ours: citro3d,
    RGBA8 over D24S8, float loaders that fill their 32-byte stride.
  - The fix writes the missing components as zeros, once on every path.
  - `tools/check_shbin.py` follows each DVLE's code both ways through
    every IFU and IFC. It counts each output register's component writes
    on each path to END, and flags two MOVAs in a row. CALL, LOOP, JMP
    and BREAK are refused as not followed. `build_cia.ps1` runs it on
    `build/*.shbin` after check_3dsx. It passes the fixed three,
    NFSU2's three and citro2d's, and fails the old three on exactly the
    components above.
  - On Azahar the checked frame passes every draw, with 0 unmapped
    accesses, the race at 29.5 FPS, and the picture as before.
  - The build is with the user. If the race runs, take the probe and
    the per-draw check out and try 5551 faces. If it stops, the last
    `draw N at` line names the draw.

### Earlier wrong turns, for the record

- CONTINUE.md said, after the stride fix, that each output component
  was written once in all three shaders. It was wrong: picasso gives
  an output with no mask named all four components, and the shaders
  wrote two. `tools/check_shbin.py` reads the binary now.
- The RGBA5551/D24S8 pair, and then the check's own flush order, were
  each taken for the cause in turn. The flush-order fix was real, but
  the device's stop did not move.

### SC-3c, RenderEffects' CPU half (not committed)

`acid_system_render_effects` (retail 0x00128da0) in `acidsys.c`, with
`acidz` (gp-23440, 4) and the `gEAttachDirectDataFn` seam (eAttachDirect
Data, 0x00110378). It builds each group's GS packet in frame memory as
retail does: a REGLIST tag of PRIM, RGBAQ and four ST/XYZ2 pairs; 80
bytes a sprite; the packet stops 33 words before CurrentBufferEnd. It
hands the packet over with the sprites' mean truncated view depth.
- A corner's Z is (bits(sc.z) & 0x0fffffff) >> acidz. The scenery's
  packed XYZF2 takes bits 4..27 of the same float, so a particle's Z is
  the scenery's real GS Z.
- `tools/mipsemu.py` gained vftoi0. afx_check runs 30 scenarios with 0
  differ. Its mutation pass has 394 mutants: 390 caught, 4 equivalent,
  0 unexplained.
- Still owed: the section in `docs/formats/acidfx.md`, the commit, and

## Session 35 (2026-10-05) -- the race runs on the device; mip chains and a GPU timing frame

### The device's run

- The user's run of the Hang Test Build (02:30) loaded the race and
  drove it. The shaders' output components were the hang. The log is
  `3DS Files/Hang Test Build/nfshp2_debug.txt`.
- 8 FPS, held by the GPU: 113-120 ms a frame, the models' list 78 ms of
  it and each envmap view 5-7 ms (the per-draw check's times). The CPU's
  part is about Azahar's. 39 MB of the linear heap was free after the
  track.
- The user asked for options that keep retail's look whole and use the
  hardware to the full, as questions. Their answers (memory
  gpu-speed-plan): lossless textures only; the disc's mip chains and
  made ones for the single-level textures; a timing build first; then
  indexed meshes and the early depth test, each kept only if the
  device's log shows it helps.

### Mip chains (commit 0355be5)

- GS TEX1's MMIN: 0 NEAREST, 1 LINEAR, 2 NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST, 3
  NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR, 4 LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST, 5
  LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR. Every track and car record has MMAG 1 and MMIN
  3: linear up close, nearest in a level, linear between levels.
  TexInfo now carries both (record bytes 0x6f and 0x70), and
  `texpack_upload_chain` sets the PICA's filters from them.
- The disc's chains: each level is within 2-5 of 255 of the 2x2 mean of
  the one above in colour. A cut-out's levels keep its two alphas: 99%
  of texels with 3 or 4 opaque parents are opaque, 70% with 2, 0.2%
  with 1. The made levels follow that: the mean, and for a cut-out
  (`texpack_cutout_alpha`) opaque when 2 or more of 4 are.
- A chain is padded to powers of two as `texpack_upload` pads (the edge
  repeated) and stops at 8 texels on the shorter side, the PICA's
  smallest; the disc's chains stop there too.
- `texpack_chain_tiled` (portable) writes every level straight into the
  PICA's tiles. A made level is made from the level above where it
  already is: in Morton order the four texels under one are four words
  in a row. So the heap takes only the decoded level.
  `texpack_test --chain` reads the tiles back, and its CRCs are the
  same as the first version's for every texture of TEX12LOCATION (from
  levels 0 and 1), TEX12TRACK, CARS/TEXTURES, DYNTEX and DRIVTEX.
  `texpack_check.py --chain` matches them against `texture_convert.py`.
- trackview picks a texture's level by the chain's size (`chain_bytes`):
  about 38 MB for the track where level 0 alone was 28.9. 24.7 MB of
  the linear heap is left on Azahar. A chain that will not upload falls
  back to the one level, counted as `unchained`.
- **The transparent car.** The first build made the levels in two heap
  buffers, the padded level and its half: 1.25 MB for the Speedster's
  512x320 skin. The race's heap has about 6 MB free after the track,
  in pieces, and the skin did not upload. The solids listing showed
  `OPEL_SKIN1!` and the texture line 1 missing; the car drew with only
  its env map's reflection, which the user saw as transparent. The
  tiled build fixed it: 0 missing, 0 unchained, the paint back. The
  track-load line now logs the heap's free KB beside the linear heap's.

### The timing frame (hangwatch.c)

- The probe (`georender_probe`) and the per-draw check are gone, with
  the Makefile's wraps for them. The watchdog stays as it was.
  `georender_forget` is new, for the frame's resends.
- Every 10 s of a race, the first 5 s in, one frame ends each draw
  stage with a split, a flush and a wait, and logs `gpu time: frame N:`
  with each stage's ms and the sum. The split's list is checked against
  the GX queue's last entry first, and citro3d is told to send all its
  state again after it.
- The models' list and the first envmap view's are copied and sent
  again onto a 400x240 RGBA8 target and a D24S8 depth buffer in VRAM
  (banks A and B), cleared before each. The copy's commands are walked
  and patched: the targets (0x11C-0x11E), the scissor (0x065-0x067),
  NUMVERTICES (0x228), the three units' sizes, LODs, addresses and types
  for the 8x8 stand-in, and TEXUNIT_CONFIG's cache-clear bit (0x080,
  bit 16). Five ways: as drawn; 8x8 textures; a 1-pixel scissor; that
  and 3 vertices a draw; no texture cache clears. CONTINUE.md says how
  to read the differences.
- On Azahar: envmap view 0 is about 205 draws, 30-41k vertices; the
  models 120-1090 draws as the view turns, about one cache clear a draw.
  The race keeps 30 FPS with a 63-66 ms hitch at each timing frame.
  Every GPU time is about 0.12 ms there, which says nothing; the
  device's say it all.

### The hitches and the ramp (commit 8bf178a)

- The race's once-a-second log lines cost their frame 50-60 ms, 150-240
  while the card was slow, once 1.2 s. `logwriter.c` copies each line
  into a 128 KB ring; a thread one priority below the main loop, on core
  2 of a New 3DS (else 1, else any), writes and flushes. The main loop
  waits only on a full ring. stderr stays synchronous, for abort
  reasons; atexit drains the ring.
- The timing frame is a hitch of about 150 ms each 10 s, so it runs only
  with `sdmc:/nfshp2_gputiming.txt` on the card at the race's start, and
  the log says which.
- The ramp: `carfinish: Player::IsJumpCamAvailable is not ported`. The
  seam is `no_jump_cam` (CleanUpJumpCam and 0, retail's answer for a
  route too short): no zone is requested and the car flies on under the
  drive camera.

### 13b-4f: indexed meshes (609b418)

Session 36's device timing put the models' vertex work at about 7.5 ms
of the GPU's frame. That is the one large share that can be cut without
changing a pixel.

- **The strips.** TRACKB12's 133,795 triangles are in 10,394 strips,
  mostly runs of separate quads cut by ADC restarts. As a list they are
  401,385 vertices. As GPU strips joined by degenerates they would be
  335,909, only 16% fewer, so strips were tried first and dropped.
  Indexed, with each distinct vertex once a solid, they are 176,505.
  The `stripstats` scripts that measured this were scratch, not kept.
- **The cache.** A simulated first-in-first-out post-vertex cache
  shades this many vertices a triangle in the strips' order: 1.70 with
  4 entries, 1.62 with 8, 1.54 with 16, against the list's 3.
- **The code.** `georender_bake` hashes each vertex's 28 bytes and
  writes three 16-bit indices a triangle. One `linearAlloc` block holds
  the vertices, then the indices. The draws use `C3D_DrawElements`. The
  linear heap for TRACKB12's meshes falls from 11.2 MB to 5.8.
- **The cost.** Each draw writes 8 command words more for the triangle
  element mode: 63,274 words a frame for 312 models against 54,338.
- **The check.** The baseline (the list) and the indexed build were
  both captured on Azahar 6 s in (`out/cap_list`, `out/cap_idx`). The
  depth buffers match to the bit. The colour differs in 85 pixels by at
  most 5, round the car, whose reflection is the envmap's. The envmap's
  faces draw on a schedule that the capture's hitch moves.
- **The capture's own fault.** The lod0 frames differed more: the
  Opel's window was pink in one. The numbered frame had painted the
  envmap's faces and fold in their numbers, and a face keeps what it
  drew until it draws again. `capture_offscreen` now leaves the
  envmap's draws as they are in the numbered and level-0 frames.
- **On Azahar** (`out/azahar_idx2`): 29.2 FPS with 300 to 380 models in
  view, 0 unmapped accesses. Azahar's GPU is not the device's, so only
  the device's timing lines can show the gain.

`docs/formats/draw-cuts.md`, "13b-4f: indexed meshes", has it all. The
`models:` line now ends each half with the batches' indices.

### The Old 3DS (6ac29d1)

The user's Old 3DS crashed back to the Homebrew Launcher on holding R

### Step 11a: what an AI car knows as it drives

The racer AI starts with the records every AI car keeps:
- a NearbyCarList, the cars around it;
- a DrivingLocation, the route, point and line it drives;
- a DrivingChoice, the line or the side of a car it has chosen.

`nearbycar.c` has the list's BuildArray, ClearArray and three lookups,
DrivingInformation's Clear and five of the AI's free functions.
`drivinglocation.c` has the location's methods. `drivetarget.h`'s
stand-in for the location is gone; AddPointToTarget reads the line's
low byte as retail does.

`nearbycar_check` runs the retail image in mipsemu as the oracle, with
only the belt mover's gravity stubbed. It has 36 scenarios, 10,309
lines and 0 differ, and catches all 99 mutations. Things the image
showed:
- BuildArray keeps the car itself in its own list, at its own origin.
- A car tried and not kept leaves its Position, Velocity and TheCar in
  the next free entry.
- The sort keeps ties and NaNs in their order.
- CalculateMaxAcceleration's cap keeps the drag force when it is below
  the table's acceleration, a force kept as an acceleration, as retail
  has it.
- A straight line's curvature is -0.
- GetNumSecondsLeftInRelaxedSwitch takes the tick difference as a
  signed word.
`docs/formats/ai-driving-info.md` has the rest. The ten other checkers
that link `drivetarget.c` still have 0 differ, and the 3DS build
succeeds. Nothing in the race calls these yet, so the build plays as
2fc77fc.

### Step 11b-1: retail's DriveTarget

DrivingChoice builds its targets with DriveTarget, and the port's was
the demo's. Retail's differs in five places:
- a byte at 516, LastPointToScore, which Clear sets to -1 and
  BuildDriveTargetAroundCar to the last point around a car;
- its accessor, EstimateScore's last corner;
- CalculateMaxSpeed split in two;
- a first corner asked from the car itself;
- EstimateScore's two walks rebuilt on those.
The rest moved with CarState's fields and nothing else.

A car at rest divides by zero twice in the from-car corner, where the
EE gives FLT_MAX and the corner fits. IEEE's infinity and NaN would
score every car at rest -1. Both divides are `ee_div`, the projection
and `bNormalize2To`'s first; the image check lists exactly those two
sites as the ones that took the EE's path.

`drivetarget_check` models retail's listing, and the image check runs
retail's image: 22 scenarios, 993 lines, 0 differ. The model's
mutation pass: 288 mutations, 268 caught, 20 equivalent, each argued.
`ct-no-clear` is caught now, since retail's Clear writes the byte the
memset leaves 0.

The 54 checkers that link `drivetarget.c` or `bvector.c` still have 0
differ. The ones whose oracle is the demo image and runs Clear hook its
tail for retail's -1 (`physicscar_check.retail_clear`), and
`drivecam_check`'s oracle divides the EE's way: its outside view takes
the same `bNormalize2To` divide below 8.32 m/s.
`docs/formats/car-drive-target.md` has the detail.

Next is 11b-2: DrivingChoice's small methods and the walk along the
route (retail 0x00241b88 .. 0x002455f8 is DrivingChoice.obj; the
demo's AdvancePoint and GetRoutePointsToUse are there, unnamed).

### Step 11b-2: DrivingChoice's small methods and the walk

`drivingchoice.c` is the choice and what a line choice does with it:
- the small methods: GetChoiceType, GetDrivingLine, the three
  SetChoices, Clear, IsValid and IsEqualTo;
- the side tests: IsEnoughRoom, FixupCarToExcludeFromCollisionPrediction
  and GetPreferredSideOfCar;
- the walk along the route: FuturePointList::Add, AdvancePoint,
  GetRoutePointsToUse and the road block's point list;
- the filling: GetSpeedBackToLine, ReduceCurrentL, AddToDriveTarget and
  FillUpDriveTarget.
Race::GracePeriodIsActive went into `racecore.c`, and as much of
AICarController's record as these read into `aicarcontroller.h`.
SignPostDecision is a seam, `gAISignPostDecisionFn`, which main.c points
at the port's since 11e-2.

`drivingchoice_check` runs the image as the model, with three stubs:
SignPostDecision, Car::GetRoutePoint and GetAmountOutOfBounds. The
result: 45 scenarios, 20,697 ops, 25,798 lines, 0 differ. The mutation
pass made 240 mutations: 239 caught, 1 equivalent. `fx-its-side` drops
a side test that the two type tests under it already imply.

The first pass left 14 alive, and closing them found these gaps in the
script, not in the port:
- **The grace period's globals.** Both sides set them at each
  scenario's start, so `racecore.c`'s initialisers were never compared.
  The model now starts them from the image's own data, and the harness
  from the port's.
- **The bend rule.** It needs a curvature near 0.12, and the noisy
  routes never gave one. A smooth route, with points evenly spaced,
  turning evenly and every line on the centre, has a curvature of
  exactly sin(6 turn). `s_bend` runs seven curvatures, 0.09 to 0.3,
  both ways round. Its roads are wide enough that no side is ever
  blocked, so each rule's choice shows unflipped.
- **FindClosestPointAhead's NULL.** It comes back when the other car is
  past the route's next-to-last point. Taking the fallback away now
  crashes, and moving it a point on is caught too.
- **The else branch of where the target ends.** GetRouteAndRoutePoint
  fails only on a point number of -1. The walk survives that only for a
  racer whose target ends on a traffic route, since it then walks from
  the location.
- **A sign crossed at no speed.** It is rare in the random fills, so
  `s_fill` now has ten of them.
- **A full list of twenty.** This needed a look-ahead of 400 m.

The five divergences are written down in the source and in
`docs/formats/ai-driving-choice.md`. Each one is where the image reads
through a NULL, a stray pointer or a stack word, or has no bound:
- GetRoutePointsToUse with no route at the target's end;
- the road-block list from a clear location;
- FillUpDriveTarget's uninitialised choice;
- AddToDriveTarget's w;
- the route table's top.
`racecore_check`, `racerun_check`, `nearbycar_check` and
`drivetarget_check` still have 0 differ. The CIA builds.

Next is 11b-3: BuildDriveTarget (0x00241ea0) and
BuildDriveTargetAroundCar (0x00243aa8) with its helpers.

### Step 11b-3: BuildDriveTarget and round a car

`drivingchoice.c` now builds the target for a choice:
- BuildDriveTarget (0x00241ea0): an invalid choice fills up as asked, a
  line fills up on that line, and a side goes round the car;
- BuildDriveTargetAroundCar (0x00243aa8): the point beside the car with
  room to pass, the way out to it, the car's own target alongside when
  it is a player or traffic, then the line again;
- its helpers: MakeDriveTargetParallelToCar (0x00243f70),
  DoSmoothOffsetChange (0x00244ea0), the clearance (0x002442c0), the
  walk's closest point ahead (0x00244d80) and how far a lateral is off
  the road (0x002455b0).
The traffic tuning mode and the two slow speeds are `.sdata` words
nothing writes: AITrafficTuningMode, AISlowCarSpeed and
AISlowTrafficSpeed, by the port's names.

`drivingchoice_check` has four new kinds of scenario: s_around,
s_pieces, s_sign_pass and s_back. The result: 71 scenarios, 46,212
ops, 79,543 lines, 0 differ. The model now runs with the EE's divide.
The one divide by zero the script takes is DoSmoothOffsetChange's slope
(0x00245050), when the walk's first and last points are in one place.
The port spells it ee_div, and the checker stops if any other site
takes the EE's path. The mutation pass made 385 mutations: 383 caught,
22 of them by a crash or a hang, and 2 equivalent. `sm-full` drops a
full-target test that AddPointToTarget makes again.

The first pass left 13 alive, gaps in the script, not in the port:
- the near cars never slid, nor went at 20.5, 10.5, -25 or exactly 5,
  nor had two wheels down;
- the cars' own targets never ran back or onto another route;
- the three globals were never moved;
- no car stood past the look-ahead, and no walk crossed a sign onto a
  route just to one side.
Two needed s_back. `sm-cap-up` wants a walk that doubles back, so a
point before the last is further from the first; the reworked s_pieces
had stopped making one. `mp-from` wants a car alongside on a traffic
route whose own target runs back down the walk, so each search for the
road starts where the last one ended.

Two more divergences are written down: BuildDriveTargetAroundCar's
entry, which the image reads with no NULL test, and the new points' w

Next is 11b-4: CarCollisionPredict's four live functions, then
IsDriveable, TryChoice, TryToDriveAroundCar and MakeNewChoice.

### Step 11b-4a: CarCollisionPredict

11b-4 is two slices now. 11b-4a is CarCollisionPredict
(`carcollisionpredict.c`): which car an AI car's target runs it into,
and when. It has the four live methods and the three free functions
under them:
- WhoWillThisDriveTargetHit (0x001e5e60): of the cars worth caring
  about, the first hit. A car stopped just ahead counts at 0. A car my
  controller leaves out, or my car at under 0.001 m/s, never counts.
  The world's CollisionPredictionID goes up once for each car tried;
- IsThisCarStoppedDirectlyInFrontOfMe (0x001e6010);
- WillIHitThisCar (0x001e60a0): the two targets are copied, then
  filled, blended or straightened by who is traffic and who is backing
  up blind. They are turned into boxes and walked together, one leg at
  a time;
- MakeOBBsForDriveTarget (0x001e6860): a box per point, the first along
  the car and the rest along their legs;
- WhenWillOverlapOccur2D (0x001e72f8), TimeIntervalForSeparatingAxis
  (0x001e7238) and IntervalOverlap (0x001e6ac0): when two moving boxes
  first overlap on the ground, axis by axis.
SeparatingAxisTest, OBBOverlap2D, OBBOverlap3D and TimeToImpact have no
callers and are left out.

The walk divides by a leg's length, and a leg of 0 (a repeated point)
divides 0 by 0. On the EE that is FLT_MAX, which leaves the car where it
is, so both divides (0x001e65ec, 0x001e65f4) are ee_div. Retail keeps
the two copies and forty boxes in a 4720-byte stack frame; the port
keeps them static. Two of retail's corners are kept as they are:
- a still axis with the boxes apart answers 9999, so two crawling cars
  "hit" at 9999 s;
- a miss after a long step comes out past 99999, which is a no.

`drivingchoice_check` links it, and `obb.c` with it. There are seven new
ops: 1 to 7 call the seven functions, and op 4 dumps every box. There
are four new kinds of scenario:
- s_predict: my car on a route with cars following, oncoming, crossing,
  beside, stopped, behind and backing;
- s_parts: the three free functions at their edges, and MakeOBBs;
- s_meet: two cars that do meet a second or more on;
- s_stopped: the stopped test's bounds.
The result is 98 scenarios, 61,530 ops, 97,604 lines, 0 differ. The
first run showed 1072 lines differing, all in the box dump: the
harness's `fx` has sixteen buffers and the line printed nineteen.

The mutation pass made 207 mutations of `carcollisionpredict.c`. All
are caught, and the checker's 592 have 590 caught and the old 2
equivalent. The first pass left 25 alive, all gaps in the script:
- Most hits were at 0, with the boxes overlapping already, where the
  path ahead does not matter. That hid the backing-up path, the blends
  and the step's edges. s_meet makes hits a second or more on: head on,
  catching up, at a crossing, either car backing into the other, both
  at one speed on the route's own points so their legs end together,
  and both crawling apart for the step past 99999.
- A car with a negative VelocityMagnitude is predicted along its body,
  away, so its fabs shows only when the other catches it up.
- For any box MakeOBBs makes, the cosine of a's A0 against b's A1 is
  exactly the negative of a's A1 against b's A0. Only axes no rotation
  makes tell those two reaches apart.
- The sort's `<` and `<=` differ only where -0 meets 0. Two such inputs
  out of 256 do it.

`docs/formats/ai-collision-predict.md` has the detail. The CIA builds.

### Step 11b-4b: MakeNewChoice

DrivingChoice is whole. 11b-4b adds the four functions that choose
(`drivingchoice.c`):
- IsDriveable (0x00241ff8): builds the target for a choice, scores it
  and asks WhoWillThisDriveTargetHit (its caller at 0x00242100). A
  choice is driveable when it built, scored above -1 and hits later than
  the longest time. With the longest time 99999 nothing is;
- TryChoice (0x002428d0): tries one choice, the preferred one scoring
  1.2 times, so a driveable preferred score can fall below -1;
- MakeNewChoice (0x00242170): the current choice first, then the lines,
  then each side of each car worth caring about, then the way round the
  car in the way when nothing fits;
- TryToDriveAroundCar (0x00242c20): the current choice, the line and
  the two sides, the target saved and restored between them.
EstimateScore's distances are static now, retail's 80-byte carry across
calls (`drivetarget.c`).

The first full run crashed the harness on s_jam. Bisecting the ops found
a `V 3`, and an unbuffered debug build put it just after `rp c1`.
IsEnoughRoom reads a car's route point with no NULL test when the car is
off the road (oob < -0.25), and s_jam's cars had none. They do now, and
nothing else changed.

The first mutation pass left 19 alive:
- 8 are equivalent, argued in the checker and the doc:
  - tc-hittime-init: IsDriveable stores the no-hit time again first;
  - mn-line-way: the car in the way is read only after the side test;
  - tc-scored: |score + 1| is a multiple of 2^-24, and 0.001f is not
    one;
  - ta-saved and the four restores: BuildDriveTarget copies the
    driver's own target over all 528 bytes before anything reads them.
- s_jam caught four once its cars had route points: id-ok-lt,
  mn-round, mn-round-target and mn-line-pref.
- mn-rle needed an exact tie: the current choice hitting at 0.1f with
  the way round hitting at once. s_tie is that case, built by hand. It
  is the 59th s_jam from seed 11 with every longest time 99999, cut
  after its third MakeNewChoice. Car 2's speed is bisected over its
  floats to 0x40cab904, which makes the current choice's hit exactly
  0.1f.
- mn-opp-side, mn-opp-extra and mn-opp-pref needed an oncoming car
  whose sides both fail and whose wider way round then wins. 24
  s_choose scenarios never made one, so there are a hundred now.
- mn-tried-or needed a car whose left side scored and right did not.
  s_pass makes that: oncoming cars at 15 to 50 m/s, one swerve fitting
  its corners and the other not.
- ta-pref-left and ta-cur-pref fell to the full script.

### Step 11c: AIPlan and the AIAction base

`aiaction.c` is the part of the racer AI every action shares:
- AIPlan: its constructor, destructor, SetTimeout, TimeToChange and the
  status tests;
- AIAction's constructor and destructor, and new and delete on
  "AIActionSlotPool" (640 bytes, 15 slots);
- UpdateStatus, which asks HasExpired, HasFailed and HasBeenAccomplished
  through the vptr in that order, each true answer overriding the last;
- the three SetDesiredSpeeds, GetHeadingClassification,
  GetCollisionClassification, ClearPointsToDrive and GetName;

  and unload (`gInitAIPlansFn`, `gCloseAIPlansFn`).

CalculateMaxDeceleration (0x001ccf78) is in `nearbycar.c`. The record is
retail's 608 bytes, with the float at 572 the port calls
DesiredSpeedTolerance. `aicarcontroller.h` includes it now in place of
its placeholder.

Things the listing gives away:
- SetTimeout's `c.le.s`: a timeout of -0 can expire, NaN cannot.
- GetHeadingClassification's second time-to-edge test repeats the
  first's three conditions, so a car drifting left is never timed.
- With the steer check, GetHeadingClassification asks the driver's
  GetSteerToPoint twice and drops the first answer.
- GetCollisionClassification holds the contact's x, across the car,
  against the box's y extents, along it.
- SetDesiredSpeedSlowerThanThisCar divides by zero for a car keeping
  pace (0x001c6520). The EE's FLT_MAX makes the time FLT_MAX or 0.1, so
  the divide is ee_div. It is the only site the model sees take the
  EE's path.

The host build caught one thing first. bVector3 has no alignment of its
own in the port, so on the PC PointsToDrive landed at 20. Both pads are
spelt out now (`_pad20`, `_pad596`).

### Step 11d-1: the five small AI actions

`aiactions.c` has the first five of the eleven actions, each with its
constructor, static CalculateScore, the three tests,
CalculatePointsToDrive, GetName and destructor, and its table, which
`main.c` installs:
- JustDrive (score 0) drives the route on its line. At most every three
  seconds it tries line 0 with IsDriveable and takes it when it is
  driveable. AIDriverAvoidCarsImpactTimeThreshold (2.0f, gp-18168) is
  defined here, as JustDrive is the first to read it.
- Draft (200 with a car ahead) drives the route and slows behind a car
  that overlaps it across and is under 6 m on: that car's speed less
  (20 less the gap), when that is under the action's own speed. It only
  ever lowers the speed.
- NudgeCar (300) and Block (400) keep a car and do nothing with it. They
  set PointsToDriveWillExecuteAction and are always accomplished.
- AccidentRecovery (500 for a car with under two wheels down that is not
  sort of parallel to the track) stops on the route, with no throttle or
  brake, and resets the car once, five seconds after it was made.
  SortOfParallelToTrack makes the body's up axis unit in VU0 and dots it
  with GetElevation's normal against 0.707.

Things the listing gives away:
- JustDrive stores the time in a delay slot, so it is stored whenever
  three seconds have gone, even for a car already on line 0.
- NudgeCar's and Block's HasExpired test `seconds <= DeltaTime` with
  `c.le.s`, so a NaN timeout goes on to the other tests. The other three
  use `c.lt.s` the other way round, and a NaN never expires.
- Retail leaves f14 stale for IsDriveable and f13 for every
  BuildDriveTarget. Neither is read, and the port passes 0.

`drivingchoice_check` runs them, not `nearbycar_check`, because the
actions build drive targets on drivingchoice_check's routes. The actions
run one at a time in a slot of their own, through retail's vptrs, over a
DrivingInformation copied from the script's list, location and choice.
The new stubs are the pool, DestoryTargetMarkers, GetElevation (the
script's normal under the car) and PleaseResetMeLater. s_actions puts
five actions in a row on s_choose's world. It steps the clock from the
action's own times, puts the car ahead at Draft's edges and tilts the car
about the 0.707 line.

### Step 11d-2: Pass and AvoidCars

`aiactions.c` has the two big actions that build on DrivingChoice's
choosing, each with its constructor, CalculateScore, the three tests,
CalculatePointsToDrive, GetName and destructor, and its table; `main.c`
installs seven tables now.
- Pass (300) goes round a car ahead of mine in the list that it can
  catch: 0 < y, x < 2y (signed) and CanICatchThisCar, then
  TryToDriveAroundCar over AIActionPassMaxTimeAheadToMakeAttempt (3.0f,
  gp-18164, defined here) and SideOfCarIsOkay. It is done 3 s on with
  the car off the list or 10 m behind the two half lengths, and fails
  when the car leaves the list, or in its first 3 s is ahead and can't
  be caught.
- AvoidCars (400) answers a hit my own target is heading for, under
  the avoid threshold, with MakeNewChoice. Its points are made again
  every 0.3 s outside the grace period. A line choice, when both cars
  are slow, becomes a side of the car to avoid first. When no choice is
  driveable and the car to avoid is close ahead, it slows behind it.
  Its least lifetime is its seconds to impact plus 2.

Things the listing gives away:
- Pass asks CalculateMaxAcceleration and hands the answer to
  CanICatchThisCar, which doesn't read it. HasFailed asks with -1, so
  the image works it out again and drops it.
- AvoidCars asks DoWeCareAboutThisCar twice at the top and drops both
  answers. In the grace period it reads CarToAvoid's player with no
  NULL test.
- AvoidCars' HasBeenAccomplished tests `seconds <= MinLifetime` with
  `c.le.s`, so a NaN lifetime is done at once.
- SetDesiredSpeedSlowerThanThisCar is handed 0.1 twice; it reads the
  first.

The model stubs CalculateMaxAcceleration (0x001cce50); the harness runs
the port's, with a ride info for each car and a two-entry table for car
type 0. GetDriverNumber is a test CarDriver table (DVT) on both sides,
which every car's driver points at. s_pass_avoid makes Pass or
AvoidCars four times on s_actions' world, with the clock either side of
each edge and of the grace period's end.

The check gives 532 scenarios, 194029 ops, 218234 lines, 0 differ.

The first CIA build failed on AvoidCars' call to MakeNewChoice: it

### Step 11d-3a: PullOver and IJustGotHit

`aiactions.c` has the two actions that read the world outside the list,
each with its constructor, CalculateScore, the three tests,
CalculatePointsToDrive, GetName and destructor, and its table. They are
installed with the other seven, nine tables in all.
- PullOver (600) is for traffic. It scores when the chopper is within
  150 m in plan 0, 1, 2 or a bombing run (the plan tested with `sltiu`,
  so a negative one is none). It also scores when an AI cop that isn't
  disabled, or a player, has its car's cop lights on within the car's
  speed times 3.5 s, and no less than 100 m. It is done when that
  stops, and never fails or expires.
- Its points head for the right edge, or for a careful driver (skill
  -2) stay on the line. Every 0.3 s, a car hit sooner than 2 s is gone
  round with MakeNewChoice from its left side. It creeps at 14 m/s while
  there is room to the right edge and brakes otherwise. New620 holds
  that: the constructor sets it when there is over 2 m, it is lost
  under 2 m and back over 4 m, and over 15 m/s it is set and the car
  brakes. A two-car collision, or a speed under 0.5, stops it. Past
  PullOverTimeout (-999, give or take 0.001, is none) it stops on the
  location's line.
- IJustGotHit (400) takes my car's two-car collisions whose other car is
  on the list: one ahead beats one behind, else the smaller y. It is
  done when none is left or its car leaves the list. Every 0.2 s it
  makes a new choice from the information's. It backs off a player's
  car ahead (unless I am traffic) and gets away from one behind. It gets
  away from any other car that is not ahead. As traffic hit head on it
  holds its speed with the throttle and brake off. Otherwise it slows
  behind, never under 20 off the line's speed. Heading out of the route
  forwards, it brakes.

Things the listing gives away:
- The cop lights are read as a word: CopLights and the three bytes
  after it. The range is worked out before the lights are asked.
- Neither a cop's car nor a player's car is tested for NULL; the cops
  are. IJustGotHit reads CarIHit through once its entry is found.
- The list has an entry for no car, found for NULL. A collision whose
  other car is NULL can be taken, and any later one beats it.
- Past the timeout PullOver's choice is its stack until
  SetChoiceLocation, which leaves it alone for a negative odd line. The
  port clears it, and the model clears sp+0 of the 720-byte frame on
  the way in (PO_CHOICE), as it does MakeNewChoice's.
- PullOver hands MakeNewChoice a side used of 1, and never reads it.
  SetDesiredSpeedSlowerThanThisCar is handed 0.2 second, unread.

The checker stubs GetCollision, IsTwoCarCollision and GetCollidingCars

### Step 11d-3b: GetUnstuck and AvoidRoadBlock

`aiactions.c` has the last two actions, each with its constructor,
CalculateScore, the three tests, CalculatePointsToDrive, GetName and
destructor, and its table. All eleven of AIActionType are installed.
- GetUnstuck (500) needs the grace period over, a location and 3 wheels
  down. It scores when my car is 20 m or more past an edge, or heads out
  of the route forwards as an AI car at 25 m/s or less (traffic at 20).
  It also scores when AreWeStuckBehindSomeone finds a slow car in my way
  within 9 m, or when something hit in front at least 0.4 s ago and I am
  all but stopped. It calls the controller's FindWhereIAm before it
  answers 500.
- Its points are one goal point, three route points on from the
  location's on its line, then the fill-up. It backs at -15 m/s as AI
  and -6 otherwise. It is done when my body faces the goal (a dot of
  0.98, both normalised in bNormalize2's order) and no one is in the
  way. It fails heading out of the route backwards, or backed into
  something at least 0.4 s ago and all but stopped. A minimum lifetime
  (-1, give or take 0.001, is none) holds both tests off. Each way out
  asks FindWhereIAm and the driver's ClearSteeringMemory.
- AvoidRoadBlock (600) takes the first active roadblock with a cop
  that is ahead by more than my speed times 2.5 s, and no less than 100
  m, by CompareDistances. It is done 15 m past it, or when both cops are
  gone, and never fails or expires.
- Its points move smoothly from my offset to the escape lane's. On the
  roadblock's route they end at its route point. Off it, they end at the
  closest point ahead of the escape lane on my route, when the lane is
  under 5 m past the edge there; otherwise at my route's last point,
  keeping my offset. A racer (not a cop, not traffic) the points hit
  within 1 s, ahead, is followed 0.1 slower, at no less than 30 m/s.

- AreWeStuckBehindSomeone tests my speed against |-15|, the constant's

  put in my car's frame. Nothing reads that.
- SetDesiredSpeedSlowerThanThisCar is handed 0.1 twice; the second is
  unread.

- gu-ctor-on-le and gu-sc-coll-eps-le: no lifetime or speed lands
  exactly 0.00100000005f from -1 or 1 (Sterbenz);

- gu-sc-coll-eps-abs: without the fabsf it differs only under 0.999,
  where the speed is under 1 already;
- gu-cp-goal-check: the target was just cleared, so the check has
  nothing to test against;
- rb-cp-slower-b: the unread second float.

Three of the earlier slices' patterns (dr-across-hl, dr-the-car,

### Step 11e-0: Average at retail's size

AICarController keeps two Averages (at 580 and 692), and the port's was
still the demo's, so it came first.

  bytes at 0, 1 and 2, then the total, the mean and the buffer at 4, 8
  and 12. The demo's was 24, with words. PidError shrank with it, from

- player_check: on the host sizeof(Average) is 24 now, which made its

### Step 11e-1: AICarController's record, route methods and action

`aicarcontroller.{c,h}` are new. They have:

  pDeltaLineSpeed and vPreviousLinePoint sit at 692 and 704;
- the constructor and destructor;
- the 17-entry table at retail's 0x002b4d90, with Think (11e-5) and
  DoSnapshot NULL, and GetRouteNumbersToUse pure;
- the route methods: SetCurrentRoute, GetCurrentRoute and
  GetCurrentRoutePoint, GetAmountOutOfBounds, FindWhereIAm,
  FindClosestTrackRoute and GetNewDrivingLine;
- JustReset, ClearStickyDecisions, SteerStraightAhead and
  GetMyDriverNumber;
- InterruptAction, GeneratePointsToFulfillAction, GetCurrentActionType
  and ForceMyCurrentAction;
- SetToPhysicsMode, GetCurrentDrivingLineSpeed (main.c points car.h's
  seam at it), the boosts and the accessors.

Things retail changed, ported with it:
- Car::GetRoute and Car::GetRoutePoint pass a find flag to the
  controller, 1 from every caller but IsFacingWrongWay. The
  AICarController's getters run FindWhereIAm first when the flag is set
  and the location is clear. `car_get_route` and `car_get_route_point`
  take the flag, and so do every controller's getters and the harnesses'
  fakes.
- CarController::SetToPhysicsMode (0x001c0100) sends a player's car to
  physics, where the demo's sent every car to mellow.
  `carcontroller_physics_or_mellow` has it, and Car::SetToPhysicsMode
  inlines the same for a car with no controller. carmode_check's
  mutations follow it.
- cardriver.h names SetSteerToPoint (72) and ZeroSteeringMemory (120).

The checker is its own, `aicarcontroller_check`, over
drivingchoice_check's world. The harness's world moved into
`tools/src/drivingchoice_world.inc`, which both harnesses include. The
harness copies the port's installed table into its test table, as the
model copies retail's, and replaces only GetRouteNumbersToUse and
ChooseNewAction.
- 156 scenarios, 24485 ops, 15468 lines, 0 differ.
- 126 mutations: 121 caught, 5 equivalent.
  - sr-relax, gl-relax and gl-relax0: GetNewDrivingLine's relaxed switch
    never reaches a target IsDriveable reads. BuildDriveTarget builds a
    valid line choice from a copy with no switch, and throws an invalid
    one's target away. s_relax drives the case: cars off the line past

  - gl-list: nothing in 11e-1 moves CurrentNearbyCarList off the

  - gp-ahead: GetCarAhead only reads, and retail drops its answer.

Found along the way:
- IsDriveable reaches WillIHitThisCar, which needs every car's
  collision box. The harness segfaulted on a NULL one until every car of
  the route world was boxed.
- A location with a route and no point is never made by the game.
  IsClear tests only the route, so the getters read the NULL point. The
  script stopped making one.
- The walk world never filled route slot 0, the first one

### Step 11e-2: AICarController's signposts and sticky decisions

`aicarcontroller.c` gains FindSignpostIndex (0x00191d40), GetStickyIndex
(0x00191d90), DoStickyDecisions (0x00191b30), SignPostDecision
(0x00191de0) and GetCurrentTrackRoutePoint (0x001921f8). main.c points
drivingchoice.h's `gAISignPostDecisionFn` at the port's SignPostDecision,
so DrivingChoice::AdvancePoint asks it.
- A decision is a sticky word: bit 0 the slot in use, bit 1 the sign
  taken, bits 2-7 the line, bits 8-15 the sign's index. DoStickyDecisions
  drops one more than 10 m past its sign (and TakenSignpostIndex with it),
  then, while a slot is free, decides the signs from nSignpostIndex on
  within AIDriverSecondsToLookAhead x speed x 1.1 (gp-29840), clamped to
  100-250 m.
- SignPostDecision: a Backwards sign, or a Cloaked one but AlwaysTake,
  keeps the line with no decision; a decided sign answers from its slot.
  AlwaysTake is taken. Any other waits out the sign grace period:
  GetTrackInfo(TrackNumber)'s SignpostGracePeriod, -1 for
  Race::GracePeriodIsActive, else seconds on the race clock (x 0.00025).
  Then Equivalent on World::Random < 0.5, DontTake never, the rest by a
  draw against the skill's TakeSignChance (skill read signed and clamped
  to 0..9; the switch at 0x002b4cb0: the first chance takes Slower, the
  second Faster, the third none, over all Faster). A taken sign needs a
  driveable line from GetNewDrivingLine (relaxed), else it isn't taken;
  AIHint 2 sets TakenSignpostIndex. A line outside 0..1 becomes the kept
  one. The store goes in the first free slot, and with none free, over
  nSignpostIndex (retail's `652 + 4 x -1`), which the port does too.
- GetCurrentTrackRoutePoint: FindWhereIAm with the location clear or the
  car further off its point's road than MyHalfSizeL; else the location
  moves to FindClosestPointAhead's point (the last at the end), and the
  signs between are decided until one is taken, which puts the location
  on its route (relaxed), sets LastTrackRouteNumber, and for AIHint 1
  TakenSignpostTimer to 10000 ticks (2.5 s). At the end with no sign
  taken, FindWhereIAm. Its car argument isn't read.

The checker stands in World::Random (the script's queue, then 0) and
GetTrackInfo (a TrackInfo of the script's), and adds s_signdec (60),
s_sticky (50), s_trackpoint (30), s_trackpoint_edge (30), s_signindex
(20), s_takechance (20) and s_sticky's edge (12), from their own seed.
- 378 scenarios, 67592 ops, 40802 lines, 0 differ.
- 226 mutations: 217 caught, 9 equivalent. 11e-2's are 100: 96 caught
  (sp-ret by crashing the harness) and 4 equivalent.
  - dsd-clamp and dsd-max-args: the clamp's orders differ only for a
    NaN, which the EE doesn't have.
  - sp-relaxed and sp-again-relaxed: as gl-relax, the relaxed switch
    never reaches a target IsDriveable reads.
- The first pass left 13 alive and the full one dsd-max; the script
  gained draws at each chance, the grace clock's first tick past (4001
  for 1 s), seconds of 1 and 3 at the clamps, s_takechance, and the
  edge family with a sign just inside 250 m.

Found along the way:
- mipsemu's EE FPU has no NaN: a NaN speed's look-ahead is 250 there,
  a NaN under IEEE. It isn't scripted.
- DoStickyDecisions goes round the signs for ever with no sign past the
  look-ahead and a slot free; every scenario has a sign 1000 m on.
- track.h and topology.md said the grace period gates "a 0x400
  signpost"; it gates every sign but AlwaysTake. trackroute.h and
  track-route.md said only AIHint 2 is tested; 1 is too.
- ct-tsi, oob-cross and gc-cross carry a line of context, as the new
  code repeats their lines.

Every other checker still runs clean. `docs/formats/ai-car-controller.md`
has the detail, under "The signposts". The CIA builds.

### Step 11e-3: AICarController's belt, glue and boost

`aicarcontroller.c` gains eleven functions:
- the belt's WeHaveTheBelt (0x00190af8), WeNeedTheBelt (0x00190b10) and
  WeCanHaveTheBelt (0x00190b20);
- the glue's WeHaveTheGlue (0x00190c78), WeNeedTheGlue (0x00190c88),
  WeCanHaveTheGlue (0x00190c90), GlueOn (0x00190f38), GlueOff
  (0x00190fb8) and GetGlueSpeed (0x00190ff8);
- the boost's DecideBoostFactor (0x001928f0) and
  CalculateDistanceAndPositionBoost (0x00192c78).

They come with the unit's globals: bBeltMover (gp-20344, 1), the glue's
two-point Graph (gp-20336, (-20, 0.1) to (20, -0.1)), the catchup's off
switch (gp-20132) and nLastGlueReason (gp-20296).

- **WeCanHaveTheBelt.** It answers no for any of these: under 3 drive
  target points; AIDemoMode; OffBeltTimer or RealPhysicsTimer running;
  under 5 m/s forward or no wheel down; no action, or PullOver,
  GetUnstuck, AccidentRecovery, AvoidRoadBlock or IJustGotHit; a careful
  driver; a player within 120 m; under 30 s raced.
- **WeCanHaveTheGlue.** Reasons 1 to 10 go into nLastGlueReason (4 is
  unused).
  - It refuses with no action, an action type of PullOver or later
    (signed), or a speed ratio under 0.94.
  - It holds within 60 m, 10 m/s and a heading dot of 0.5 while
    GlueOnTimer runs. When that runs out, GlueOffTimer is set to 20 s.
  - It takes within 30 m, 6 m/s and 0.7, with GlueOffTimer out and the
    player not ahead.
  - Each velocity is normalised by the VU0's `vrsqrt`, so a standing car's
    direction is 0.
- **GlueOn and GlueOff.** GlueOn counts nGlueCount up and sets 7 s and a
  bias of 0.2. GlueOff counts it down.
- **GetGlueSpeed.** Without both RacingCars it answers the driver's
  GetDesiredSpeed. Otherwise it is the glued car's speed times
  `(graph(gap - bias x speed) + 1) + dv x -0.05 / (gap^2 x 0.01 + 1)`,
  clamped to 0.9-1.1. The gap is negative with the glued car ahead.
- **CalculateDistanceAndPositionBoost.** The laps between the cars are
  folded to within half a lap in a cop race. Times the track length that
  gives `ahead`, and nothing comes of it past MaxDistanceForBoost.
  - The two distance Graphs, between skill 0 and 9, give `dist`, plus a
    speed term clamped to 0.05.
  - The position boost's index is `diff + 7`, or `diff + 8` when the
    player is behind.
- **DecideBoostFactor.** Nothing changes for a car with no RacingCar,
  with no boost allowed, or with a player.
  - It runs every BoostCalculationFrequency seconds.
  - With the catchup on, outside AIDemoMode and with player cars, an
    action that doesn't allow the boost sets 1.
  - After 30 s, the factor is `(dist + 1) + pos x BoostScale`, against
    the one player or the two-player target. That target is the leader,
    or the trailer for an AI car placed past NumAICars / 2, plus one for
    each player within it.
  - It is then scaled by the player's speed ratio through the
    PositionRatio table, no less than the skill's SlowFactor, when
    Player::CatchupAllowed(SlowFactor) passes.

`player.h` gains `player_get_speed_ratio` and `player_catchup_allowed`
(0x001811e8 and 0x001811f8). Retail's CatchupAllowed compares its
argument with fMaxSpeedRatio, not the mean, as the first try had it.

Only Think's two belt calls and ExecuteCurrentAction's DecideBoostFactor
have callers in retail. WeHaveTheBelt and the glue's WeNeed, WeCanHave,
GlueOn, GlueOff and GetGlueSpeed are reached by no `jal` and no data
word, so the glue never runs in the game.

The checker:
- **The stand-in.** It stands in the driver table's GetDesiredSpeed.
- **The memory.** The script fills the rest: players, speed-ratio
  Averages, RacingCars, the coordinator's state, the race parameters'

- **The glue Graph.** The model builds it with the image's own start-up

- **The divides.** drivingchoice_check's Model keeps its allowed divides

- **The scenarios.** s_belt (40), s_glue (60), s_boost (60) and s_boost's
  catchup (30) come from their own seed.
  - Each round of the first three fails at most one test, chosen at
    random (`gate_picker`).
  - The glue's headings hit their edges exactly through unit vectors

  - The catchup draws every NumAICars and place, so the two-player split

- 568 scenarios, 95996 ops, 75041 lines, 0 differ.
- 407 mutations: 394 caught, 13 equivalent. 11e-3's are 181: 177 caught
  (5 by crashing the harness) and 4 equivalent.
  - wcb-race-le and dbf-early-le: no whole tick count is 30 s exactly

  - dbf-ratio-allowed: a catchup player is only ever set past the

  - dbf-ratio-over: at a ratio of exactly 1 the row is multiplied by 0.
- The first pass left 16 alive, which led to the changes above:

### Step 11e-4: AICarController's horn and ExecuteCurrentAction

`aicarcontroller.c` gains MaybeHonkAndOrBlinkHeadlights (0x00192fa8) and
ExecuteCurrentAction (0x001932e8). `car.c`'s HonkAndOrBlinkHeadlights and
UpdateHeadlightsAndHorn move to retail's (0x00134130, 0x00134198).

- **MaybeHonkAndOrBlinkHeadlights(car, list).**
  - It returns for a cop's or a traffic car's `car` (UsageType - 1,
    unsigned, under 2), and unless the coordinator is in AIDemoMode or
    `car` is REAL controlled.
  - `car`'s entry comes from my own list. An AI car goes on only when
    DoWeCareAboutThisCar(entry, list) passes (0 for NULL), a traffic car
    always, any other control never.
  - The draws: `on = (R(0.4) + 0.3) - 0.2`, `off = (R(0.2) + 0.15) -
    0.1`, `second` as `on`, `two = R(1) < 0.5`.
  - The chance: over 50 m/s closing, 1, with `two` set and `second` 0.6
    longer; a traffic driver closing under -3, 1; a car with a player,
    0.75; else 0.075 under 6 cars in `list`, or 0.05.
  - `honk = R(1) < chance`, and only then `blink = R(1) < 0.9` (over
    50 m/s) or `0.5`. My car's HonkAndOrBlinkHeadlights takes them.
- **The car's honk and lights.** Retail takes the second on phase's
  duration as a third float and keeps it at Car+2088 (the port's 2176).
  The guard's cycle is `(On + Off) + SecondOn`, with the old durations.
  UpdateHeadlightsAndHorn's gap ends On after the first phase, not Off
  (0x001341ec compares with f3, still On), and the second phase is lit
  while the time past the first, less Off, is under SecondOn. car_check's

  the old SecondOn runs over 0, 0.75 and the constructor's -1, and
  honk-cycle-demo, honk-second-is-on, honk-drops-second, lights-gap-off,
  lights-second-on and lights-second-from-on are new mutations.
- **ExecuteCurrentAction.**
  - The driver's SetTarget (slot 64) gets the action's PointsToDrive,
    then DecideBoostFactor runs.
  - SetDesiredSpeed (slot 56) gets (speed, time, tolerance, allowed):
    (0, 0, 0, 1) with the location clear; (15, 0, 10, 1) for SuperEasyAI
    (gp-20120, retail's alone); (the location's point's line speed, 0, 0,
    1) for BoringAIForCameraTuningOn (gp-22580); the action's own four
    (564, 568, 572, 580) with UseDrivingLineSpeed clear; else (the line
    speed, 0, 572, 580).
  - The line speed: with a sign taken, its GetNewRoutePoint's byte for
    the line (CompareDistances is asked and dropped); else 99999 while
    TakenSignpostTimer runs; else the byte at the location's point plus

    LastRoutePointLookaheadSwitch: `Random(2v) - v` with `v` the
    skill's RoutePointVariance byte plus 1. A cop race takes 0.75 of the

  - ClearPointsToDrive ends it.

### Step 11e-5: AICarController's Think

`aicarcontroller.c` gains Think (0x00191148), the controller's frame, and
installs it in slot 32. `timer.c` gains Timer::CountDown (0x001a3cf0) and
`race.c` Race::CanAICarsStartDriving (0x00149078), both new in retail.

- **CountDown(dt).** A timer of 0 or 0x7fffffff is left alone. Otherwise
  `(int)(dt * 4000)` ticks come off by a wrapping `subu`, a negative
  result becomes 0, and it answers whether the timer is still running.
- **CanAICarsStartDriving.** RaceStage is RACING (4), or a cop race
  (BeACop, 0x0031ab0c) is at the pre-race (2) or later.
- **Think(dt).**
  - **Before the start:** before the pre-race SetDesiredSpeed(0, 0, 0,
    1); from it on, the brake stand: BrakeStanding (560) drawn by
    `bRandom(2)` when BrakeStandTimer (552) isn't running, flipped once
    the phase's length is under the time since BrakeStandTimerStart
    (556); each phase `bRandom(0.25) + 0.35` s on the brakes or
    `bRandom(1) + 1.5` s off; speed 100 on the brakes, else 0. Then
    SteerStraightAhead, and it returns.
  - **The progress check:** an action that isn't a PullOver, when
    ProgressTimer (576) runs out on this step: 1.5 s again, the ten-slot
    pProgress records TrackLength x |dCurrentLapNumberExact|, and
    PleaseResetMeLater when the car isn't blinking, the ring is full, its
    mean is under 0.2 and no player is within 50 m.
  - **The timers:** RealPhysicsTimer, run out, gets 1 s more under 4
    wheels down, else the default mode; OffBeltTimer, running, takes a
    car off the belt and counts down; GlueOn, GlueOff and TakenSignpost
    count down.
  - **The debug reset** for the camera's car with ResetThisCarsPosition
    (gp-20320): cleared, and DebugSetPosition at (-890, -332, -78), speed
    0, angle gp-13390's halfword (the 0xc000 the start-up code stores).
  - **The turn:** SecondsBeforeNextActionEvaluation comes down by dt and
    the list is cleared. An AI racer thinks when `WorldLoopCounter % 8` is
    under CopCarPos - AICarPos and the CarTable's slot there is its car, a
    traffic car the same by 6 from TrafficCarPos, anyone else when its
    seconds are 0 or less. Not its turn, with an action: between thinks
    (a choice beside a player's car is steered round it again when it's
    still in the list), and it returns.
  - **The think:** 0.1 s more, DoStickyDecisions, BuildArray,
    GetCurrentTrackRoutePoint; a clear location stands and steers
    straight. Else the action: BoringAIForCameraTuningOn's JustDrive; a
    new JustDrive (AIActionJustDriveScore, -1) by bOMalloc for none;
    else UpdateStatus, a done one deleted for ChooseNewAction's next, or
    InterruptAction's answer. Then GeneratePointsToFulfillAction,

  `gBeltMoverSetBeltFn`, NULL until the BeltMover is ported; Think aborts

### Step 11e-6: the BeltMover

`beltmover.{c,h}` are retail's BeltMover.obj (0x00204098 to 0x002056b4),
all but DoSnapshot. It is the cheap mover AICarController::Think puts an
AI car on when no player is near.

- **The belt.** SetBelt resamples the driver's DriveTarget and makes its
  points a QuickSpline's (EXTRAPOLATED, 20 points, w 0). FindCoordinates
  finds the car's parameter `v` on it, its rate `dv` (the speed in
  control points a second) and `ddv`, towards 0.899 of the desired speed
  over the desired time, clamped to the car's most acceleration and to
  -20 m/s/s. The car's parameter is `v + t(dv + t ddv)` on the belt's
  clock.
- **Move** puts the car on the curve each frame:
  - the heading, eased towards the tangent 0.5 s on by a tCubic2D;
  - the slide out of a bend, from an Average of the sideways
    acceleration 0.3 s on through SlideCoef's two Graphs, by a second
    tCubic2D;
  - the offset across the belt, by a tCubic1D the slide steers.

  It then writes the position, yaw rate, velocity and speeds outright,
  places the four Wheels and their slips, makes skids near a player, and
  sets the controller's OffBeltTimer (0.6 s) when AverageAir says the
  belt drops away.
- **banim.c** gains GetddVal (0x001da830) and the tCubic2D's inline
  SetVal, SetdVal, SetValDesired, GetVal, GetdVal and Seek
  (`bspline2d_*`). cPoint::SplineSeek's two clamps never run: every seek
  the mover makes passes 0 for both.
- **Wired in.** main.c sets `gBeltMoverCtorFn`, `gBeltMoverSetBeltFn` and
  `gBeltMoverGravityFn` and installs the table. BELTMOVER_SIZE is
  `sizeof(BeltMover)`. No AI car is made in the game yet (AIDriver is
  11f-2), so nothing reaches it.

The checker, `tools/beltmover_check.py`, is new:
- **What runs as shipped.** Every method but DoSnapshot, through the
  table where retail calls them so, with QuickSpline, Average, Graph,
  the tCubics, bSin, bCos, bATan, bNormalize and the Graphs' start-up
  code beneath.
- **The stand-ins.** bOMalloc and the Wheel's constructor, SetState,
  MaybeMakeSkids and destructor; DriveTarget::Resample;
  CalculateMaxAcceleration; PutFlatOnTrack (a scripted lift);
  CalculateGeometryPosition; ShouldVisualEffectsBeGenerated; the
  closest player's distance; ComputeFakeRPM; ~CarMover; and the driver's
  GetDesiredSpeed and GetDesiredTimeToSpeed.
- **The scenarios.** Construction, straight, hill, bend, crest,
  hairpin and random belts, every way to `ddv` and its tie with the most
  acceleration, SlideCoef's knees, the EE's divides (no length, a
  standing car, a Move at scale 0), the w lanes, `dt` round 0.0001, the
  wheels' numbers, the skids at 200 m and the destructor with each
  pointer cleared.
- 6049 ops, 34239 lines, 0 differ.
- 277 mutations: 271 caught (8 by crashing the harness), 6 equivalent:
  cross-z (each cross product is against (0, 0, 1), so z is a zero
  either way), del-vptr (nothing derives from BeltMover), sb-dirty
  (SetNumControlPoints has set the flag), air-h-le (h is exactly 0 only
  for a dt of 0), mv-s-w (only the sum's x and y are read) and mv-steer
  (cvt.w.s and a halfword store give the same bits for 65535.0 and
  -1.0). The first pass left 30; the rest became scenarios.

Found on the way:
- A belt of one point has no length, so its scale is the EE's FLT_MAX.
  A Move then overflows, which the EE clamps and the host does not, so
  the one-point scenario is given a length. The scale's own divide is
  checked at FindCoordinates, with the car standing.
- AverageAir's step rounds alike either way for Move's 0.5 s, a power of
  two, so the checker also asks it over 0.7 s.
