### Step 11f-1: PsychoDriver

`psychodriver.{c,h}` are retail's PsychoDriver.obj (0x00139700 to
0x0013a6ac and 0x0013ab68 to 0x0013ad84), all but DoSnapshot, with
AIDrivingInfo.obj's SteerStraightVector3D and SteerStraightVelocity3D.
It is the AI's CarDriver: AIDriver's constructor (11f-2) and
TrafficDriver's each build one on their car.

- **The record**, 624 bytes: CarDriver's 560, the car, the steer-to
  point, MaxThrottle (never read), the desired speed with its time and
  tolerance, AllowedToUseThrottleAndBrake, the e-brake timer, the
  direction latch and three PidErrors, "Phsycho" Body, Heading and
  Velocity (40 bytes each: Averages of 15/5, 15/5 and 6/3).
- **The tuning.** The start-up code (sinit.c's [16], 0x0013ab68) builds
  seven Tables over the speed and sets fPsychoCounterDiff. Indices 3
  and 4 of GetMovementIndex (traffic, delivery, and mellow under
  traffic control) take their weights from four arrays instead.
- **Drive** steers on a PID of the heading's error, or the body's when
  the two disagree in sign or the heading's is much the larger or the
  car is under 5 m/s. It clears the steering's memory through the table
  when the car touches another, turns the wheel at the speed table's
  rate (twice that back towards the middle), and picks the gear and the
  pedals by a latch on the speed's sign: a car rolling the wrong way
  faster than 7 m/s brakes until under 2. CalcThrottleAndBrake (new in
  retail) coasts within the tolerance and otherwise nudges the pedals
  by a clamped PID on the speed.
- **Not reached.** 0x0013a630 (a `sw zero,0(a2)`), SetMaxThrottle,
  StepOnItJeeves, ClearThrottleMemory and SetEBrakeTimer have no
  caller, so the e-brake never comes on in the game.
- **Wired in.** main.c installs the table. The horn's three seams stay
  NULL until BaseCarSound is ported (a NULL one is the no-sound answer).

The checker, `tools/psychodriver_check.py`, is new:
- **What runs as shipped.** Every method but DoSnapshot, the destructor
  and Drive through the table, with ~CarDriver, ~DriveTarget, Average,
  PidError, Table, bATan, bSinCos, bNormalize and the start-up code
  beneath.
- **The stand-ins.** bMalloc and the frees, DriveTarget's constructor,
  Clear, operator=, Resample and InterpolatePoint, the two collision
  calls, GetYawAlways and the horn's three.
- **The scenarios.** Every table's grid, RadianWrap's edges, each
  constructor and destructor flag, GetError about 1 m/s, every movement
  mode pair, and drives over the wheels down, collisions, every latch
  edge, the time about 0.001, the e-brake about 20 mph, the wheel about
  180 degrees, dt under 0.0001, the swap's tests met exactly, 200 m, a
  fixed index at up to 175 m/s, steering ratios to 40000 (`cvt.w.s`
  saturates) and 150 random drives.
- **Rounding.** The order of the sums in the steer shows only where it
  moves the wheel across a BAM. A search of `rounding_drive`'s seeds
  found steps where it does: three on a fixed index with a steering
  ratio of hundreds, and one in about 15000 on a speed-table index.
- 55673 ops, 49373 lines, 0 differ.
- 247 mutations: 238 caught (3 by crashing the harness), 9 equivalent:
  rw-le (no BAM is 3.14159 radians exactly), rw-dead (the angle is
  unsigned), ni-steer (CarDriver's constructor zeroed it), ni-zs and
  ni-zt (a fresh PidError is what Reset(0) leaves), dd-vt (nothing
  derives), dr-fwd (a desired speed of 0 takes the slow branch first),
  dr-rate-dbl1 and dr-rate-dbl2 (with `des == cur` the step is 0). The
  first pass left 11; a time left of -0 in a step of 0 then caught
  dr-tfloor, first thought equivalent.

`docs/formats/psycho-driver.md` has the detail, and `car-driver.md`

## Session 40 (2026-10-07) -- 11g-1: AI racers that drive

### The config file

`sdmc:/nfshp2_config.txt` is the port's own, in the place of the joylog's
channel 32 that LoadConfigItems reads and only a development kit records.
Each line is a name from configitems.h and its value, `#` a comment;
`SkipFE 1` turns SkipFE on as R held at boot does. `config_items_apply_text`
(configitems.c) parses it and reports each item, and anything it skips,
through a log callback. main.c's `readConfigItems` runs it at boot, before
InitFred. With no file nothing changes. It is a test aid: the user wants
the AI race from the frontend's Hot Pursuit setup (11g-2).

### Why the AI racers did not drive

`SkipFE 1` and `SkipFENumAICars 3` gave a race with three AI racers on
the grid (drivers 100 to 102, types 43, 35 and 13), and nothing aborted.
They never moved. A new log line per AI racer showed each one in
MELLOW_MOVEMENT on JustDrive with RACING reached, and the PsychoDriver
asked for 0 m/s:
ExecuteCurrentAction's speed is the line's speed byte (62 there) times
`AISkillLevel[skill].SpeedFactor` times the BoostFactor, and SpeedFactor
read 0.000.

TheDifficultyInfo was all zeros. GLOBALB.BUN's last top-level chunk is
0x34b00 at 0xb8500, 992 bytes. Retail's LoadGlobalChunks hands every
chunk to LoadChunks, whose slot 25 copies it in. The port's
`loadGlobalCarInfo` walks GLOBALB itself and offers each chunk to the
loaders it needs (texture packs, car info, characters, the track info
table, light list, acid FX), and `loader_difficulty_info` was not one of
them. It is now, and the boot log's "car data" line counts 9 chunks, not 8.
GLOBALB's skills read SpeedFactor 0.91 to 0.98, RoutePointVariance 10 to 4,
Misc (5.0, 0.3, 100000) and TwoPlayerCatchup the four knees
difficultyinfo.h quotes.

After the fix the three racers leave the grid at full throttle for
56.4 m/s (62 x 0.91) and race the route: about 680 m out at 40 s,
switching between JustDrive, AvoidCars and Pass, and the HUD has the
player 4th of 4. The same empty table had other effects:
- every frontend opponent's skill came out 0, as StartRace draws it from
  SkillLevelDistribution's CDF;
- DecideBoostFactor recalculated each frame (BoostCalculationFrequency 0).

GLOBALB's NisInfo chunk (0x37010) is still dropped: its loader (slot 20)
is not ported.

### A false lead

In two runs the player's car drove itself. The log showed the analog
gas, the Cross pressure byte, at 255. joyhid sets that byte only while
the 3DS A is held, and a third run, with no key sent, stood still at the
resting 4 (the scanner's 1, x4 for a stiff pedal). It was keyboard input
reaching Azahar.

### Checks

aicarcontroller (865 scenarios, 0 differ), fred, fredrace, hudfeatures
and hudrender (each builds configitems.c) and difficulty_check (68
facts, 11 readers, 0 wrong) still run clean. The CIA builds.
`docs/formats/difficulty-info.md` has the loading. CONTINUE.md's next
slice is 11g-2, the Hot Pursuit race from the frontend.

### 11h-2: TrafficDriver

`trafficdriver.{c,h}` are retail's TrafficDriver.obj (0x0018c380 to
0x0018d070) but DoSnapshot, with `_vt$13TrafficDriver` at 0x002b4730:
the controller SetControlMode builds for a car under TRAFFIC_CONTROL.
The record is AICarController's 720 and PickLowNumberedRoutes, rounded
to 736, which retail's SetControlMode asks for (the demo's 720 had a
CurrentAction of its own). The table is AICarController's but for the
destructor, DoSnapshot, Think, JustReset and GetRouteNumbersToUse.

- The constructor builds a PsychoDriver (624, pool 16) for the driver.
  It sets ForceCurrentAction to 11, PickLowNumberedRoutes to 1 and no
  action, and staggers the clock by CarIndex x -1/70 s.
- Think runs the clock down, then decides whether this frame is the
  car's turn:
  - a traffic car (driver type 3): the odd frames of WorldLoopCounter's
    twelve (`div`/`mfhi`, so a negative counter's remainder is
    negative) whose half is its place after TrafficCarPos in the
    world's CarTable; the clock is not read;
  - any other driver type: the clock run out (`<= 0`).

  Then it runs the sticky decisions, adds 0.2 s to the clock, builds the
  nearby cars and gets the route point, and stops if the location is
  clear.
- With no action it makes a JustDrive. Otherwise the action's status,
  and then the cascade from its Score (-1 when it is time to change).
  Each step is tried while the best so far is below its global, and
  taken (the old action deleted, flags 3) when it scores above:
  1. GetUnstuck, only more than 2 s (8000 ticks are exactly 2.0) after
     the last, stamped;
  2. AccidentRecovery;
  3. IJustGotHit, with a honk after the delete;
  4. AvoidCars, with AIDriver's quirk (okay as the float seconds,
     unsigned; used as okay; 0), the choice copied, a honk, and off the
     belt (TRAFFIC_MOVEMENT to MELLOW_MOVEMENT);
  5. PullOver, with the -999 traffic timeout, the nearby list and the
     location, and off the belt;
  6. JustDrive.

  Then the choice's driving line (types 1 to 4) through GetDrivingLine,
  SetDrivingLine(0) and HighlightDrivingLine when it changes, and
  ExecuteCurrentAction by `jal`. Retail's PrintAbove call (when
  CameraFollowDefaultCar is 0) is empty and left out.
- JustReset sets PickLowNumberedRoutes from MyDrivingLocation's route
  (`(uint32)(n - 50) < 10`), deletes the action, clears the sticky
  decisions, makes a JustDrive and executes it.
- ExecuteCurrentAction calculates the action's points and shows them for
  the camera's car. It works out the speed, gives the driver the target
  and then the speed, time, tolerance and AllowedToUseThrottleAndBrake,
  and clears the points.
- CalculateDesiredSpeed scans from the location's point for the first
  hairpin sign that is not a backwards one. The scan stops after 75 m,
  19 points or the route's end. A hairpin gives a most of 0.32782 x the
  distance and a tolerance of 2. Within 10 m the sign's route is taken,
  and PickLowNumberedRoutes becomes `RouteNumber < 60` (-1 with no
  route). With three points or more, a bend whose halves' normalized
  dot is under 0.64 gives 10 and 2. The most is then floored at 10. The
  speed is the action's own or, with UseDrivingLineSpeed, the most with
  no time, and is capped at the most. 75 x 0.32782 is the top speed,
  24.5865.
- SetDirection stores the bool. Nothing in retail calls it.

main.c installs the table and sets `gTrafficDriverCtorFn`.
`TRAFFICDRIVER_SIZE` is `sizeof(TrafficDriver)`, and carmode_check's
malloc hook maps it back to the demo's 720 (size-trafficdriver caught).
No traffic car is built yet: the TrafficTeleporter (11h-3) places them.

`tools/trafficdriver_check.py` runs retail's methods in mipsemu. Running
as shipped under them:

- DrivingLocation's IsClear, SetRoute, SetDrivingLine and

- the sign lookups and DrivingChoice::Clear;
- GetMyDriverNumber, IsDrivingLine, PrintAbove and bNormalize.

The AICarController calls, PsychoDriver, the six CalculateScores and
the six action constructors are stood in for on both sides, and print.
The scenarios:

- the turns over counters -30 to 30 and the extremes, in eighteen world

- each gate a point either side, each global moved, and the order;
- the 8000-tick edge, AvoidCars' okay through the unsigned conversion,

- the hairpin scan at its 10 m, 75 m, 19-point and route-end edges, with

- the bend's cosine in 241 steps and at exactly 0.64 (out = (16,

- JustReset over the route numbers;
- 400 random rounds.

## Session 42 (2026-10-07) -- 11g-2b, Race::Update

### What it fixes

Session 41's race from the frontend stayed at COUNTDOWN for good:
World::DoTimestep's call to Race::Update (0x00148a78, from 0x0014e20c)
went through `gRaceUpdateFn`, which was NULL. Update is what sets
RACING once GetCountdownNumberToDisplay reaches 4 (GO), and it also runs
the race time, the laps, the finishes and the leadership. The SkipFE
race starts at RACING, so it had never had any of those.

### The port

- `raceupdate.{c,h}` are retail's Race::Update, both FinishCars (by
  index, 0x001485f0, and by car, 0x00149250), GetLeadingUnfinishedCar,
  GetFinisher, GetNextFinishRank, MonitorLeadership, MaybeSaveGhostCarData
  and UpdateGhostCar, with the race time projection that is new in
  retail (0x001473f8, no name; the demo's FinishCar has none of it).
- `playerfinish.{c,h}` are Player::SetFinishedRacing (0x00176650; the
  demo's 0x001700d0 has no near-car count).
- racesplit.c adds RacingCar::GetLastFinishLineCrossingTime (0x00147558),
  and aicarcontroller.h the pull-over at 0x001908d8 (PULL_OVER forced,
  the timeout `min.s`'d with AIActionPullOverCrossFinishLineTimeout,
  15.0).
- main.c sets `gRaceUpdateFn` and `gRaceFinishCarFn` (SimulateRaceFinish's).
- What Update does, in order: the countdown's end; the race time
  (`Timer::Round`ed); UpdateGhostCar; each unfinished car's lap counts
  and a player's best lap (signed); the forced finish (the player cop's
  win or loss through the cop manager); SortRacingCarsByLeadership and
  MonitorLeadership; the lap knockout; the time trial; the laps led (a
  halfword that wraps); the finish at NumLapsInRace; LapFinishedSpeech.
  Each loop re-reads the count and the car, so a car finished in one
  loop is finished for the next.
- FinishCar: the cop's times, the place (the next rank and the finish
  line's time, or a projected time for a car short of the laps), the
  reason, the exact lap, the count, RecordResults; for a player's car
  SetFinishedRacing and SetControlMode(AI_CONTROL); every AI-controlled
  car then pulls over; BlinkBlinkPoof on a blink.
- The image reads past the five boundary arrays for a boundary out of
  [0, 4], and indexes `pRacingCars[prev - 1]` unchecked in
  MonitorLeadership. The port reads 0 and skips; neither happens in a
  sorted field. RegisterInterestingEvent is called on a NULL
  `pReplayManager` unchecked; the port tests it, as carfinish.c does.
- The speech, ClearEventQueue, TriggerFinishLineSound, the ghost
  samples and bWriteToFile are NULL seams until speech (task 26), the
  sound and the ghosts come; NULL does nothing. Retail's SetupGhostCars
  is empty, so no ghost is ever made.

### The checker

`tools/raceupdate_check.py` runs the 12 functions as shipped, with
GetCountdownNumberToDisplay, AreAllPlayersFinishedRacing, the
accessors, the pull-over, Timer::SetTime, Round and bSin under them;
UpdateLapCounts, SortRacingCarsByLeadership, SetRaceStage,
SetControlMode, BlinkBlinkPoof, the replay and results calls, the
speech and sound, the ghost data and the file write are stood in on
both sides. 997307 ops, 73230 lines, 0 differ. The mutation pass: 161
mutations, all caught, 7 by a crash, none equivalent. Four needed a
scenario of their own after the first pass (a saturated best time over
laps 0, Round's half for two truncations, a car taken out of 30 m by z
alone). `docs/formats/race-update.md` has the detail; race.md,
race-coordinator.md, world.md, player.md, quick-race.md,
ai-car-controller.md and ai-driver.md link it.

### On Azahar

`tools/run_azahar_quickrace.ps1`: track 31 backwards, 3 AI racers, car

reads lap 1 of 2 and a running time, the player 4th of 4 with the AI

The countdown itself still has no camera mover: that is the countdown

### 11g-2c begun

CameraCoordinator.obj (0x00199a98 to 0x0019c0d0) was read for the
countdown cameras. CountdownCameraCoordinator::Update looks up
`COUNTDOWN_%d` in the camera data and builds a BumperCameraMover on it.
A scan of every retail bundle found no camera named COUNTDOWN_n (the

the frame's UpdateCameraCoordinators) and the doc are 11g-2c-1's rest.

## Session 43 (2026-10-07) -- the menu's tune stops at the loading screen, the race's starts after GO

The user's notes on the frontend's Quick Race: the menu's tune played on
through the loading screen with its EA TRAX box up (their image 1), the
race's music should wait until the 3-2-1 is over, and the countdown
looked wrong (image 2: the view high over the track, the cinema bars,
the bottom screen blank). They also showed the race's new top-screen
assets.

### The menu's tune

The port's `bgf_begin_unloading_frontend` left the screen and cleared
the stack, where retail's BeginGameFlowUnloadingFrontEnd (0x00168830)
calls UnlaunchFrontendMenus (0x0016fa80). That one pops back to "View
Event Tree" (game types 8 and 9) or "New Main Menu" (2 to 7), leaves the
screen, stops the jukebox, sets FrontendLaunchType (2 after a demo race,
else 3), stops the movie and resets the song monitor.
`bgf_unlaunch_frontend_menus` is now retail's, with two new int hooks
(`gameType`, `raceDemo`) and `songMonitorReset`. Retail's
tNewSongMonitor::Reset does nothing (it deletes an animation nothing
makes), so the box would have stayed up for its five seconds; the
port's `bsm_reset` takes it down, a documented change.

`bootflow_check` runs retail's function as shipped (`RetailUnlaunch`)
over game types -1, 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10 with each demo flag, and
with the menus' movie playing: 61 scenarios, 46779 lines, 0 differ. 25
new mutations, all caught (one, the screen change moved after the
no-op PopScreens(0), was equivalent and was replaced by one that moves
it before the pops).

### The race's music

Retail turns the jukebox to the racing list (category 4) in
LoadSoundRegionsInGame (0x001ae798) and starts it from
RACE_IN_PROGRESS's first TICK at RACING with DelayedStart(6.0)
(0x0014af60), once the ReplayManager's Timer at +92 is marked. None of
that ran: no hook set the selection, the replay stand-in had no Timer,
and the stop and delayed-start seams were NULL. main.c now has
`hookLoadSoundRegionsInGame` (the music's part, then the callback at
once), the replay stand-in's beginning of time, and the seams.

### On Azahar

`run_azahar_quickrace.ps1`: the log has `jukebox stop` and `flow
unlaunch 3` at the unload and the loading screen has no box;
`jukebox selection: racing music` as the track loads; `jukebox delayed
start: 6.0 s` at world frame 183, the first at stage 4 (RACING); and
the EA TRAX box for the race's first tune at frame 545, six seconds on.

### The countdown

The cinema bars are retail's: `player_determine_hud_features` gives a
one-player countdown only the bars and the music box. The view is the
port's: with no countdown coordinator, `choose_camera` leaves the
player with no mover through the countdown, and the camera sits at its
default, 1100 m up. That is 11g-2c-1, next.

## Session 46 (2026-10-07) -- 11g-2c-2a, the fly-by camera

The user's photo 2 has retail's Starting Grid over a slow camera that
flies along the track. That camera is the fly-by: RCSTATE_CAMERA_FLYBY
makes a FlyByCameraCoordinator on view 1, and the coordinator flies the
track's fly-by cameras with a TrackFlyCameraMover.

### What is ported

- `trackflycam.c`, TrackFlyCameraMover (412 bytes): its constructor
  (0x00159d08), destructor, Update (0x00159e98), IsFinished (0x0015a2a0),
  GetTarget and GetCarToFollow, and its table (0x002b1a50).
  - It builds four clamped splines (eye, bank, look, and the 32-entry
    FOV table), all with a table size of 16384.
  - Each parameter steps at `speed * dt * 25`, or follows the car's share
    of the area when the record locks it.
  - With no car the field of view is 13020, 71.5 degrees.
- `cameracoord.c` adds FlyByCameraCoordinator (40 bytes): its
  constructor (0x0019abd8), destructor, IsFinished (0x0019ac40), Update
  (0x0019ac50) and its table (0x002b52c8).
  - Update builds the next fly-by when there is none yet, the data are
    marked, the mover is not a track fly, or the mover is finished. Then
    it moves on to the next, wrapping round.
  - IsFinished is true only with no fly-bys loaded. So with a track
    loaded, CAMERA_FLYBY ends only on RC_SKIP, which the Starting Grid
    posts on X (PreRaceStats::HandleEvent).

main.c sets the mover's two seams. The race coordinator's fly-by seams
(`gFlyByCameraCoordinatorCtorFn`, `gFlyByCameraIsFinishedFn`) stay NULL.
With them set and no grid to skip it, the race would sit in the fly-by
for ever. They go in with the grid, 11g-2c-2b.

### What the disc has

Fifteen fly-bys: each track bundle's `PreRace_01`. Every one:

- is type 2;
- has 2 to 23 eye points and 8 look points;
- has eye speeds of 0.0025 to 0.025;
- has a field of view of 71.5 degrees;
- locks nothing to a car.

### The check

- `tools/trackflycam_check.py` runs the mover beside retail's, with the
  splines, the camera and bATan as shipped. It covers the 15 disc
  fly-bys, built records with cars, locks and ISO FOVs, and the edges.
  - The result: 25 scenarios, 14170 ops, 39418 lines, 0 differ.
  - There are 84 mutations, all caught. Five survivors needed a
    scenario of edges: a lock set with no car, a frozen camera under a
    no-car mover, and an eye within 2 of the look.
- `tools/cameracoord_check.py` adds the fly-by coordinator. It runs over
  each disc fly-by, built cameras with 160 random steps, and the edges,
  with a stand-in mover that prints the record it is given.
  - The result: 3970 ops, 9251 lines, 0 differ.
  - There are 209 mutations: 206 caught and 3 equivalent. The
    equivalent ones are the destructor's table store (the base
    overwrites it first), clearing the mover before the new one is
    stored, and re-reading the index (it already equals `idx`).
  - Three countdown mutations had patterns that also matched the
    fly-by's lines. They now anchor on the countdown's own context.

Nothing changes on screen: the coordinator is not made until the grid

## Session 48 (2026-10-07) -- 11g-2d, the pause menu

The user asked for the pause menu before the pre-race camera. START in a
race paused it with no screen and no way out.

### What is ported

- `pausemenu.c` (0x00170560 to 0x001710f4), retail's PAUSE_MAIN:
  - PauseMenu, 56 bytes: the constructor and destructor, EnterPause,
    ExitPause, Activate, DeActivate, AllPlayerJoysticksPluggedIn,
    CheckJoysticks, MaybeRestart, MaybeQuit, MaybeResume and
    MenuCallback;
  - PauseMenuCallback, the screen's callback;
  - ChooseWhoSelectedMenuItem;
  - tHighlightAnimation's new HandleMessage (0x00248ae0), which moves
    and animates the bloom.
- `jukebox.c`: sound::Mute (0x001af850) as `jb_sound_mute`. It pauses
  the music, and with the category's volume at nothing keeps it paused
  either way.
- **The wiring in main.c:**
  - "Pause Menu" (0x605d2bf1) is added to kScreens[];
  - the pause seams: the menu's constructor, destructor, EnterPause and
    ExitPause, GrayMenuItem, SummonPopup, the current screen, the
    translate, the bloom's BAnim, ChangeGameFlow and Mute.
  - SetScreenFilterPort, PortStopForce, the replay's snapshot count and
    the type-changed handlers' restore stay NULL. There is one pad and
    no rumble, and with no replay View Replay stays grayed.

### Three fixes along the way

- **The input order.** The first run paused and unpaused on the same
  START. Retail's GenerateJoyEvents runs after ExecuteQueuedMessages and
  gives the same events to the Flailer and the players. The port read
  the screens' input before the race frame, so the menu was up in time
  to see the START that put it up. The screens' input is now
  `flowInput`, which runs after `raceFrame` in a race and before the
  flow's frame otherwise.
- **Screens not yet ported.** Options, View Objective and View Cop
  Controls change to screens no kScreens row has. The flow took the
  menu down and left nothing. `flowChangeToScreen` now keeps the screen
  up and logs "not ported".
- **The Quit popup over the frontend** (the user's screenshot: QUIT
  RACE over Language Options). The Quit popup is KEEP_VISIBLE, so
  retail leaves it up over the unloading. Retail then unloads INGAMEB
  with the track's common files. The port keeps FRONTB and INGAMEB
  from boot, and POPUP (0x037f3133) is in both. `uirender_find_screen`
  finds FRONTB's first, so the popup stayed drawn over the frontend.
  `flowBeginUnloadingTrackCommon` now hides every screen of both
  bundles, which is what dropping them does in retail.

### Things that look wrong but are retail

- **Quitting a SkipFE race lands on the language screen.**
  frontendLaunchType is 1 from boot, and only UnlaunchFrontendMenus
  writes it. SkipFE never ran that, so the frontend runs its boot
  stages: autoload, language, title. A race from the frontend returns
  to the New Main Menu (game types 2 to 7) or the event tree (8, 9).
- **A different tune in the menu after a quit** (the user noticed).
  The jukebox's first pick (0x001aea40) plays "Fever for the Flava"
  once a boot. Later menu visits carry on down the menu list.
  `jukebox_check` runs this from retail's code.
- **The gap in the menu.** A hidden item keeps its place, so a quick
  race's menu has a space where View Objective and View Cop Controls
  would be.
- **"Player1" and "Speedster" taking turns on the HUD after a restart.**
  That is hudrender's name alternation, every 500 frames.

### The check

- `tools/pausemenu_check.py`: retail's PAUSE_MAIN in RetailEmu, with
  every call it makes stubbed and printing on both sides. 14633 ops,
  28698 lines, 0 differ. 198 mutations, all caught.
- `tools/jukebox_check.py` gains sound::Mute under each enable, both
  categories, three volumes, and `on` at 0, 1 and 2. 1263 ops, 7061
  lines, 0 differ. Of 292 mutations, 287 are caught and 5 are
  equivalent. The new equivalent one is `mute-down`: with the volume
  at nothing, `on ? on : 1` and 1 are both true, and
  cJukeboxPlayer::Pause takes a bool.

### On Azahar

`run_azahar_race.ps1` and `run_azahar_quickrace.ps1` gain `-Presses`,
single key presses after RACING with a shot after each.

- The menu draws over the race and mutes the music.
- Resume unmutes, and the race goes on with no second pause.
- Restart: Cancel brings the menu back; OK restarts the race.
- Quit: UNLOADING_TRACK_SPECIFIC, UNLOADING_TRACK_COMMON,
  LOADING_FRONTEND, IN_FRONTEND, with no popup left over. From a quick
  race it lands on the New Main Menu.
- The memory comes back. The linear heap is 69397 KB free at boot,
  23844 KB in the race, and 68926 KB once the track detaches. The log

## Session 49 (2026-10-07) -- 11g-2c-2c-1, the pre-race coordinator

The pre-race is the close-up of the cars after the Starting Grid (the
user's photo 2). Retail builds it from two pieces:

- PreRaceCameraCoordinator, which picks the cars and the cameras;
- BumperCameraMover, which flies each camera.

This session ported the first. The second is next.

### What is ported

`cameracoord.c` adds PreRaceCameraCoordinator (0x0019ad78 to 0x0019c0d0,
188 bytes, table 0x002b52b0). See "The pre-race" in
`docs/formats/camera-coordinator.md`.

- **The cars.** Racing car 0 first, then the player three times. Be A
  Cop takes racing cars 1 to 3 (mod the count). Two players take player
  1, player 2, player 1, and Be A Cop with two players takes only the two
  players.
- **Update.** It moves on when no camera is active, on a reload, with no
  mover or when the mover is finished. It deletes the mover, finishes
  after n cameras unless `TunePreRaceSequence` is set, steps the car and
  camera indices, starts the driver's pre-race animation, parses the
  camera and builds a BumperCameraMover on the car read before the step.
- `configitems.c` gains `TunePreRaceSequence` (gp-23108), with its row in
  the config file's table.
- main.c sets `gPreRaceCameraCoordinatorCtorFn` and
  `gPreRaceCameraIsFinishedFn`. The mover's two seams and the
  AnimatedDriver's stay NULL, so for now the coordinator ends after four
  frames with nothing drawn. The user saw no camera on Azahar and asked
  why; BumperCameraMover is what draws it.

### The check

`tools/cameracoord_check.py` and `tools/src/cameracoord_test.c` gain a
world of 6 cars, 8 racing cars, 4 drivers, the race and the players.

- **Ops:** 6400, giving 13655 lines, 0 differ.
- **Mutations:** 293.
  - 289 are caught.
  - 4 are equivalent. The new one is the pre-race destructor's table
    store, which the base's overwrites first.

The constructor runs every mix of Be A Cop, 0 to 3 players and 1 to 5
racing cars that picks differently. Update runs 400 random steps, then to
the end, then its edges.

### Task 37

The user asked for Local Wireless (multi-card) play. It is TASKS.md's
task 37: each console loads from its own card and sends only small
packets each frame (positions, rotation, speed, physics vectors, inputs
and events). It comes after the single-player race is whole.

### BumperCameraMover's decode, for the next session

- **Size and table.** 1116 bytes, table 0x002b1bd0, type 5, constructor
  0x00158800. The table holds:
  - dtor 0x00158910;
  - Update 0x00158a68;
  - GetCarToFollow 0x0015fb10 (+112);
  - GetTarget 0x001589a8 (+120): the car's +80, or the camera's target
    with no car.
- **Layout:**

  | Offset | Field |
  |---:|---|
  | 0 | base |
  | 44 | CameraDataItems, 164 bytes |
  | 208 | EyeSpline |
  | 256 | BankSpline |
  | 304 | EyeParam |
  | 308 | LookSpline |
  | 356 | LookParam |
  | 360 | FOVSpline |
  | 408 | CarToFollow |
  | 412 | TopologyCoordinate |

- **Constructor.**
  1. `camera_mover_init(viewID, 5)`, the table, the record copied.
  2. Four type-0 splines with a table of 16384: eye (NumEye, EyeVerts),
     bank (NumEye, BankVerts), look (NumLook, LookVerts), FOV (32,
     FOVTable).
  3. Both params 0, CarToFollow, and the TopologyCoordinate built.
  4. If the camera is updating: CarNotToRender NULL, RenderDash 0, FOV
     13020.
  5. Near and far clips from the record, always.
- **Destructor.** The table back. If the camera is updating, the focal
  distance and the depth of field to 0. Then the TC's dtor(2), the FOV,
  look, bank and eye splines' dtor(2), and the base's.
- **IsFinished** (0x001589c8). The eye is done if EyeSpeed is 0 or
  NumEye-1 <= EyeParam, and the look the same way; it returns eyeDone ?
  lookDone : 0.
- **Update.**
  1. Return if paused.
  2. pct is the car's track percent; area = max(0, (pct-MinArea) /
     (MaxArea-MinArea)).
  3. The eye, then the look: the param is locked to (N-1)*area, or
     param + speed*WTE*25 clamped to N-1.
  4. M is the identity with row 3 = -(car+80); T is the transposed
     BodyMatrix; W = eMulMatrix(M, T).
  5. eye = EyeSpline(EyeParam), plus road noise times 0.877 at (pos.x,
     pos.y), then y-1, then y+2; the w lane is 0.
  6. elev = GetElevation + 0.7, and eye.z is held up to it.
  7. look = LookSpline(LookParam); bank = BankSpline(EyeParam).
  8. up = ComputeBankedUpVector with (u16)trunc(bank.x).
  9. L = LookAt(eye, look, up); R = W x L.
  10. span = clamp01((pct-MinP)/(MaxP-MinP)); fov = FOVSpline(span*31).
  11. With IsFOVIso: dist = max(|eye - car+96|, 1) and bam = (u16)(bATan(
      dist, fov.x*0.25) << 1). Otherwise bam = (u16)trunc(fov.x *
      182.044449). If updating, FOV = bam.
  12. dist = |eye - look|. If updating: TargetDistance = dist, focal =
      max(2, dist), DOF = 7.5.
  13. With RaceStage 4, the wall routine 0x00157c60(m, &R, car).
  14. SetCameraMatrix(cam, &R, RealTimeElapsed).
- **The wall routine** (0x00157c60).
  1. inv = invert(mat); eye = inv's row 3; geo = car+80.
  2. mid = 0.5 eye + 0.5 geo; r = 0.5 |geo-eye| + 0.5.
  3. A local TC, SetInterestBBox(&mid, r).
  4. o = mat x geo; off = (o.x/o.z, o.y/o.z).
  5. camera_wall_offset (drivecam.c has it); eye += its out.
  6. d = eye - geo; dist = |d|.
  7. GetCarSpaceBoundingBox; f = max(max.x, |min.x|) + 0.7. If dist < f,
     eye.z = geo.z + ee_sqrt(f^2 - (d.x^2 + d.y^2)).
  8. camera_look_at_offset(mat, &eye, geo, &off).
  9. The TC's dtor(2).

## Session 52 (2026-10-08) -- two graphics faults, and 11h-3, the TrafficTeleporter

### The car with only its wheels

The user saw their car lose its body mid-race, all but the wheels.

- **The cause.** A car that can be dented and has an InstanceIndex above
  0 draws its body from `%s_A%d` and `%s_B%d` (carrenderinfo.c). The
  player's car always can be dented (fredrace.c), so it gets those names
  whenever an AI drives the same type ahead of it in the list.
  GameFlowLoadingTrackCommonPart2 makes the copies through
  `gEDuplicateSolidFn`, which was NULL, so Body[0] had no solid.
- **The fix (commit d110c44).** `esolid.c` has eDuplicateSolid (retail
  0x00103bf0), eSolid::ChangeName (0x00104030) and
  eDeleteAllDuplicatedSolids (0x00103d58), and `main.c` sets both seams.
  `docs/formats/loader-table.md`, "The copies", has the detail.
- **The check (commit 5b098db).** `loadertable_check` copies the
  Viper's and the bus's solids as a race does and runs retail's code
  beside the port: retail image 37,558 ops, 49,626 lines, 0 differ. Its
  13 new mutations are all caught. The harness had stopped linking when
  cameracoord.c began to read the players (Session 49); it defines them
  now.

### The see-through car

Then the car looked like chrome you could see through. The same look
was a missing skin on 2026-10-05 (commit 0355be5), and it was again.

- **The cause.** `texpack_upload` and `texpack_upload_chain` decoded
  into a `w*h*4` scratch from the main heap. On TRACKB45 with traffic the
  heap was down to about 1.5 MB, in pieces, and six cars' 512x320 skins
  (640 KB of scratch each) failed. A car with no skin draws its
  reflection alone.
- **The fix (commit d110c44).** The scratch comes from the linear heap
  first, which has megabytes spare, and is asked for after the texture,
  so freeing it leaves no hole below the texture. The main heap is the
  fallback.
- **On Azahar.** A forced race on track 45 with eight Vipers (the
  player's is instance 7, `VIPERGTS_A7`): 0 textures missing, every car
  painted, 3,372 KB of main heap free.

### Found on the way

- **TRACKB45 runs at 15-20 FPS on Azahar.** The draw takes 45-50 ms of
  CPU: about 550 models in view (15 ms), and eight cars close to the
  camera at LOD 0 (17 ms), in about 1,194 batches. It is a frame-rate
  problem of its own, for the speed work.
- **The main heap is short on the big tracks:** 1.5 to 3.4 MB free.
  bMalloc aborts when it fails, so big buffers that can live in linear
  memory should move there.

### 11h-3, the TrafficTeleporter (commit cd443d0)

- **What.** `traffictele.c` is retail's TrafficTeleporter.obj
  (0x002226f8 .. 0x002232c0) but DoSnapshot. PlaceNewCar puts each
  traffic car on a random point of routes 50-69 that no player can see
  (250 round the track) and no car is near (100), and keeps 2000 off
  the start line in the race's first 20 s. DoTimestep wakes every 1-16
  s and moves the next car out of sight to 250 or more ahead of a
  random player, with a new skin. `airouteplan.c` is
  GuessTargetDestinations (0x001cbb70), the walk it asks.
  `carrenderinfo.c` gains Car::SwitchSkin and the two it calls.
- **The check.** `traffictele_check`: 7563 ops, 0 differ; 180
  mutations, 178 caught, 2 equivalent (each with its reason in the
  script). `carrenderinfo_check`: 327 scenarios, 108561 lines, 0
  differ; the 12 new mutations are caught (175, 173 caught, 2
  equivalent).
- **On Azahar.** The user saw no traffic in the first runs. It was
  there, all drawn, but 198 m and more from the player. Quick Race's
  density is 0.33, under DoTimestep's 0.4, so no car is ever moved and
  the traffic drives where it was put, none of it near the start line.
  A 150 s run on track 24 with the gas held passed four of the six
  cars at 10 to 42 m
  (cd443d0's message says 8, a misread of the log).

### The mirror without its frame

The user's photos showed the mirror late in a long race with no frame
and the main view through it. The log had RVM and RVM_MASK, and 40-odd
other textures, failing to upload with 6 MB of linear heap left.
`trackview.c`'s load_texture takes the largest mip level that leaves
6 MB free, and a texture that fails is not tried again. On track 13
forwards the mirror was right. Not fixed yet: it is the texture memory
work below. `main.c` logs each missing texture now ("race: texture
... missing").

### B in a race (commit f539fdf)

The user pressed S (Azahar's B, the brake) and the frontend's Hot
Pursuit menu came up over the race. `flowInput` passed B to
`bgf_back_button` with no screen up, and it popped the stack to New
Main Menu. Retail only has the screen list's JoyHandler while a screen
is up (ChangeToScreen, 0x0016c4c0, adds it out of none and removes it
at none). The run script's held A then picked Quick Race, and the
second race's load aborted in bMalloc (CARS\DIABLO\GEOMETRY.LZC, 5
MB free). `flowInput` now passes nothing with no screen. On Azahar two
B presses mid-race brake, and the race goes on.

### The texture memory: the research (the user's ask)

The user asked for every texture to load on every map, done globally.
`texbudget.py` (the session's scratchpad) priced every retail texture
as the port uploads it now (RGBA8, padded to powers of two, the chain
down to 8) and in the smallest exact PICA200 format:

| Set | Now | Lossless | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TEX11-16 | 39.9 MB | 31.4 MB | 79% |
| TEX21-26 | 33.7-34.4 MB | 29-29.9 MB | 86-87% |
| TEX31-36 | 39.1-40.7 MB | 31.3-32.6 MB | 80% |
| TEX41-46 | 38.4 MB | 32.2 MB | 84% |
| TEX61-66 | 41.6-42 MB | 33.2-33.5 MB | 80% |
| CARS/TEXTURES.BIN | 266.3 MB | 198.6 MB | 75% |
| DYNTEX | 17.3 MB | 10.5 MB | 61% |
| GLOBALB | 4.1 MB | 2.6 MB | 63% |

The tracks are mostly RGB8, then RGBA8, LA8 and L8. The 162 car skins
512 wide are all RGB8, with 38% of them padding. PS2 alpha 0x7F is
opaque (254 doubled).

The plan, in CONTINUE's "Next": the format per texture, a cache with a
budget, the spare VRAM, LINEAR_WANT on the device, then the skins'
padding. Pre-decoding offline would not help: memory is the limit, the
decoded texels are 3-8 times the PS2's 4- and 8-bit ones, and the card
holds retail's files only. ETC1 is lossy.

**The memory mode.** The user confirmed the CIA's 178 MB on their New
3DS XL, and the device logs agree: memory type 7, grant 182272 KB,
heap 96 MB, linear 80 MB. There is no larger mode. The split is what
can move: the race uses about 45 MB of the malloc heap, so about 30 MB
can go to the linear heap (LINEAR_WANT). heapcfg.c's step-down finds
what the kernel will give in one block.

## Session 53 (2026-10-08) -- the mid-race hitches, and the AI pack's cost

### The texture formats (commit 3b62e00)

- `texpack.c` stores a mip chain in the smallest of RGBA8, RGB8, LA8 and
  L8 that holds its texels exactly (`texpack_format`, a scan of every
  texel). It also gains `texpack_chain_bytes` and
  `texpack_upload_chain_as`. Lossless, as the user asked.
- `texpack_check --chain --packed` compares the stored chain against
  the Python decoder: TEX12LOCATION, 396 of 396 match, 21 scrolling
  textures, 0 differ.
- `heapcfg.c`: LINEAR_WANT is 112 MB. The race uses about 45 MB of the
  malloc heap, so about 30 MB moves to the linear heap.

### The hitches (the user's ask: "I want them eliminated")

- **The cause.** The cars' solids were baked on their first draw, and
  their textures uploaded then too (render_model, model_solid,
  bake_solid, resolve_textures, load_texture). So were the textures
  that a replacement table, a rename or a first draw reaches. One frame
  took up to 237 ms.
- **The fix.** `trackview_prepare` runs once the track is attached:
  1. It bakes every ModelList model.
  2. It uploads every frame of each flipbook a solid uses.
  3. It uploads every other pack texture with pixels, smallest first,
     while TEX_RESERVE plus PREPARE_RESERVE (6 MB each) stay free and
     128 slots are left.

  `raceAttachTrack` waits up to 150 frames for the streamed packs before
  it runs.
- **The log.** main.c logs `race: prepared in ...`. Whenever a bake or
  an upload happens later, it logs `race: made N bakes ... and N
  uploads ..., the longest X ms: <names>`.
- **On Azahar.** Track 45 with eight cars and traffic:
  - The prepare took 4228 ms: 407 uploads, 17 left out (12.3 MB), 700
    textures, and 12.5 MB of linear heap free.
  - In the race: 0 late bakes or uploads.
  - Worst frames 67-74 ms, against 237 before.
- **The cost.** The load is about 4 s longer. An upload is about 13 ms
  of CPU on Azahar. The texel scan is done once an upload now, not
  three times.

### The AI pack's cost (open; the user's ask)

The user's words: "sluggish until I get away from all the AI racers",
then "still hitching when all the AI cars are in the view at once". It
is no hitch now, but a steady 15 FPS while the pack is in view, and 30
once it is gone.

The frame profiler gained a `cars:` line and counts the lit batches'
command words (frameprof.h). Track 45's start on Azahar, eight cars in
view:

- **The frame.** 66.7 ms: draw 48 ms, models 16.6 ms, cars 18.2 ms.
  Later, with the pack gone: cars 2.7 ms.
- **The cars stage.** Setup 0.2, shadows 4.1, body 3.4, wheels 3.0, and
  the lists 7.4 ms.
- **The lit batches.** 143 lit batches wrote 64,740 of the view's
  127,676 command words: **453 words each**. A scenery batch writes
  about 43.

The causes, read from the code:

- **The lit batches' state.** Every one runs `bind_lit` in
  georender.c, which forgets the run, binds geolit and resends about 25
  uniforms.
  - geolit and geosolid are separate DVLBs, so each switch between them
    makes citro3d upload the other's shader code again
    (C3DiF_VshCode).
  - Most of those uniforms are the same for every batch of a model.
- **The shadows.** Each car makes about 18 strips: the hull's fan and
  edge, and the grid's three. Each strip in `georender_draw_strip`
  forgets the run and sends the program, the buffers, about 13
  uniforms and the combiner before one small draw. The shadow's CPU
  side also asks the topology for 20 to 30 elevations a car.

The plan, in order:

1. Build geosolid and geolit into one shbin (picasso takes both files),
   so they share one DVLP and a switch sends no code. Check it with
   check_shbin and on the device: see the PICA freeze notes.
2. Keep the lit uniforms last sent, and send only what changed. Keep the
   run's state across lit batches instead of forgetting it.
3. Strips: keep their state between strips with the same texture, pass
   and model-view, so each costs only its draw. Or join a car's strips
   into one draw.
4. Measure again with the `cars:` line and the lit words.

## Session 54 (2026-10-08) -- the AI pack, from 15 FPS to 20

### The lit batches and the strips (commit 569dfde)

Session 53's plan, steps 1 to 3. The details are in
`docs/formats/draw-cuts.md`, 13b-5.

- geolit is linked into geosolid's shbin.
- c3dwrap.c's uniform cache sends only what changed.
- The lit batches and the strips keep the run's state.

Each lit batch now writes about 248 words, against 453 before. The
frame stayed at 15 FPS.

### "STILL REALLY BAD LAG": the battery

The user's laptop was on battery. Azahar ran at Speed 38 to 69%, with a
host frame of 25 to 44 ms. Plugged in, the same build read 100% with a
6 to 8 ms host frame. The user: "RUNS JUST FINE! With all the AI cars
in the scene at once it definitely runs a lot better, but its still
not 30 FPS". The `azahar-speed-limit` memory has the battery note.

### Where the time went

A pair of timers round render_model's draw (taken out before the
commit) showed georender's calls were most of the cost:

- The view's draw: 16.9 ms for about 1,470 batches.
- The cars' models: 5.6 ms.
- The envmap and the mirror: 3.1 ms and 2.7 ms.

That is about 11 us, or 3,000 instructions, a batch. Disassembly put
about 700 of a draw's instructions in citro3d writing its 15 registers
one GPUCMD_Add at a time.

### Citro3d's draws in one go (commit ba9ef1f)

c3dwrap.c wraps `C3D_DrawElements`, `C3D_DrawArrays` and `GPUCMD_Add`
(the Makefile's C3DWRAP). A draw is written from a template after
citro3d's own `C3Di_UpdateContext`. The first draw of each kind is
citro3d's, compared word for word with the template, and the
context's head is checked, before any draw is written here. Both
checks pass on Azahar: `c3d: indexed draws written here` and `c3d:
array draws written here`.

## Session 55 (2026-10-08) -- the texture cache and the spare VRAM

The user's ask: "so no matter the map or circumstances, all textures
load and they all load perfectly", done globally. Steps a and d were
3b62e00 (the formats, LINEAR_WANT 112 MB). This session did b and c
(commit 2f0a300).

### b, the texture cache (trackview.c)

- Before, a texture that would not fit went in at a smaller mip level
  or not at all, and was never tried again.
- Now `load_texture` makes room at level 0 first (`make_room`): the
  textures in the linear heap drawn longest ago are let go of
  (`evict_lru`, `evict`). The prepare's guesses that nothing drew go
  first. An evicted texture keeps its pixels in its pack. Its slots are
  cleared, so `follow_table` uploads it again when it is next drawn
  (`retry_texture`).
- Room by the count is not room in one piece. When the chain will not
  go in, more go one at a time until it does (`upload_room`). One level
  without a chain is the last resort. Flipbook frames of a texture drawn
  of late do the same.
- A texture that finds no room is tried again 30 frames later
  (`retryAt`), not never.
- The clock: `cacheClock` moves once a race frame (begin_frame) and once
  a frontend frame. `note_use`, `load_texture` and `follow_table` stamp
  `lastUse`; `follow_table` stamps all of a solid's textures before it
  loads any, so none it is about to draw goes. Nothing drawn this frame
  or the last goes (CACHE_KEEP_FRAMES).
- The log's race line gains "evicted". A texture missing for room is
  still listed; an evicted one is not.

### c, the spare VRAM

- During `trackview_prepare` (between frames, `vramOk`), an upload goes
  to VRAM while it leaves 512 KB (VRAM_RESERVE). The screens', envmap's
  and mirror's targets are all made at boot, so VRAM's other textures
  never compete with them.
- `texpack_upload_chain_vram` builds the chain in a linear copy, then
  copies it whole with `C3D_SyncTextureCopy`, as `C3D_TexLoadImage`
  does. Outside a frame citro3d waits for the copy. Inside one it would
  queue it, so mid-race uploads stay in the linear heap.
- `evict_lru` skips textures in VRAM: they give the linear heap nothing.
- The prepare's line gains "(N in VRAM, KB, KB of VRAM free)".

|---|---|---|
| Track 12, 7 AI: textures | 733 | 745 |
| left out by the prepare | 18 (10.9 MB) | 5 (6.1 MB) |
| in VRAM | 0 | 39 (3.9 MB) |
| Track 45, 7 AI: left out | 17 (12.3 MB) | 4 (6.8 MB) |
| in VRAM | 0 | 58 (3.9 MB) |
| the prepare | 4.2-4.4 s | 5.1 s |

Both races: 0 missing, 0 reduced, 0 late uploads, 30 FPS with the
pack out of view.

**The squeeze test (not committed).** At frame 90 every texture that
could go was let go of, then the linear heap was held down with 1 MB
blocks. The first version lost VAUXHALL_SKIN8 and ELISE_SKIN2 with 13 MB
free: no hole was big enough, and the one retry looked only at the
count. With `upload_room`: 0 missing and 0 reduced. 213 more textures
went for room over the run; CL55AMG_SKIN3 went in on its fourth try.

### e, the skins' padding: left

A 512x320 skin is padded to 512x512. Cutting that means splitting each
car's batches at v = 256, or packing other textures into the padding
with a UV offset. Neither is needed while every map's textures fit with
the cache, so it waits for a map that needs it.

## Session 56, continued (2026-10-08) -- 12c, CopMover

CopMover, the mover half of retail's copdriver.obj: what a cop car rides
when no player is near enough for physics. `copdriver.c` is new, and
`copdriver.h` has the record. `docs/formats/cop-mover.md` has the record,
the tuning, Move step by step, and the check.

### What it does

- **Two states.** STEERING turns the heading towards the one wanted, at
  a rate the speed sets, and brakes or accelerates the speed towards the
  one wanted. TRANSLATING eases a velocity towards the one wanted: the
  part along the velocity brakes or accelerates, and the part across it
  is held to 35 m/s/s and its change to 150. The heading follows the
  velocity. CopDriver asks for TRANSLATING only at 13.41 m/s or more.
- **Braking** climbs a ramp (retail's new word at 64) at two a second,
  and the most it may brake scales with it. The driver's Brake shows it
  past 0.3 of the most, or with the ramp full.
- **The throttle's most** falls from fMaxThrottleAccel (by car type,
  11.25 to 15) to nothing at the top speed. The top speed is 84.935 m/s
  less 10 or 5 mph for the easier strengths. Past the throttle's most,
  the car's nitro flag is set.
- **Held to the ground.** Up to 4 m/s into the ground's normal is taken
  off; more puts the car in the air. On the ground it is sat on five
  height samples, tipped to their slopes, unless they span more than
  2 m. The wheels turn at the speed, on the road, with nothing on them.
- **The record** is retail's 128 bytes (the demo's is 112). The port's
  bVector3 is word-aligned, so the image's padding at 12 is spelled out.
  The ARM build's layout check caught it.
- main.c installs the table and binds `gCopMoverCtorFn`;
  `COPMOVER_SIZE` is `sizeof(CopMover)`. Nothing builds one until
  CopDriver (12d) asks for COP_MOVEMENT.

### What it does

- **The record**, 76 bytes in both images: a TrackedController, the
  state, the state before getting stuck, the sub-state, two timers, the

  class. The constructor gives it a NullDriver.
- **Think**: TrackedController's, then on COP_MOVEMENT only:
  - stuck (in a collision, under 2 m/s, for 1 s) and not within 20 m of
    the chased car, it backs up for 2 s at 20 mph;

  - PATROLLING steers for the point 20 m along its drive target, at the
    patrol speed;
  - PURSUIT, within 40 m of the chased car, going its way and at
    30 mph or more, *translates*: a velocity, the chased car's (a
    player's from the pursuit's history) plus the way to the target,
    weighted by the sub-state. Otherwise it *steers* for the target at
    a speed by the sub-state. That speed is held to the route's driving
    line speed times 1.15 to 1.25, and to 20 mph while the chased car
    is more than a quarter turn off.
- **GetPursuitTargetPoint** takes the pursuit's near or far drive
  target, or builds its own along the chased car's route (ACQUIRE,
  STOP) or its own (LIMBO_DISABLED).

  InitializeDriveTarget picks a route point by the state asked for: on
  patrol, the nearest oncoming point if it's on the road (else the

  UpdateDriveTarget walks the point up to a position, at most ten

  Then it lays twenty points down the route at the cop's offset and

## Session 57, continued (2026-10-08) -- 12e, the track graph

Retail's TrackGraph.obj, in a new `trackgraph.{c,h}`: the racing routes
as a graph, which the cops search for roadblock and radar-trap spots.
With it come two more of `coputil.obj`, GetForwardTrackDistance and
IsTeleportLocationClear. `docs/formats/track-graph.md` is new.

### What it does

- **The records.** Retail's edge is 48 bytes, the demo's 40 with two
  words before the lists: the cloaked argument and a NoHelisheet flag.
  So the graph is 23216 bytes, not 20016. Vertex[100], Edge[400], the
  table at 0x002bf3d8 (slot 8, the destructor), and two slot pools of
  128 twelve-byte infos.
- **The constructor** takes a vertex for each signposted point of
  routes 0 to 48, skipping a Backwards sign that is not a Stop. The
  edges depend on the sign:
  - a Stop that is not Backwards gets none;
  - AlwaysTake and a Backwards Stop get one, down the sign's route;
  - any other sign gets two: one down the vertex's own route, and one
    down the sign's, cloaked as the sign is.

  Each edge runs to the next signposted point that is a vertex, where
  GetVertexNumber matches either the point or a sign's target. It
  takes every spot on the way, both ends included. Last come the
  backward edges, and a swap that puts first the one on the forward
  edge's route.
- **The searches.** FindRoadBlock and FindSpeedTrap find the car's
  edge by its route and point, then walk forward (To vertex, first
  forward edge) or back (From vertex, first backward edge), five edges
  at most. They take the first spot whose forward track distance
  is in [fMin, fMax). A roadblock must also be clear to teleport to:
  at least 250 from both players and 15 from every car.
- **Two of retail's reads off the end.** Neither happens on any retail
  track; a survey of all 30 found none:
  - A dead-end edge's backward pass lands its number in
    bHasCloakedEdge. The port does the same.
  - A forward walk from a dead-end edge reads the word before the
    block. The port stops there instead.
- main.c installs the table and binds `gInitTrackGraphFn` and
  `gCleanupTrackGraphFn`, so World's constructor builds the graph after
  InitCops and its destructor frees it. Nothing searches it yet; 12j's
  roadblocks and the radar traps will.

## Session 58 (2026-10-08) -- 12g-1, tAICop::Think

Retail's tAICop::Think and what it runs on its own, in `cop.c`, with
ResetAllDamage in `copmgr.c`. `docs/formats/cops.md` has a new Think
section. Before it, b94f189 put the logic sub-states in retail's
numbering: retail has two values the demo's `.mdebug` lacks, at 1 and
2 (2 is PATROL_ONCOMING; 1 is not named yet), so every later name is
two higher.

### What it does

- **Think** (`0x0022df88`, slot 24): the grace timer at 32 counts down;
  the camera's car shows its drive target; MovementModeTransitions; a
  car on its side or roof below 10 mph, or with a tire blown, is
  disabled (DisableMyCar with 1 or 0); the sub-state's timer counts
  down to 0; a state change goes through HandleStateTransitions; the
  state's logic runs; and the offset at 48 eases toward MyDLOffset at
  6 and 3 a second.
- **MovementModeTransitions** (`0x0022e578`): off COP_MOVEMENT, after
  the time in physics mode is past 0, a 0.1 s delay that restarts while
  the car has a wheel up, skids (more than 10 degrees off its heading
  above 17.88 m/s) or spins (above a radian a second); at its end, back
  to COP_MOVEMENT. On COP_MOVEMENT, a car the cop mover says is in the
  air drops to MELLOW_MOVEMENT with its upward speed held to 2 m/s and
  its driver on full throttle.
- **HandleStateTransitions** (`0x0022e1f0`): what leaving DISABLED,
  LIMBO and SPEED_TRAP undoes, and what entering each of the eight
  states sets: the collisions, drawing, the mover, the driver's state,
  the lights, the siren, the map and the sub-state. The doc has the
  table.
- **The three still states.** Limbo, disabled and guarding hold the car
  where it is (retail's `0x00230a60`). Limbo turns LIMBO_DISABLED into
  LIMBO_READY when its 1 s is up; disabled asks for limbo once no
  player is within 250 m.
- **ResetAllDamage** (`0x00228750`): the blown tires fixed, the
  traction boost 1, the manager's damage 0, the CarDamage repaired (a
  seam that aborts; no port car has one yet), and a player's e-brake
  stop let off.
- **The EE's products.** A part of the offset already in place divides
  0 by 0, FLT_MAX on the EE, and the EE's `mul.s` gives FLT_MAX again
  where IEEE has an infinity. Times a frame of 0 that is 0 on the EE and
  a NaN on the 3DS. `eefpu.h` has `ee_mul` for it, and `mipsemu.py` an
  `eemul` option that collects the sites (only this one so far).
- **Seams.** The seven state logics and tPlayerCop's Think are NULL and
  do nothing; CarDamage's repair aborts if reached.
- **The cops' cars.** `main.c` now binds `gAddCopCarToRaceFn`, so a race
  with cops makes them: each starts in limbo and stays there, since
  nothing asks a cop out yet.

## Session 58, continued (2026-10-08) -- 12g-2, the radar traps, roadblocks and patrols

The logic of three of tAICop's states, ported from retail into
`cop.c`, with two more `coputil.obj` helpers in `coputil.c`.
`docs/formats/cops.md` has a new section, "Radar traps, roadblocks and
patrols".

### What it does

- **Teleport** (`0x0022de70`): COP_MOVEMENT, then ResetToPosition at
  (x, y, 0), speed 0. **SetSpeedTrap** (`0x0022ded8`) and
  **SetRoadBlock** (`0x0022df18`) link the cop to its spot, teleport it
  there, and ask for SPEED_TRAP or ROAD_BLOCK.
- **InitSpeedTrapLogic** (`0x0022e798`) and **InitRoadBlockLogic**
  (`0x0022ebc0`) park the car (stopped, off the map, the driver
  PARKED). The trap clears its pursuit, waits 15 s, and has its lights
  off. The roadblock keeps its pursuit and has lights 1. HandleState-
  Transitions now calls both directly.
- **DoSpeedTrapLogic** (`0x0022e838`) holds still. Once its 15 s are up
  with no player within 250 m, it goes to limbo. Otherwise it goes back
  to its spot when it is 1 cm or 100 BAM off and CanTeleport allows it,
  and searches.
- **DoRoadBlockLogic** (`0x0022ec38`) holds still and goes back to its
  spot the same way. It keeps the grace timer at 3 s.
- **DoDrivingOnPatrolLogic** (`0x0022ee50`) clears the offsets, updates
  the drive target, goes to limbo with no player within 250 m, and
  otherwise searches.
- **The search** looks at the players' and racers' cars within 45 m in
  x and y, and 2.5 m in z. It checks **IsValidPursuitTarget**
  (`0x0022ea88`): not Be A Cop's car, not pulled over, not inside its
  pursuable time; then a car that caused a crash, one above 80 mph, or
  one already chased. A patrol also needs **CanPatrollerSeeThisCar**
  (`0x0022ed68`): within 50 m, moving, and 20 m on along its own way of
  travel. Then tCopManager::RequestPursuit (`0x00225078`, the new NULL
  seam `gCopManagerRequestPursuitFn`) is asked, and a granted chase
  means HOT_PURSUIT.
- **CanTeleport** (`0x00230ff0`): no player within 250 m of the car or
  of the spot, and no other car within 15 m of the car.
  **CarCausedRecentCollision** (`0x00231118`): the first two-car
  collision this frame whose other car is stopped, or in front and
  slower.
- **tRoadBlock**: the `.mdebug`'s `bVector4 pos` and `int ang` are read
  as two cops' spots and headings, so `copmanager.h` now has
  `CopPos[2]` and `CopAng[2]` there, with the same offsets.

The game plays the same as before: RequestPursuit grants nothing and no
cop leaves limbo yet.

## Session 58, continued (2026-10-08) -- 12g-3, the chase

The hot pursuit and caught speeder logics, ported from retail into
`cop.c`. DidTheseCarsCollide is added to `coputil.c`.
`docs/formats/cops.md` has a new section, "The chase".

### What it does

- **DoHotPursuitLogic** (`0x0022ff58`) takes up the sub-state asked
  for, then measures the gap round the track (CompareDistances).
  - 450 m either way: ReturnToPatrol and ClearPursuit.
  - 180 m behind: ACQUIRE.
  - 6 m ahead of a car at 20 mph or more: FOLLOW_BACKWARDS if it's going
    against its route, else BLOCK.
  - Then it runs the sub-state's logic.
- **The ten sub-logics** (`0x0022f000` to `0x0022fee0`):
  - follow behind, 6.5 m for the primary and 13 m for the other cop;
  - draw for a flank, if the other cop's zone allows it;
  - pull out 3 m to the side, come level, then bump the chased car or
    get ahead of it, by the pursuit's behaviour bit 4 and a 2-in-15
    draw;
  - BUMP shoves the chased car through its collision body's physics
    mode and impulse, by 7, 10 or 15 for the level;
  - block ahead, follow a car going backwards, follow close when slow,
    and stop on it.
- **ReturnToPatrol** (`0x00230cb0`): DRIVING_ON_PATROL, racing above
  30 mph and oncoming below.
- **GetBestFlankSide** (`0x00230248`): the side with 3 m of road free.
  The cop's own side comes first, then 0 when it is level within
  2.5 m.
- **DoCaughtSpeederLogic** (`0x002303c8`): holds still. In WAITING it
  goes to limbo with no player within 250 m, or back on patrol when its
  timer is 0; then it searches.
- **DidTheseCarsCollide** (`0x00231268`): whether this frame's two-car
  collisions include the other car.
- The other cop's flank side is read from AI cops only. Retail reads it
  past the end of a tPlayerCop; the side never counts in a sub-state a
  player's cop holds.
- `gAICopDoHotPursuitLogicFn` and `gAICopDoCaughtSpeederLogicFn` are
  gone: Think calls the logics straight.

The game plays the same as before: RequestPursuit grants nothing yet,
so no cop is in a chase.

## Session 59 (2026-10-08) -- 12h-1, tPursuit

tPursuit's object and how a chase is granted, ported from retail into
the new `pursuit.c`, with retail's BarricadeManager in `barricade.c`.
Also new: `docs/formats/pursuit.md`.

### What it does

- **The records:** tPursuitHistory's and tRoadBlockStateMachine's
  constructors and destructors, and the state machine's
  DisbandRoadBlock.
- **The constructor** (`0x00228fc8`):
  - builds the drive targets, the history, the state machine and the
    barricades;
  - sets the timers, and the roadblock spawn time by difficulty;
  - measures the chased car's top speed (GetTopSpeed, `0x00231338`);
  - takes a speaker: Be A Cop's, or one from the queue for a player;
  - starts at LEVEL0, or LEVEL3 in the AI demo.
- **The destructor** (`0x00229198`) releases the cops and gives back a
  player's speakers. It sets the id to -2, deletes the barricades, and
  frees the slot.
- **The states:** SwitchPursuitState, its timer (the table at
  0x0031c570, scaled by the race's length) and DoStateTransition.
  LEVEL2 and LEVEL3 may call the supervisor (PossibleCallSupervisor).
  Giving up backs the cops off, scores BEAT_THE_COPS and releases them.
- **The cops:** ReleaseAllCops, DisbandRoadBlock, RemoveCopFromPursuit,
  IsCopInPursuit and SelectPrimaryCop.
- **The speakers:** GetCopSpeaker, GetSecondaryCopSpeaker,
  IsPlayerInvolved, RemovePrimarySpeaker and
  RoadBlockEncounteredRecently.
- **The one-liners** at `0x0022d210`..`0x0022d338`.
- **The manager's:**
  - RequestPursuit (`0x00225078`), with the limits for split screen,
    one player, AI cars and Be A Cop;
  - NewPursuit (`0x002244e0`);
  - DeleteRoadBlockSpikeStrips (`0x00227be8`).
- **BarricadeManager** (new in retail): ten barrel ids and fade
  timers. It has a constructor, a destructor that deletes the barrels,
  and Fade.

Two retail quirks are kept:

- ReleaseAllCops releases only the first of two cops.
- An empty speaker queue hands the constructor 0x41a00000. That is
  ReserveCopSpeaker's leftover a2, the first word of the constructor's
  copy of {20, 15, 10}.

`main.c` binds `gPursuitRemoveCopFromPursuitFn` and
`gPursuitRemovePrimarySpeakerFn`, and installs the two tables.
`gCopManagerRequestPursuitFn` stays NULL until Update is in (12h-2), so
no chase is made yet and the game plays as before.

The cop speech calls and the Busted NIS do nothing while NULL. These
abort if reached, and nothing reaches them yet:

- the helicopter's (12k);
- the barrels' delete and fade byte (12i);
- BlinkBlinkPoof (12j).

## Session 59, continued (2026-10-08) -- 12i-1, the roadblocks' running logic

What a chase does with its roadblock once it has one, ported from
retail into `pursuit.c`. `docs/formats/pursuit.md` has a new section,

### What it does

- **RequestRoadBlock** (`0x0022cc38`): the state machine, at NONE, has
  the cop ask for a spike strip or a roadblock, once. In Be A Cop it
  spends one of the manager's roadblocks, or dispatch says none is left.
  The machine then waits 8 s at CALLED_FOR_ROAD_BLOCK.
- **MonitorRoadBlock** (`0x0022c390`): a player's car that hits a
  roadblock cop is braked. A real driver gets ForceEBrakeStop for 5 s,
  an AI car's PsychoDriver 4 s on its e-brake timer. Above 40 mph, and
  with the zone's say-so, the bust sound plays. The car has got by when
  it is within the road's width and more than 5 past the roadblock
  along the route, the chase's way.
- **RoadBlockDefeated** (`0x00229970`): the chase gives up near the
  end of a long race, or else the failed-roadblock speech, the
  DODGE_ROADBLOCK score and the replay's DodgeRoadblock event. A chase
  following backwards waits longer for the next one. The roadblock
  count sets behaviour bit 0x80, 0x40, or 0x110 with the helicopter.
- **UpdateRoadBlocks** (`0x00229b58`): a blown tyre takes the roadblock
  down. A car that got by, or that is 100 to 100 + a fifth of the
  track past it when the disband timer runs out, passes it. With none,
  the spawn timer runs down and a new one is asked for.
- `main.c` binds `gPursuitUpdateRoadBlocksFn`. Nothing makes a
  roadblock before 12i-2, so a race plays as before.
- New NULL seams: six speeches, the bust sound, and
  RealDriver::ForceEBrakeStop. The port's RealDriver is still the

  cop allowed it sets behaviour bit 0x10 (a spike strip), then asks the

  The cops placed get SetRoadBlock; with bit 0x10, AddSpikeStrip lays
  the strip.

  a gap, a spike strip and barrels by the spike side, World::Random and
  bSpikeStrips. **The plan** (`0x0024fb78`) sizes them to the road: the
  escape lane (`0x0022ca78`, 3.75 down to 2.75 by the roadblock count,
  plus 0.5, 0 or -0.25 by difficulty), 0.8 a gap, the cop cars at 45
  degrees, barrels 3 each (at most 10), strips in 0.65 segments, and
  the rest to the lanes, the wider side of the road getting more. The
  layout then walks the plan from the road's left edge and sets the
  escape lane, the belt, the cops' spots and angles, and spawns the
  barrels.

RealDriver's forced e-brake stop, ported from retail into

### What it does

## Session 59, continued (2026-10-08) -- 12j-1, the radar traps

The manager's SpawnSpeedTraps (`0x00224a20`) and FindCopForSpeedTrap

### What it does

- **FindCopForSpeedTrap** gives the first AI cop that wants LS_LIMBO
  and sits in LSS_LIMBO_READY.
- **SpawnSpeedTraps** goes over the racing cars. For each one not
  finished and not held off by its pursuable timer, it does three
  things:
  - It runs the car's spawn timer down.
  - It rolls by difficulty: a lost roll waits 10, 5 or 1 s.
  - It decides whether the car wants a trap, by these rules:
    - a chased car wants one when its chase has no cops, or has called
      for backup and has room;
    - with two or more chases, an unchased AI car does not;
    - otherwise, the split to the leader must be later than -15 s, or
      the leader finished, or Random(20) gave 19. If none of these
      holds, the car waits 1 s;
    - a free run or a player's car then wants a trap;
    - an AI racer wants one while its tickets lag its laps.
- A car that wants one gets a ready cop and the next free radar trap
  250 m on, if its spot is clear. The cop's SetSpeedTrap teleports it
  there, the car waits 20 s, and the function returns.
- `main.c` binds `gCopManagerSpawnSpeedTrapsFn`. Cops now leave limbo
  for radar traps.
- The harnesses of cop and pursuit stand in for the new calls they
  lack with ones that abort if reached: the split, Timer::SetTime and
  FindSpeedTrap in both, the free run in cop's, and
  IsTeleportLocationClear and SetSpeedTrap in pursuit's.

### The knock fix

The first Azahar run (on AC, Speed 100%) raced, then logged sixteen
unmapped reads at 0x11C, PC `0x001298F4`:
carcollisionbody_get_mass_inverse through a NULL RigidBody. The user,
watching, saw a cop hit them. Only one PC faulted, so it was the
Player's knock test in `hudscore.c`, which asks both bodies of the
player's collision for their inverse mass.

A cop in COP_MOVEMENT has no RigidBody. On contact, CarController's
SetToPhysicsMode (`0x001c0100`) puts it in MELLOW_MOVEMENT, but
taicop_movement_mode_transitions can put it back before the knock test
reads that collision. Retail would read the PS2's word at 0x11C; on a
3DS it is a data abort. The port answers 0, as a static body does.
The knock test only asks whether the other body's inverse mass is under
500, and any car's is at most 0.769, so the score is unchanged.

`tools/collisionbody_check.py` now asks a car body with no RigidBody for
its mass. The model's word at 0x11C is 0, which the checker asserts.
35,427 lines, 0 differ. The new mutations `ccb_mi_no_rb_guard` and
`ccb_mi_no_rb_value` are caught.

### What it does

- **`elightflare.{c,h}`:**
  - Retail's nine parts (`0x002d6080`, 60 bytes: sizes, colours, the
    facing's power, how far toward the camera, the scale clamps, the
    texture) and the ten types' pairs (`0x002d62d8`). The demo's table
    was 64 bytes in another order, so these were read from the image.
  - eLightUpdateTextures: HEADLIGHTFLAREINNER, HEADLIGHTFLAREOUTER and
    HEADLIGHTGLOW from GLOBALB.
  - eRenderLightFlare: it takes the flare to the world, clips it with
    `vclipw`'s rule, and finds the facing (its magnitude for Flags bit
    0, the cops' red and blue) and the depth over H. Then it draws the
    type's parts.
  - The part: pow(facing, Power) from the float's bits, times the
    intensity. The size and colours run from min to max by that, the
    centre is moved toward the camera, and the scale is clamped. A
    square goes to ePoly::Render3D.
  - eRenderWorldLightFlares: while InGameFlag is set, every pack's
    flares through the identity at intensity 1.
- **`epoly.{c,h}`:** `gEPolyRender3DFn`, ePoly::Render3D's seam.

- **`main.c`:** `gELightUpdateTexturesFn` and `gERenderLightFlareFn`.

## Session 60, continued (2026-10-09) -- 12k-3, the route planners

The helicopter follows routes the AI's planners find. Four of them were
not ported: ReturnToLastBranch, FindRoutesToTarget, FindPointsToTarget
and FindNearbySignpost. They are now in `airouteplan.{c,h}`, with
GuessTargetDestinations. `docs/formats/ai-route.md` ("The helicopter's
planners") has the details.

### The light flares' Azahar run

On AC: 30 fps at 100% speed, the headlights glow, and a pursuit with
wanted stars. The user saw the cop's light bar flash ("I mean I did see
a working light bar"). It was also 12k-2's rerun after the knock fix,
and nothing aborted. A longer `-HoldKeys 65` run reported "reached
RACING, then died" at 146 s: the user had closed Azahar, because the
held A kept them from driving. Azahar's log showed a clean shutdown and
there was no `nfshp2_stderr.txt`. Keep held-key runs short.

### What it does

- **`RoutePlanRoutes`**, `Deque<TrackRoute *, 20>` (92 bytes), and
  **`RoutePlanBranches`**, `Deque<NearestRoutePointInfo, 20>` (172).
  Empty is Front == Back with Full clear. Every caller skips a push when
  Full.
- **ReturnToLastBranch** takes the newest branch off, then routes off
  the back until the branch's route is the last.
- **FindRoutesToTarget** searches depth first. A sign that applies and
  names a route not taken is followed, the way on kept as a branch
  unless the sign is 2. A sign 2 or 3 naming a route taken, or a no-go
  point (`TRP_NO_HELISHEET`) with `heli`, goes back to the last branch.
  The branch's point is looked at as it is, without a step.
- **FindPointsToTarget** lists the points towards a target. Its signs
  other than 2 and 3 ask FindRoutesToTarget, and are taken only when
  they name the route at the routes deque's front. That is the start's
  route, so in practice they are passed by. Retail's quirk, kept.
- **FindNearbySignpost** counts the steps to the next signpost.
- **The divergences.** None of these happen on a shipped track:
  - ReturnToLastBranch with the routes run out answers 0. The image
    compares a stale word for ever.
  - A branch with no point counts as running off. The image steps from
    address 0.
  - The look through a full routes deque stops at twenty. The image's
    never ends when Back is 0 or the deque is full.
  - The walk gives up after `ROUTEPLAN_MAX_WALK` (0x11800) steps. The
    image can walk a loop of routes for ever once the deque is full.

them in pseudocode.

### What it does

- **`ChopperTarget`**, 12 bytes on HighLevelPlanning's stack:
  `Location` (bVector2) and `DesiredSpeed`.
- **StartChaseLogic / EndChaseLogic.** The chase starts 150 over the
  sheet, dropping at 25. It ends by climbing at 25 until 150 over the
  sheet, then leaving the world. Off the sheet, the end walks on to the
  first point more than 30 away, at 50.
- **FindPreviousFork** walks back through signposts. It goes on
  through an ALWAYS_TAKE (sign 2) a step into the new route, and
  answers the steps counted. **SwitchToNearbyFork** then looks at up to
  twice that many points from the fork for one within reach.
- **FollowRoute** aims at the first of FindPointsToTarget's five points
  that is the goal or beyond the least distance (Speed * 0.1, at least
  30). Failing that, it aims at the last. It speeds up to the car's speed
  plus 30 unless it is aiming at the goal.
- **BeginStakeout** picks the first signpost ahead without NO_STAKEOUT,
  on a point the helicopter may fly over. It goes to the sign's point
  when the sign is BACKWARDS, else to its new route and point. If the
  helicopter is already past that spot, it stays on its own point.
- **HangoutNearHere** pulls the target towards a point, 0.7 at a time,
  until it is over the sheet. **AdjustTargetInBounds** nudges a local
  target 1.5 towards the sheet's side, up to three times.
- **The signpost's word:** the Flags byte is bits 8-15, the sign the low
  three, BACKWARDS bit 3 and NO_STAKEOUT bit 4.
- **The divergence:** HangoutNearHere stops after a miss once both
  offsets are below the least normal float, or NaN. The EE has flushed
  them to zero by then, and the image tries the point itself for ever.
  In IEEE, 0.7 times the least denormal rounds back to itself, so a
  test for zero never fires.

## Session 60, continued (2026-10-09) -- 12k-3b, the plans

The helicopter's three plans are now in `chopper.{c,h}`:
HighLevelPlanning, CleverPursuitPlan and BombRunLogic. They sit on top
of 12k-3a's chase logic. `docs/formats/chopper.md` ("Planning") has
them in pseudocode.

### What it does

- **HighLevelPlanning** runs every 0.1 s:
  - takes 0.1 off Timeout;
  - looks 0.3 s ahead of the car (bScaleAdd, y before x) and asks the
    sheet about that spot;
  - finds its own route point;
  - runs the plan, then AdjustTargetInBounds and AdjustTargetLocal.
  - A stakeout gives up for PURSUIT once the car's spot is on the sheet
    and within 60, or the time is out. Heading to one, it arrives
    within 30 of the point and waits 45.
- **CleverPursuitPlan:**
  - holds still while climbing or falling off the sheet;
  - with no car point, bails to a point near the helicopter;
  - otherwise takes the car's point ahead of the spot.
  - On the sheet and near, it leads the car along the road above 20.
  - Off the sheet, a TRP_NO_HELISHEET point, or a different fork, means
    a stakeout. Otherwise it hangs out near the point, or follows the
    route.
- **BombRunLogic:**
  - Adds the car's progress to TargetDistance, negative forwards or
    onto another route, then calls AdjustBombTarget.
  - Fires the first salvo within 30 of the target when it is over the
    road at its own point (its offset across, less RightWidth or
    LeftWidth, below 0). Later salvos fire on the SalvoDelay clock.
  - A salvo needs the sheet below and at most 10 over the ground. Each
    resets Timeout to 25, and the last one, or a timeout, means
    PURSUIT.
- **FireSalvo** is 12k-6's. `chopperfire.c` holds a placeholder that
  fires nothing.
- **The divergence:** BombRunLogic skips the car's progress when either
  point is NULL. The image reads address 0 for the position.
- **No NULL car:** Fly (`0x001ea7d0`) returns before Think in
  EATING_DONUTS, the one plan in which FollowThisCar(NULL) leaves
  CurrentCar NULL. END_CHASE never reads the car.

### What it does

- **Think** runs the plans and stops on their 1. Then:
  - **HoverTime:** at rest (speed at most 0.001) within 5 of the target
    and not speeding up, the helicopter turns to face the car's heading
    (PURSUIT) or the way to the car, at 90 degrees a second at most.

    the spot at up to 180 a second.

  the target is ahead, else 100 times the target's x less a tenth of the
  speed; at least GetMaxDeceleration, at most 20.
- **SetYAccel:** none from 90 degrees off the nose, else 100 times the
  target's y. The roll is what is past 5 of it, at most 20.
- **CheckMomentumWithinBounds:** three probes 4.5 off where the
  helicopter will be; off the sheet to a side pushes it the other way by
  0.3 of the speed, and ahead slows it by as much.

### 14-8c in the working tree: bSampleStream, bSampleChain and the stream

`git status` shows:

- **Modified:** `bsnd.c`, `bsnd.h`, `bsound.c`, `bsound.h`,
  `tools/bsound_check.py` and `tools/src/bsound_test.c`.
- **New:** `bsndstream.c`, `bsndstream.h`, `tools/bsndstream_check.py`
  and `tools/src/bsndstream_test.c`.
- **Not part of the slice:** the five `3DS Files/nfshp2_cap_*` files are
  captures left over from earlier sessions. Don't commit them.

What the slice holds:

- **`bsound.c`**, bSample's stream side:
  - `bsample_play` takes `bsnd_voice_play_part` when the sample has an
    offset or a size.
  - `bsample_set_rate` is SetSampleRate (0x00280340).
  - `bsample_chain_new` is the chain sample, which cSEDWedge::Initialize
    builds inline at 0x00205cb4: bSample(1), the "_STREAM" bank and name,
    then LockVoice. The wedge sets the rate (24000) after.
  - `bsample_chain_add` is AddToChain (0x00206760).
  - The stream-active query calls `bsnd_stream_active`.
- **`bsnd.c` and `bsnd.h`**, the driver's streams:
  - the "_STREAM" bank's mono path, `stream_play` (0x0026129c);
  - the "_CHAIN" queue (0x00261e80): 8 parts, retail's at 0x003353b8 in
    52-byte entries, with the count at gp-14344;
  - PlayChain, `play_chain` (0x00262848);
  - `bsnd_voice_play_part`;
  - `bsnd_stream_active` (0x00263090);
  - the BsndSink's new last member, `stream`;
  - BsndDriver's `chain[]`, `chainCount` and `streamVoice`.
- **Where the port departs from retail**, decided this session:
  - **A full queue is guarded.** After a chain finds no voice, retail
    leaves the count at 8; its next part goes past the queue, and
    PlayChain copies nine entries into a frame of eight. The port's
    "_CHAIN" branch drops the part. A "_STREAM" part takes the eighth
    slot.
  - **`streamVoice`:** there is one mono stream, so any voice with a
    StreamChannel asks after the newest stream's channel, as retail's
    GetStreamInfo(2) does. It is set in `stream_start`, starts at -1 in
    `bsnd_init`, and goes back to -1 when `bsnd_voice_stop` or
    `bsnd_update` frees that channel.
  - **A chained part's offset of 0** means the file's own start, past its
    48-byte VAG header, as it does for the first part.
  - **A stream's file name** is the patch's first 32 bytes (0x00261304).
- **`bsndstream.c` and `bsndstream.h`:**
  - the decoder, `bss_decode`, which also builds on the host. A frame
    flagged 7 is not decoded and ends the part; one flagged 1 is decoded,
    then ends it. Predictors above 4 become 0.
  - the 3DS worker (`bsndstream_init`, `exit`, `play`, `stop`,
    `playing` and `owns`). It reads the parts off the card, decodes them
    to PCM16 and queues them on the voice's own ndsp channel.

  The 3DS half of `bsnd.c` wires it in: `hw_stream`, `hw_playing` through
  `bsndstream_owns` and `bsndstream_playing`, and `bsndstream_init` and
  `bsndstream_exit`. The Makefile's wildcard picks the file up.
- **Nothing calls the chain yet.** cSEDWedge, in 14-8d, is its first
  caller.
