  longer found. Here is each of the six, with its fix:
  - **start-key** (pattern not found): `stream_start` now has
    `d->streamVoice = (int16_t)ch;` between the key line and the sink
    call. Make the pattern the key line followed by the streamVoice
    line, and drop the key line in the mutant.
  - **chain-name** (survived): copying 33 bytes changes nothing, since
    `name[32]` is set to '\0' straight after. Mutate it to 31 instead, as
    stream-append-name does.
  - **stream-effect** (survived): no op ever sets EffectVolume. Add an
    `eff|voice|value` op to both sides: the model writes the u16 at
    VOICES+80*v+24, the harness `gD.voice[v].effectVolume`. Use it before
    a deterministic stream on that voice, and now and then in the random
    runs.
  - **stream-stereo** (survived): EQUIVALENT. Once "_STREAM" has matched,
    `bank[6]` is always 'M'. The mutant therefore only lets "_STREAMS"
    through as mono, and "_STREAMS" is not compared.
  - **path-join** (survived): EQUIVALENT, because the case cannot happen.
    The port's load path holds 159 bytes and a name 32: 191 < 254.
  - **dec-pred** (survived): `pred > 5` reads `kFilter[5]`, past the
    table. Whatever the host has there is zero, which is predictor 0's
    pair, so the clamp looks the same. Mutate the other edge, `pred > 3`,
    which the predictor-4 frames catch.
- **Not run yet** since the `bsnd.c` edits:
  - `tools/bsnd_check.py`. Its harness, `tools/src/bsnd_test.c` line 105,
    also needs a trailing NULL for `stream` in kRecSink, to quiet the
    warning.
  - The CIA build, and Azahar.

### Gotchas met this session

- **Bash heredocs mangle backslash escapes**, even with a quoted
  delimiter: `\\n` arrived as a newline, and `'\\0'` as a NUL byte in
  `bsnd.c`. Write any script that has a backslash with the Write tool,
  then run it with python.
- **Line endings:**
  - CRLF: `bsnd.c`, CONTINUE.md, HANDOFF.md and `sound-driver.md`.
  - LF: `bsnd.h`, `bsound.c`, and the checkers and harnesses.
- **The checker's random runs** free every voice every 15 ops (the
  `clear` op). Without that, the streams' keys pile up and a chain finds
  no voice: the full-queue case, which is not compared.

## Session 71 (2026-10-11) -- the Select Car turntable after a race

The user's second device log of 2026-10-10 (`3DS Files/nfshp2_debug.txt`):
a Hot Pursuit quick race on track 62, finished, the End Game Menu's
Quit, then New Main Menu, Hot Pursuit, Be A Cop and Select Car, to see
the points carry over (they did: NFS Points 22360). With it, a photo:
the Crown Victoria on a floor of blue and magenta checks with yellow
and green, where the first visit had shown the brushed-metal turntable.

- **The race.** A median of 22 fps, 13 at the lowest; the user called
  the slowdowns minor. The one long frame, 4846 ms, is the first
  frame's texture prep before Pre Race Stats. The user also confirmed
  on the device that the spike strips work.
- **The cause.** Retail's EndGameFlowLoadingFrontEnd (0x001687a8)
  starts with `sw zero,-24944(gp)` (eDisableFixUpTables = 0) and
  `jal eFixUpTables`. The port's bgf_end_loading_frontend had left both
  out, since at boot the flag is 0 and frontres_load's PostLoadFixup
  had already fixed the tables. BeginGameFlowUnloadingTrackSpecific
  sets the flag, so after a race FRONTB loads with it still set.
  FRONTB's solid list (0x128) comes before its texture packs
  (0x175534), and the solid loader resolves each table as it loads,
  with the default allowed. PLATFORM's BRUSHEDMETAL and
  BRUSHEDMETAL_OUTER are in no pack yet, so both get GLOBALB's
  DEFAULTTEXTURE (0x19006835): 32x32 blue and magenta checks, yellow
  edges, a green arrow. That is the photo.
- **The fix.** gameflow.h's new `fixUpTables` hook, untraced, runs first
  in bgf_end_loading_frontend; main.c's hookFixUpTables clears the flag
  and calls efix_up_tables. bootflow_check (61 scenarios, 46779 lines)
  and bscreens_check (17 scenarios, 1269 lines) still have 0 differ.
  `docs/formats/boot-flow.md`, "End", has the story.
- **On Azahar.** A Hot Pursuit quick race on track 14, paused, Quit
  Race, OK; then Hot Pursuit, Be A Cop (Cops On Mode Select item 2,
  ChallengeBeACop item 3), Be The Cop Setup and Select Car. The
  turntable is lit brushed metal with the car's reflection on it.
- **The build.** RE-6a's eventtree.c does not link yet: it defines
  is_track_an_event_reward and event_tree_is_track_unlocked, which
  quickrace.c has too. For this fix's build it was renamed
  `eventtree.c.wip` (and copied to the scratchpad). It goes back to
  eventtree.c for RE-6a, and step 3 of RE-6a's list must take
  quickrace.c's two stubs out, or make quickrace.c call the trees.
- **Next.** RE-6a from the Session 70 entry above: its checker first.

## Session 76, continued -- TASKS 41, the Starting Grid after the load (done)

- **The cause.** The flow's pass that enters RACING hides the Loading
  screen (Part6), and the End makes the coordinator, whose fly-by puts
  up Pre Race Stats. That frame drew the grid over nothing. The next
  frame's `raceAttachTrack` (main.c) attached and prepared the track
  for 9.3 s (attach about 5 s, `trackview_prepare` 3.3 to 4.4 s), with
  the grid over black on the screen all that time.
- **The fix.** `raceHoldsLoadingScreen`: while a race is up and its
  track is not attached (and the attach has not given up), the frame
  draws nothing. It keeps the blank's pace and the loads' service, and
  the screens keep the last frame drawn, the Loading screen. The attach
  stays after the first `raceFrame`, as before. It now reads the
  streamed packs in place for up to two seconds before the frames'
  wait (bfile's reads are whole in the service), and it gives up on a
  missing file or a failed attach instead of trying each frame. The
  log line says the ms of reads too.

  Pursuit quick race with no keys, shots every 2 s: the Loading screen
  stayed up at App 0 FPS through the 9.3 s, then the Starting Grid

  (`-HoldKeys 65`): PASS, 30.0 fps.

## Session 77 -- the device crashes and the debug log

- **What happened.** The user's New 3DS XL crashed twice on 2026-10-11,
  at random points of a race: Luma's Arm9 data abort, in Process9 (the
  console's own SD driver), in the middle of a two-sector card access
  (R5 0x4a592; 0x094B2400 = 0x4a592 * 512). stderr was blank both times.
- **8afa111.** At first the log's many small flushed writes looked like
  the cause, so on the user's ask the debug log is off by default:
  `DebugLog 1` in sdmc:/nfshp2_config.txt turns it on (configitems.c),
  and with it off main.c opens no nfshp2_debug.txt and skips the race's
  sums. When on, logwriter.c batches two seconds of lines and writes
  whole 512-byte sectors through a 32 KB buffer.
  `tools/azahar_debuglog.ps1`, dot-sourced by every run_azahar script,
  puts `DebugLog 1` on the emulator's card.
- **c2c079a.** It still crashed with the log off. The user's Luma dump
  (`crash_dump_00000000.dmp`, untracked, in the repo root) has
  Process9's cluster lookup returning NULL on a 1 KB read of the cop
  speech's ENGLISHDAT.PCK at 0x094B2400. So it is the card or that file,
  not the port's writes; logwriter.h's comment says so now.
- **Open.** At the end of the session the user was copying all the
  NFSHP2 files to the card again. If the crashes stop, it was a bad copy
  of that file. If not: a read-only check of the card's ENGLISHDAT.PCK
  (its hash against extracted-retail, its fragments, a read at
  0x094B2400), then think about the card itself.

## Session 78 -- 12m-3c-2, Select Track's slideshow (done)

- **Ported.** main.c's five pack hooks are retail's TexturePack over
  `texturestream.h`: `packNew` is `newStreamedPack("TrackSelect",
  "FRONTEND\\TSELECT.BIN")`, `packDelete` `texturepack_destruct(p, 3)`,
  and the rest `UnloadAllTexturesFromFile`, `GetTexture` and
  `LoadTexturesFromFile`, serviced each frame as the race's packs are.
- **The pictures on the GPU.** The port's renderer draws from bundles,
  not from a pack's records, so `trackSelSyncPictures` runs as the frame
  begins: it asks `btracksel_show_textures` for the two bitmaps'
  textures, decodes a shown one the pack has loaded through texpack.c's
  upload, and draws it in the hash's place with
  `uirender_override_texture`. A picture neither shows is freed, and
  `uirender_forget_texture` (new) gives its slot back, so 159 pictures
  over time cannot fill uirender's 256. All TSELECT texels have alpha
  0x7d, so they stay RGBA8, lossless.
- **The specks.** Some pictures have single white pixels. They are the
  disc's: the loaded bytes equal the file's (a temporary check, now
  gone), `texpack_check.py` decodes all 159 the same as the C, and the
  source pictures have them (39 of 159; `TRACK11C`'s are sky between
  leaves at its right edge, where the first run showed them).
- **Y fixed.** `run_azahar_carsel.ps1` sent key 0 for SQUARE because
  `$VK_X` was undefined; with 88 the log has "last SQUARE". The script
  also now waits for Cops On Mode Select's HIGHLIGHT before DOWN: one
  run's early press was dropped and it started a quick race.
- **Checked on Azahar.** build_cia.ps1 built clean (relocations OK,
  shaders OK). `run_azahar_carsel.ps1 -Choose -RunSeconds 150` passed:
  Select Track opens on FRONTB's `TRACK11`, cross-fades after four
  seconds to `TRACK11C`, SQUARE goes to National Forest's `TRACK12B`
  behind its locked box, and leaving the screen frees the picture
  ("tracksel picture 55ca90d9 down"). tracksel_check: 3132 ops, 30026
  lines, 0 differ.
- **The device.** The user reported French and English speech playing
  at once and then the crash again, after deleting and recopying the
  files. The port opens one language's speech, so this looks like the
  card's FAT (two files sharing clusters), which recopying cannot fix.
  Told the user: back up, then `chkdsk X: /f` or a FAT32 reformat and a
  fresh copy, and H2testw if it still fails.

## Session 86 -- the profiles: the saver, Load/Save and a save prompt after each race

The user's order of 2026-10-12: finish the save and load work in
`memcard.c`, then the munitions (TASKS 39), then the debug menu.

- **The saver.** `memcard.c` gains retail's `MemcardSaver` (0x00246b68
  .. 0x002469e0, its tables at 0x002bee00 and 0x002bee40). It has the
  checks, the format, the overwrite, the write and the cancel that
  turns autosave back off. It also gains `LoadSaveWrapper` (0x00247830),
  which is "Phils Load Save", the Options menu's Save, Load and
  Autosave line, and `Autosaver` (0x00247d00) with
  SetAutosaveCompletionCallback (0x00247d98). `gameflow.c`'s
  `bgf_load_save_callback` and `bgf_autosave_callback` are the two
  screens' callbacks. `main.c` registers "Phils Load Save" and
  "Autosave". "Autosave" uses BootAutoload's Flailer screen, which INGAMEB
  has a copy of. The Load/Save screen gets a setLanguageId hook, and
  the card's CHECK_EXISTENCE sets fileExists.
- **The prompt after each race (the user's ask).** endgame.c's
  `gEndGameAlwaysAskToSave` (main.c sets it) sends Quit and Next Race
  through "Autosave" even with autosave off. `gf->saveAskCreate` makes
  the Autosaver ask 151023 ("create the save?") before it makes the
  file. So each race ends with a create or overwrite question, and No
  goes on without saving. Retail never asks 151023: it is the demo's
  question, and the retail saver's state 16 is unreached. A pause menu
  Quit still leaves without a save, as retail's does.
  `bgf_set_autosave_completion_callback` calls the callback at once when
  no Autosave screen is up.
- **The checker.** `bootflow_check` runs retail's LoadSaveWrapper and
  Autosaver Callbacks and SetAutosaveCompletionCallback against
  `gameflow_test.c`: 95 scenarios, 0 differ. Its 34 save rows cover
  create, overwrite, decline, no card, unformatted, format (it works,
  fails, or the card was fixed under the prompt), a full card, a failed
  write, a new card, a pulled card, a file gone, autosave on and off,
  the skip question, Load, the bloom, BACK, the Options movie and the
  port's create question. For that question the checker patches the
  `jal StartWrite` at 0x0024631c to a stub that runs retail's own
  DisplayYesNoMessage and sets state 5. There are 76 mutations: 75 are
  caught, and `lsw-menu-live-while-saving` is equivalent (the menu is
  hidden and the popup takes every button). `endgame_check`: 0 differ.
  Its dismiss mutations, 6 of 6, include the new
  `dismiss-always-autosave`.

## Session 87, continued -- TASKS 55, the Luma dumps on closing

The user's report: closing the game from the HOME Menu, or powering off
while it runs, leaves a Luma ARM11 dump
(`3DS Files/crash_dump_00000002.dmp` and `..03.dmp`).

- **The dumps.** Luma's format 1.3: an ARM11 data abort in "NFSHP2 3",
  the same in both:
  - pc 0x0021b818 and lr 0x001f02b4, sp 0x0807e728;
  - DFSR 0x805, a write translation fault at FAR 0x0807e718 (sp - 16);
  - the last word of the code dump is `push {r4, r5, r6, lr}`.
  In the build's ELF (`3DS Files/build/NFSHP2-3DS.elf`, where the code
  bytes sit at the same address) pc is LightLock_Lock and lr is
  threadguard's `guard_main`. Its stack is in the heap (0x08xxxxxx).
- **The cause.** The log shows the teardown ran to the slot pools, so
  `main` returned. libctru's exit then frees the heap before it ends
  the process. threadguard's thread (since 2026-10-12) wakes every 10 ms
  above the game's priority, and nothing stopped it. Its next push hit
  unmapped memory. hangwatch's watchdog (every 250 ms, detached) and the
  log's writer (a 2 s timed wait, detached) could do the same.
- **The fix.** `threadguard_stop`, `hangwatch_stop` and
  `logwriter_stop` each end their thread and join it:
  - the guard checks a flag after each tick;
  - the watchdog waits on a stop event instead of sleeping;
  - the writer writes everything left and quits.
  The three threads are made joinable. `main.c` registers the stops
  with atexit, so they run on every way out, before the heap goes. They
  run last first: the guard, the watchdog, then the writer (in place of
  the old atexit drain). The speech, jukebox and movie workers were
  already joined in their closes, and the movie's waits have no
  timeout.
- **Seen on Azahar.** run_azahar_test, leaving through the screen
  viewer: PASS, every line through the slot pools on the card, and
  Azahar back at its game list 3 s after START, so the joins return.
  Azahar's own log is cut when a run kills it, so the device is the
  real check.
- **Not changed.** An abort still ends through the same exit with the
  threads up. It is a crash either way, and the reason is on the card
  first.
- **The user's idea of a Quit item** on the main menu would leave
  through this same exit, so it needed this fix too. HOME's Close now
  does the same job cleanly; there is no Quit item yet.
- **Next.** TASKS 56, the NFS points kept and summed.

## Session 87, continued -- TASKS 56, the NFS points kept

The user's report: a race's points said they were saved, but the next
run had none (`3DS Files/nfshp2_debug.txt`).

- **The log.** BootAutoload loaded the save ("flow fred loaded ...
  7bd4f315"). Then "Language Options Pre FE" came up, and choosing a
  language logged "fred defaults": FrontendDatabase::InitWithDefaults
  on Fred, which wiped what was just loaded. That is everything the
  save held, not only the points.
- **The cause.** The port's boot stages had the demo's order.
  - The demo's LaunchFrontendMenus (0x0016aa40) pushes the language
    screen and then BootAutoload, so the card is checked first.
  - Retail's (0x0016f950) pushes BootAutoload and then the language
    screen (`ShouldSeeAutoloadScreen` at 0x0016f9e8, then
    `ShouldSeeLanguageSelectScreen` at 0x0016fa04, pushing 0x002b2fb8
    "BootAutoload" and 0x002b2fc8 "Language Options Pre FE").
  The stack is LIFO, so retail asks for the language first.
  OverwriteFred then copies the save over the defaults, and keeps the
  language just chosen at +372, which only makes sense in that order.
- **The fix.** `main.c`'s kBootStages and `gameflow_test.c`'s have
  retail's order, and so does `bootflow_check`'s Python. The PAL rows'
  inputs moved to the language screen's frames. A new row, `palcard`,
  boots PAL with a save, chooses French and shows "frontend defaults",
  then BootAutoload, then "fred loaded". 96 scenarios, 0 differ.
  `run_azahar_test` now expects the language screen before
  BootAutoload. boot-flow.md has retail's order, the demo's, and why
  it matters.
- **Seen on Azahar** (100%):
  - run_azahar_coprace: the boot loaded the card's 11,000 points over
    the defaults, and the cop race ended with "points 11100".
  - Quit on the End Game Menu, Yes to the save: the card holds 11,100
    with a good checksum (b3cbc847).
  - run_azahar_test: PASS. The language screen, then BootAutoload
    loaded b3cbc847, then the movies. Its "START was taken before
    PRESS START" line is the log's lag: only one START reached the
    title, after PRESS START was up.
  The user saw the points kept.
- **New, TASKS 58.** While watching the cop race, the user saw the car
  clip through the road, walls, rails, hills and other cars. It comes
  next, before TASKS 57.

## Session 87, continued -- TASKS 58, the car through things (closed)

The user saw the car go through the road, walls, rails, hills and
other cars in a scripted cop race on Azahar. The user closed the task
on 2026-10-12 before a cause was found. No code changed, and the
diagnostics below are not kept.

- **The hull is the body's size.** CROWNVIC's `_CV` hull has 36
  vertices and 68 faces. Back in model space (the hull is moved by
  -CoG, 0.26 0 0.24), it spans x -2.41..2.45, y -0.90..0.95 and
  z 0.18..1.33. The body model's box (carrenderinfo's AABB, less its
  0.1) spans x -2.36..2.46, y -0.97..0.97 and z -0.02..1.69. Only the
  tyres, the mirrors and the light bar reach past the hull.
  GeometryPosition (Position - R CoG) matches the physics.
- **No penetration found.** A logger in `main.c`, gated by DebugLog,
  checked car 0 every frame:
  - every hull vertex against the planes and edges of its
    TrackPolygons;
  - the hulls of the cars within 8 m;
  - VClip again on a copy of each of its witnesses, counted by status.

  The clip13 run (Coastal Parklands, Be A Cop, Crown Vic, gas only for
  70 s) had depth 0.00 for walls, floors and cars every second. VClip
  said "apart" for every pair, except one second with one unsettled
  pair and one inside pair, which was out again within that second.
  Earlier runs flagged two cases:
  - clip12: the hull wrapping round the end of a wall segment. An
    offline replay put the overlap at 3 cm.
  - clip10: the car landing behind a rail after the user's jump at
    189 km/h.
- **Ruled out:**
  - tunnelling through the floor (the lowest point stayed 0.3 to 0.5 m
    over the ground);
  - a missing `_CV` (it is found, so it is not CAR_BOX);
  - junk in the rotation's w lanes;
  - the walls' decode (their z of +/-508 is retail's, so they are
    infinitely tall).
- **The inside views.** POV_BUMPER and POV_INCAR set CarNotToRender.
  render_cars skips that car, as retail's does. RenderDash is read only
  by acidsys's particles, so retail draws no dash. NearZ is the image's
  0.5, and 0.4 in the car. A wall or car within half a metre of the eye
  is therefore cut away, as on the PS2.
- **If it comes back:** compare the rail meshes with their wall
  polygons, which are retail data. A car scraping a rail can show its
  side through the rail (clip9's shot 35, at 2 km/h).

## Session 88 -- TASKS 57, the fire truck track's lag

The user's report of 2026-10-12: the track with the fire truck, its
fire, smoke and fog, lags a bit. Session 87 found the track and
profiled it before it ran out. This session made the change, ran it on
Azahar, and ended at the user's word ("wrap up those GPU optimizations
... and end your session").

- **The place.** Track 11 (TRACKB11.BUN, Coastal Parklands). The
  fire's emitters (`XE_FFire_` flames, smoke and sparks) are at about
  x -580 to -700, y 145 to 240. The truck's water jets
  (`XE_FireTruck_WaterA` to `D`) are at about -584 to -570, 151.
- **The user's device log** (`3DS Files/nfshp2_debug.txt`, track 11
  with four AI and two cops). It is slow from about (434, 229) to the
  fire at (-588, 220): 13 to 18 FPS, with track triangles at 30k to
  50k and up to 511 sprites. The worst second: 13.8 FPS, 72.6 ms. That
  is world 4.5, draw 23.1, vsync 8.7 and GPU wait 35.2; citro3d's GPU
  time was 49.6.
- **GPU-bound, one part after the other.** A least-squares fit over
  274 s of the log (rms 2.4 ms) gives the GPU about 0.09 to 0.14 ms
  per 1,000 indices and 2.3 to 2.5 ms per 100 sprites. The worst
  seconds split as:
  - the view, about 22 ms;
  - the envmap, about 16;
  - the mirror, about 5.5;
  - the sprites, up to 12.8 at the fire.

  The GPU started only at `C3D_FrameEnd`, so a frame was the CPU's draw
  plus the GPU's, about 23 + 50 ms.
- **Not a smaller vertex.** Retail's strips hold positions and texture
  coordinates as 32-bit floats, so a 16-bit vertex would not be exact.
- **The change.** `ConfigGpuSends` is 1 by default (`configitems.c`;
  its comment is in `configitems.h`). TASKS 46's sends had been
  opt-in since 9e044f3. `main.c` adds one more send between the envmap
  and the mirror. A race's frame now goes to the GPU after the envmap,
  the mirror, the models and the top screen's HUD, and before
  `C3D_FrameEnd`.
  - **Expected at the fire:** about 4.4 + 50 ms a frame, where it was
    23 + 50, so about 18 FPS from 13.8. Not measured on the device.
  - **To go back:** "GpuSends 0" in nfshp2_config.txt.
- **Why the pixels are the same:**
  - the parts run in order on the one GX queue;
  - each clear still runs before the draws to its own target;
  - each send flushes the linear heap after its split (04aa510).

  A mid-frame end of the queue only runs citro3d's onQueueFinish with
  no swap pending and no GPU clock started. The GPU clock starts at
  `C3D_FrameEnd`.
- **The profiler.** citro3d's "gpu" time on the frame line now counts
  only what the GPU has left after `C3D_FrameEnd`. The frame rate and
  the GPU wait are the measures (`frame-profiler.md`).
- **On Azahar** (AC power, speed 100%). The fire's config (track 11,
  2 laps, 3 AI) and `nfshp2_warp.txt` ("6 -476 88 -66.6 22380 20")

  - The race ran whole, with no hang, at 20 to 30 FPS on Azahar's CPU.

  - The shots at the fire (`$TEMP\nfshp2_fire57`) match Session 87's

## Session 89 -- TASKS 53, the debug menu (designed, no code yet)

The session picked up TASKS 53 after Session 88. It ended at the
user's word ("Stop work, write up HANDOFF.MD etc."). Nothing in `3DS
Files/source` was changed. The only modified file in the tree is
`tools/run_azahar_coprace.ps1`, and only its line endings, from before
this session. The design below is settled and ready to write.

### What the user asked for (2026-10-12, verbatim)

"implement a custom debug menu you enable by pressing L + R and up on
the D-Pad at the same time on the main menu, or by setting "DebugMenu
1" in the config document. It will be a custom debug menu panel on the
main menu navigation. When you go into it, it lets you do things like
just jump into custom tracks or wtv with custom settings, unlock all,
give yourself NFS points, etc."

### Retail's own debug menu (not reused)

- INGAMEB has a "Debug Menu" screen, `d4742cd7`, with 19 objects.
  Its rows are MENUITEM_1..11 at x 176, in FONT_HUD (`a2d444f6`) at
  scale 0.6.
- Its rows hold only 19 to 64 characters each, and they are in-race
  toggles: finish position, collisions, mirror, env mapping, super
  easy AI.
- Its code is PauseDebugMenu:
  - the constructor, `0x00173e30`;
  - MenuCallback, `0x001740c0`;
  - OnMenuItemScroll, `0x00174198`;
  - the callback, `0x00174590`.

  The decompile is in this session's scratchpad (`dbgmenu.c`). Rerun
  `DecompileByAddr.java` with `DECOMPILE_ADDRS=00173e30,...` (no `0x`)
  to get it again.
- `pausemenu.c`'s `kPauseDebugMenuScreen` ("Debug Menu") is never
  reached on the retail disc. Leave that name free.

### The plan

**1. FRONTB's Flailer chunk rebuilt at boot**, in a new
`debugmenu.c`/`.h`.

- **The call.** `debugmenu_patch_frontend(data, len, &outLen)` runs
  in `main.c`'s `addBundle` for FRONTB only. It runs after
  `uirender_add_bundle` and before `flailer_add_project`.
- **The swap.** It does `bui_close(&b->ui)`, then
  `bui_open(&b->ui, newBuf, 0, newLen)`.
- **Keeping the buffer.** Add a `uint8_t* uiData` to `UIBundle`
  (`uirender.h`) to hold the new buffer, and free it in
  `uirender_free`. The bundle's own `data` stays as it is, so the
  textures, fonts and `frontres_load` don't change.
- **Why rebuild the bytes** rather than insert into the BUI's object
  table: `flailer_object_index` (`flailer.c:95`) binary-searches the
  payload addresses, so they must rise in file order. A rebuilt chunk
  keeps that true.
- **The chunk format** (`bchunk.c`) is `[u32 type][u32 size][payload]`,
  little-endian, with no alignment. Every object size is a multiple of
  4. `flailer_add_project` needs 4-aligned payloads, and a malloc'd
  buffer gives that.
- **The writer.** Write each container's header with size 0, then
  patch the size once its children are written. Keep offsets, not
  pointers, because `realloc` can move the buffer.
- **What gets copied.** The project chunk (`0x00010213`) and every
  screen container (`0x80010201`) go across in order. Padding chunks
  (`0/0`) can be dropped.
- **Retail object fields**, as offsets from the payload:
  - NameHash +8, GroupHash +12, Name[24] +16;
  - ObjectType +40, Visibility +41 (0 invisible, 1 visible), Z +42,
    DirtyFlag +43;
  - X +48, Y +52, ScaleX +56, ScaleY +60.
- **Text fields:** FontHash +80, MaxChars +84, Format +88, Color +92,
  LanguageID +96, and String at +100. The payload is
  100 + roundup4(room).
  - To make a text's room bigger, copy its first 100 bytes, set
    MaxChars to the new room, and copy the old string.
  - `flailertext_set_string` writes up to MaxChars, so MaxChars must
    not be more than the chunk has.
- **The screen definition** (`0x00010203`, 40 bytes): NameHash +8,
  CallbackHash +12, HelpMenuHash +16 (set it to 0 on the copy),
  ResX/ResY +24, NumObjects (u16) +28.

**2. The main menu's 4th item.** Two objects are added to the end of
NEW_MAIN_MENU, and its NumObjects goes up by 2.

- **The label** is a copy of MENUITEM_3, at (152, 236): 55 below
  Options, as 1, 2 and 3 are 55 apart. It has room 16, LanguageID 0,
  string "Debug Menu", and MENUITEM_3's GroupHash, so it slides in with
  the others.
- **The mask** is a copy of MI_3_MASK, at (141, 238).
- **Hidden until revealed.** Both start invisible, under dummy hashes:
  `PORT_DEBUG_ITEM` `0xd988c438` and `PORT_DEBUG_MASK` `0xd98aa6b5`.
  - bmenu only finds MENUITEM_n by hash, and bsel only finds the
    masks by hash, so neither sees the item until then.
  - The main menu's ctor already passes MI_4_MASK in
    `kMainMenuMasks[5]`.
- **The reveal** (`debugmenu_reveal`) writes MENUITEM_4 (`0x52e039f6`)
  and MI_4_MASK (`0x75345d33`) into +8 of each and makes both visible.
  `bui_find_object` and `flailer_find_object` read +8 every time, so
  nothing is cached.
- **The layout fits.** The dark filler `aa5d7d3f` at (141, 228),
  scale 32 x 7.06, covers y 228 to 341, so the new row sits on it.
- **"DebugMenu 1"** reveals the item at boot, straight after the patch.
  - Add `ConfigDebugMenu` to `configitems.c`'s table (that file is
    CRLF).
  - Put its comment in `configitems.h` (LF), next to `ConfigForceChopper`.
- **The chord**, in `main.c`'s `flowInput`:
  - The test: `g_flow.screen->callback == bgf_new_main_menu_callback`,
    with `hidKeysHeld()` having both KEY_L and KEY_R, and KEY_DUP in
    `kDown`.
  - The action: reveal, then `fesound_play(30, NULL)` (the Easter
    egg's sound), and take KEY_DUP out of `flowDown`.
  - Then `bgf_change_to_screen(&g_flow, "New Main Menu", 0)`. It is

    MENUITEM_4, then ACTIVATE and enterScreen.
  - Last, `bmenu_set_active_item(&g_boot.menu, 0x52e039f6)` to land on

  - L and R are not in `kBinds`, so the menu never hears them.
- **`gameflow.c`** (`mainMenuHighlight`, `mainMenuEvent`): a
  MENUITEM_4 case, marked as the port's own.
  - **HIGHLIGHT:** the brackets to MI_4_MASK, and a literal blurb

  - Add `BGF_ITEM_MENUITEM_4 0x52e039f6u` and
    `BGF_DEBUG_MENU_NAME "Port Debug Menu"` to `gameflow.h`.
  - Run `bootflow_check.py` after. It runs retail's main menu, and
    none of its scenarios sends MENUITEM_4.

**3. The debug screen.** "Port Debug Menu" uses hash `0xd98ab71e`,
which is `bhash("PORT_DEBUG_MENU")`. It is a new screen container at
the end of FRONTB's project. It copies Be The Cop Setup (`d1eadbca`,

- **What d1eadbca has:**

- **Rooms made bigger:** labels to 24, values to 40, and the title to

- **Registering it.** Add it to `kScreens[]` with
  `debugmenu_callback`. Also teach `tools/screen_registry.py

**4. The callback.** It shows 7 slots over a longer list, and handles
scrolling itself.

- **Moving.**
  - bmenu sends PAD_UP and PAD_DOWN to the callback first, and a
    nonzero `data->param` eats them (`bmenu.c:250`). So at the edges
    the callback scrolls, or wraps and calls
    `bmenu_set_active_item`.
  - A consumed move plays no sound, so call
    `fesound_play(BSND_MENU_UP/DOWN, NULL)` directly.
  - For PAD_LEFT and PAD_RIGHT, set `data->noise`; bmenu plays it
    after the callback.
- **On HIGHLIGHT:**
  - every mask is visible except the current slot's (IndicatorMode 1's
    look);
  - the brackets go to the mask's box (under: bottom - 3, over:
    top - 6);
  - the left and right arrows go to the row's y + 4, shown only on
    rows with a value;
  - the scroll arrows show when there are rows above or below;
  - the blurb gets the row's help line.
- **Setting text:** `flailer_printf(DEBUGMENU_SCREEN, obj, ...)` and
  `flailer_set_visibility(..., FLAILER_OBJECT_VISIBLE/INVISIBLE)`.
  `printf` caps at 128 characters and sets LanguageID 0.
- **Avoid apostrophes.** The fonts may not have one, so the mode is
  "Be The Cop", not "You're The Cop".
- **The rows:**

  | Row | What it does |
  |---|---|
  | Start Race | A starts the race |
  | Mode | Hot Pursuit (express, cops on), Single Race (express, cops off), or Be The Cop |
  | Track | Every TrackNumber with `track_get_info`. Be The Cop leaves out Point2Point, as `isTrackUnavailable` does. The name is `gFredTranslateFn(TrackLanguageID)`, or ReverseTrackLanguageID when backwards, else `ti->Name`. The time of day comes from `kTODLang = {0xd6e0, 0xd6e1, 0xd6e2, 0xd6e3, 0xd70a}` (`btracksel.c:90`) when TimeOfDay != 0. |
  | Direction | Forwards or backwards |
  | Car | Types 0..63 whose UsageType is RACING, or COP for Be The Cop, with a GeometryFilename and skins (`fredrace.c`'s `next_car`). The name is `pCarSpecs->FullName` translated, else CarTypeName. |
  | Colour | `cartypeinfo_get_skin_number(ct, i)`, with the PrettyName from `cartypeinfo_get_skin_info` |
  | Opponents | Defaults: Hot Pursuit 3, Single Race 7, Be The Cop 4. The most is 7. |
  | Laps | 1 to 10. Point2Point is 1, and Be The Cop has none. |
  | Traffic | None, Light, Medium or Heavy: 0, 0.33, 0.667 or 1.0 |
  | Difficulty | 0, 1 or 2: OpponentStrength and CopStrength |
  | Gearbox | TransmissionType |
  | Unlock Everything | See below |
  | Lock Everything | See below |
  | NFS Points | Shown with `nfs_format_points`. Left and right change it by 10,000; A adds 100,000. The points' rewards come at the end of the next race, as retail's do. |

- **Unlock Everything:**
  - `unlock_events()` (retail's UnlockEvents, which nothing calls);
  - every `TaskRewardStates[10]` and `PointsRewardStates[18]` set to 1;
  - `fred_make_challenge_cars_available(&Fred)`.

  It is kept only if the user saves (Options' Save/Load, or the
  autosave after a race).
- **Lock Everything:** `lock_events()`, the states back to 0, and

- **Start Race in Hot Pursuit or Single Race** is `start_quick_race`
  (`quickrace.c`) with the choices in it:
  - `Fred.MainMenuOpts[1] = cops`;
  - GameType 2, one player;

  - NumAICars, with the player at NumAICars + 1;
  - the cops' fields as in `start_quick_race`;
  - the traffic, the difficulty, RaceType 1 and the laps.

  Then:
  - `fred_make_challenge_cars_available`;
  - `fpi_set_car_availability(p0, CAR_STATUS_AVAILABLE, type, -1, 1)`;
  - `fpi_assign_car_of_type(p0, 2, type, skin, 0)`;
  - the transmission;

  - start the race through a hook that does `fred_start_race(&Fred)`

### The sound

- **The first fix** paused every playing ndsp channel around
  `swkbdInputText`. The user still heard it go wrong.
- **Why.** Azahar had no DSP sleep or wake in its log. Its keyboard is
  a Qt dialog, and `QtKeyboard::Execute` waits on it with a
  BlockingQueuedConnection, so the whole emulated console stops while
  it is open. Its audio stretcher (`TimeStretcher::Process`: tempo from
  input over output, a 0.712 s low-pass, a floor of 0.05) is fed
  nothing and slows to 5%. A simulation of its code
  (`tools/azahar_stretch_sim.py`, 10 s frozen) has the tempo at 1.32x at
  1.5 s, 0.88x at 2.8 s, and within 5% of normal by 3.5 s.
- **The fix.** The channels are paused and the master volume set to 0.
  Afterwards, on a 3DS, the channels go on at once and the volume fades
  in over 250 ms. On Azahar they wait 3.5 s first, so the swing is over
  silence. `svcGetSystemInfo(0x20000, 0)` is Azahar's EMULATOR_ID (2;
  Citra 1), and an error on a 3DS. Nothing else in the port sets the
  master volume.
- **On a 3DS**, libctru's `aptLaunchLibraryApplet` calls ONSUSPEND, the
  DSP sleeps (ndsp's `ndspFinalize(true)`), and on wake
  `ndspInitialize(true)` sends every channel again. Already queued
  waves are not sent again, so the pause beforehand is the safe side.
  Not yet heard on the device.

## Session 92, continued -- 51b, the renderer reads the env flag (done)

- **The fault.** Retail's RenderStrips (`0x0010dd58`) reads each
  strip's Flags as it draws. The port bakes a solid's strips into
  batches of one texture, flags and material (`georender.c`), and
  trackview's `strip_flags` started from the batch's baked flags. A
  window that CarDamage broke kept its environment map.
- **The fix.**
  - `GeoBatch.strip` keeps the batch's first strip.
  - `geometry.c`'s `geo_strip_flags(solid, index, otherwise)` reads that
    strip's Flags (`0x0e`) from the solid's entry table as it is now.
  - `strip_flags` takes the GeoSolid and starts from it.
  - A car's solids are opened over the engine's own `StripEntryTable`
    (`find_other`'s `geo_open_in_place`), which
    `esolid_set_environment_mapping` writes. Every strip of a batch has
    its texture, and SetEnvironmentMapping changes every strip of a
    texture, so one strip speaks for the batch.
- **Checks.** The build is clean, and `loadertable_check` already shows
  the strips' flags (`sf`) changing on the duplicated solids. On Azahar
  (AC power, CPU 4%), `run_azahar_race.ps1 -HoldKeys 65` ran 66 s at 30
  FPS and Speed 100%, and the car draws as it did. The Speedster's
  hardtop leaves only a small rear window, so no shot shows the map go.
- **Next.** 51c, the vertices: DamageVertexFunction's dents, colours
  and scuffs, through `gBodyDamageVertexWalkFn`, on meshes that live
  on the GPU.

## Session 95 -- 37a, the local wireless link (done)

`docs/formats/wireless.md` has the whole of it; this is the short form.
TASKS 37's design (lockstep) is in TASKS.md, from Session 94.

### What is where

- `wlproto.c`/`.h` (new): the protocol, free of `<3ds.h>`. A 7-byte
  header with a CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE; reliable messages (15-bit numbers,
  32 in flight, 100 ms resends, acks on every packet, early ones held);
  unreliable ones for the next packet only; keepalives every 100 ms, and
  a 3 s timeout.
- `wireless.c`/`.h` (new): wlproto on UDS. Host, scan, join, leave, and
  the status (the host takes the first client and blocks the rest).
  The beacon's appdata is `NHP2`, the version, a length and the
  caller's bytes.
- `wirelesstest.c`/`.h` (new): the soak, run from `main.c` in place of
  the game when `WirelessTest` is 1 (host) or 2 (join).
  `WirelessTestSeconds` is how long it sends (`configitems.c`/`.h`).
- `meta/app.rsf`: `nwm::UDS`, and the nwm module in Dependency.
- `tools/wlproto_check.py`, `tools/src/wlproto_test.c` (new): two links
  over a simulated channel (drops, repeats, delays, cuts, reader
  stalls, crafted and random bad packets).
- `tools/run_azahar_wireless.ps1` (new): the room, two portable Azahar
  copies, Direct Connect through UI Automation, and both logs read.

### What bit

- **The first mutation pass left 8 survivors.** The harness took the
  unacked count from the link itself, so it now does its own arithmetic.
  take() had two delivery paths that overlapped, so every reliable
  message now goes through `held[]`. A length check was redundant and
  is gone. Reader stalls had no reordering, and nothing checked that a
  full read left nothing deliverable held. Both are covered now, and
  two equivalents are named.
- **Azahar's room nickname is the console's user name.** The Direct
  Connect dialog shows it read-only, and every fresh copy is "AZAHAR".
  A room takes one member of a name, as it does of a console ID. The
  Configure dialog shows no children to UI Automation (it is modal, and
  the Invoke that opens it times out). So the script writes the name
  into block 0x000A0000 of each copy's config savegame, which Azahar
  makes on its first start.

## Session 95, continued -- 37a, the link for up to 8 consoles

The user asked for as many consoles as Download Play takes, up to 8, a
race's grid (2026-10-14). Download Play does take 8: a UDS network has
up to 16 nodes (`UDS_MAXNODES`), DLP's own network is made with
max_nodes = its max clients + 1, and Mario Kart 7 races 8 over Download
Play. Each console still has the game and the retail files on its own
card. Sending the game itself over the air is a separate thing, not
asked for.

### What changed

- `wireless.c`/`.h`: a star of up to `WIRELESS_MAX_CONSOLES` (8). The
  host has a peer for each client (its node, name, alive and its own
  `WlLink`), sends to each by `udsSendTo(node)`, and stays open until
  `wireless_set_open(0)`. Late nodes, and nodes that come once it is
  full, are ejected. A client that goes quiet is ejected, and
  `goneMask` stops it being taken again until the mask shows it gone.
  A lost peer keeps its place (`alive` 0); `wireless_forget_lost`
  compacts the list. `wireless_link()` and the stats' `peer` are gone,
  as nothing else used them.
- The scan logs `wireless: scan sees N network(s): ...` each time what
  it sees changes, with the skipped ones counted as not the port's or
  full.
- `wirelesstest.c`/`.h`: a soak per link. `WirelessTestConsoles` (2 to
  8; `configitems.c`/`.h`, passed in by `main.c`) is how many the host
  waits for, itself among them, before it closes. It passes when every
  link has, and fails unless the network held all of them at once.
- `tools/run_azahar_wireless.ps1 -Consoles N` (2 to 8): copies A to H,
  nicknames `hp2host` and `hp2join1` to `hp2join7`, a room of N + 2
  places, and a deadline of `-Seconds` + 60 + 20 a console.

### What bit

- **The room is not capped at 4.** The user saw 4/6 in the 4-console
  run, and the 6 was the script's `--max_members`. The room server has
  no limit of its own, and 5 and 8 copies took part.
- **The first 8-console run never held 8 at once,** and passed anyway.
  The script joins the copies to the room one at a time, so G and H
  joined after B and C had finished their 30 s and left. Azahar's
  source showed no cap at 6 either: its beacon always carries max_nodes
  entries, and the host turns a join away only when total == max. The
  soak now fails a run that never held them all, and the 8-console run
  is 60 s.
- With 8, the 150 s deadline ran out before the last ones finished, so
  it grows with the count now.

ndsp, and main.c gave the sound no driver (`sound_init`'s NULL, as it

  pitch and patch volume of 0, and no chained part. Everything else
  stops at no voice already; the bSound's own calls stop at status 0.

  ("nodriver", the port's boot with NULL), 212 ops over samples on their

## Session 100 -- 37d, the lockstep race (finished in Session 101)

The user asked to wrap up partway through 37d. Nothing of 37d is

modified files git status always shows (`git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol
--stat` lists the real ones). The user also asked this session for

after 1 min 30 s its car goes to the CPU); both are written into

to be Download Play: it is multi-card over UDS, as Download Play cannot
send 2,291 MB.

### Done and checked on the host: the lockstep core

- `3DS Files/source/netstep.c`/`.h` (new): every console runs both
  players' race, frame by frame, on the same inputs. Each frame's record
  carries every live place's pad and the host's quantised step `q`. The
  input delay is NETSTEP_DELAY, 3 frames; frames 0 to 2 are built
  locally, q 120 and every pad at rest. A pad is 8 bytes: the DS2
  buffer's bytes 2 to 7 and a u16 of the flow's presses (`menu`).
  PADS (0x16, place to host) and FRAMES (0x17, host to all) are
  unreliable, with a 15-byte header, each repeating what the other side
  still needs, resent every 16 ms. The link's own timeout comes back
  (setPatience(0)) once D + 30 frames are built. Each side keeps a ring
  of the world's checksums and compares a frame once both have it. API:
  netstep_bind, init, start, stop, on, put, poll, current, done, frame,
  rest. Place p's pad is port p's (`r->pad[port]`).
- `tools/src/netstep_test.c`, `tools/netstep_check.py` (new): 20
  scenarios, faults 0, among them a slow link, one slower than the
  delay, the client's GO late, a checksum differing with the host
  slower, and netrace's messages on the same link. `--mutate`: 107
  mutations, 104 caught, 3 equivalent (named in the check).

  hudrender's tickets and places, warp, cardamageabove and rendercars.

### Not applied yet: main.c

`tools/main_lockstep_37d.py` holds main.c's half as exact replacements.
A dry run found every one of them in main.c as it stands. It has not
been run, and main.c is unchanged. It adds:

- `gJoypadRead = joypadRead`: in a lockstep frame each port reads its
  place's pad from the record (`joyhid_from_wire`), else joyhid_read.
- `netRaceGoRacing` as netrace's goRacing: the racing places' mask, then
  netstep_start, then port 0's last ring entry set to a pad at rest, so
  the first frame's edges are the same on every console. It logs the
  clocks at GO, then calls trackflow_go_racing.
- `lockFrame`, at the loop's top. It measures the step, puts this
  console's pad and q with the flow's presses since the last begin, and
  waits up to LOCK_SPIN_MS (8) for the record, pumping the link. A
  record later than that leaves the loop drawing without stepping; the
  next loop asks again. On its record's arrival it sets the frame's
  step from `q`.
- The clocks advance only after a lockstep frame ran (`g_lockRan`).
  bgf_frame, raceFrame, uiTimer and the flow's presses run only on a
  frame that steps; the presses are the record's, each place's on its
  port (`lockFlowInput`).
- `flowInput(kDown, port)` and the screen filter ports: retail's
  SetScreenFilterPort (0x0016d4c8), bound as gSetScreenFilterPortFn. The
  menu takes the port when made; START and BACK filter on it.
- `netstep_done(world checksum)` after each frame. netstep_stop runs
  once the coordinator is gone, but only after a lockstep frame ran with
  it up (`g_lockRaced`, added in the review).
- `PlayerNetLocal` from netrace's place once its stage reaches
  NR_LOADING (place 1 is player 1, every other place player 0), back to
  -1 once the coordinator is gone, and `eViewShowOne` with it.
- The bottom screen's HUD features and track map, the sound's players
  and joyhid's race layout read the player shown.

The review also added a forward declaration of flowInput, as joypadRead
and lockFlowInput sit above it.

## Session 105, continued -- TASKS 65, the sends' flush by the kernel

The user's other report from 4988138: "there was a minor FPS slowdown
too at one point, locate that and fix it too". The log's one slow
second is world 186 s on lap 1 (`3DS Files/nfshp2_debug.txt` lines
~6902 to 6936): 23.1, 10.7, then 20.2 FPS.

### What the log shows

- In the 10.7 FPS second, mirror 17.3, sky 13.0, models 15.8 and
  bottom 13.9 ms: each about 10 ms over the seconds either side. Every
  other stage was as before (envmap 2.9, scenery 1.5, cars 3.2, hud
  0.9, submit 0.3), and so were the counts (models, words, flares,
  effects, sprites).
- Those four are the stages a mid-frame send ends: the envmap's in
  mirror, the mirror's in sky, the models' own, the top screen's in
  bottom. Submit holds the last send and `C3D_FrameEnd`'s own flush and
  stayed at 0.3 ms.
- The same corner on lap 2 ran at its usual rate. The chopper was 50 m
  off (plan 4), but it flies as close elsewhere with no dip.
- A send's flush was `GSPGPU_FlushDataCache`: a request to GSP's thread
  on the system core, which calls `svcFlushProcessDataCache` on the
  range for us. GSP slow to answer for 3 s fits; it is not proven.
- Ruled out on the way: a queued `GX_FlushCacheRegions` (libctru: "This
  command cannot be queued in a GX command queue"; the queue counts
  interrupts, and a flush raises none). citro3d's `C3D_FrameEnd` makes
  the same synchronous GSP request (disassembled `libcitro3dd.a`).

### What changed

- `hangwatch.c`: `flush_heap`, the sends' flush. The CIA calls
  `svcFlushProcessDataCache(CUR_PROCESS_HANDLE, heap, size)` itself. A
  3DSX from a homebrew launcher (`envIsHomebrew`) asks GSP, since its
  host title might not allow the call and a call not allowed ends the
  app. A failed call goes back to GSP for good. The first send logs
  which ("gpu sends: the linear heap flushed by the kernel").
- Each send is timed, the flush and the queue apart: `frameprof`'s new
  `sends:` line after the cars' (`sends: 5.0 a frame; flush .., queue
  .., worst ..`).
- `app.rsf`: `FlushProcessDataCache: 84` in SystemCallAccess.
- `configitems`: "KernelFlush" (1); "KernelFlush 0" asks GSP in the CIA.
- `docs/formats/frame-profiler.md`, "The sends"; `draw-cuts.md` and
  `hangwatch.h` point to it. TASKS 65 has the findings; it stays open
  for the next device log.

- tools/build_cia.ps1: built, relocations OK, 2 shaders each output
  component written once.
- The built CIA's exheader (scratchpad `cia_svcs.py`): 53 calls in both

(this), 37f-2 a rematch (Restart Race, Next Race), 37f-3 one player
leaving mid-race.

### The design

- Every console runs the same flow on the same pads, so all of them
  leave lockstep after the same frame: the one that asks for the end's
  save (Quit or Next Race after the results; `endGameAutosaveNow` sets
  `g_lockEnd`), or the one the pause's Quit Race unloads the race in
  (the coordinator gone after it was up). From the next frame each
  console's save is its own, on its own card, with its own pad.
- The end on the link: every message carries `stopAt`, the frames its
  sender ran before its stop (the header is 19 bytes now). The host
  serves its last records until each client has said it stopped, is
  gone, or 10 s have passed (`NETSTEP_DRAIN_MS`). A client says its
  stop 30 times, 16 ms apart, and reads nothing more. Neither reads past
  a message that is not the race's (`wl_link_peek`): it is the lobby's.
  Should two consoles ever part, a client stopping first has left the
  host's race, and a client still on past the host's last frame goes
  on alone and says that as its stop.
- `netrace_end`: `NR_RACING` to `NR_OFF`, netrace's long patience on
  the link again (each console saves, unloads and loads the frontend in
  its own time), and the lobby next (`lobby_back_next`).
- The frontend's relaunch pops to the lobby, not the main menu:
  `gameflow.c`'s new `raceReturn` hook names it while netrace is on.
- The lobby, back from the race with the link up: the host's list open
  again, each client awaited and sent `LOBBY_MSG_BACK` (0x18), listed
  once its own comes, Start once none is awaited; a client sends its
  own and waits for the next Start. Once every other console still on
  is back, each gives the link its own timeout again ("every console
  back"). A client gone while awaited loses its place to the next, as
  the peers do.

  both reads; `NETSTEP_TELLS`, `NETSTEP_DRAIN_MS`.

## Session 107 -- 37f-2, a rematch in a wireless race

The user's standing word: continue from the last session and never
stop until the port is at 100%, one task at a time. The session ran
over two sittings (2026-10-15, the night's stop and the morning). Late
in it the user said "Stop Azahar testing" (the Next Race run was
stopped and every copy closed), then "Once 37f-2 is committed fully,
stop working for now". So 37f-2 is committed with Next Race and
Restart Event checked by the harness only, and the work stops here.

### The design

- `netrace_end` no longer goes to `NR_OFF`: a new stage `NR_ENDED`
  waits for what comes next. Once the flow is at
  `BGF_LOADING_FRONTEND` or `BGF_IN_FRONTEND` netrace goes off
  ("netrace: off, the frontend next"); the lobby's return was already
  decided at the race's start by `raceReturn`.
- The event's next race (Next Race; Restart Event): `netrace_hold`
  takes `NR_ENDED` as well as `NR_LOADING`, counts `round` and says
  "netrace: race N loaded", and holds again. A client's `LOADED` now
  goes from `netrace_frame`'s `NR_HOLD` case (`saidLoaded`), not from
  `netrace_hold`.
- `NetRaceNet.busy` (`netstep_ending` in `main.c`): `netrace_frame`
  returns at once while the last race's end is still on the link. So
  a client's stop messages go before its `LOADED`, and the host's last
  frames go before its `GO`; otherwise the next race's netstep would
  read the old `stopAt` as a stop.
- Leftovers of the last race (the host's last frames, a client's
  stops) are read and dropped in `NR_HOLD`: `clientRead` reads only
  between `NR_OFF` and `NR_RACING`, and `hostRead` the same.
- Restart Race from the pause resets the race in place with the
  coordinator kept, and stays in lockstep with nothing new (seen on
  two Azahars, below).
- `main.c`:
  - `fedSetupNextRace` keeps `PlayerSettings[0]` as raced when netrace
    is on (the event's next race would otherwise differ per console).
  - `raceEventRestart` calls `netRaceGrid()` after `raceevent_restart`
    when netrace is on: CPU racers first, the two players at cpu+1 and
    cpu+2, the humans in AI places (driver 100+k) at cpu+3+k, then
    `fred_calculate_starting_positions`.
  - `netShownPlayer()`: a knocked-out player's console shows the other
    player (`PlayerNetLocal`). Lap Knockout (GameType 4) is the race
    event's mode for Next Race and Restart Event; the elimination is
    between races.
  - `lockTestFinish()` and the config item `WirelessTestFinish n`
    (off by default): finishes a wireless race on lockstep frame n on
    every console (`racecoordinator_the_race_has_finished`), so an
    Azahar run can reach the results and Next Race. The gas alone does
    not finish a race.

### Restart Race's hang: strict aliasing

The first Restart Race runs on two Azahars passed (seed ec5fd1d5, 18
logged frames' parts the same on both), but the restart could hang in
the world's update: WorldObjectList went round a NULL node. Temporary
DIAG lines (removed since) showed two smokeables and 237 virgins still
alive and on WorldObjectList at the restart, though their bodies were
off CollisionBodyList and their pool freed.

The cause was GCC's strict aliasing at -O3, not the port's logic:
`delete_smokeable_collision_bodies` and the far-away delete moved the
bodies onto a list whose head was a bare `CollisionBodyNode` on the
stack, then emptied it through `CollisionBody*` links. To GCC a write
through a CollisionBody could never touch an 8-byte node, so the head
read as empty and the whole destroy loop was dropped. Every smokeable
and virgin leaked at each race end and far-away delete. Once the head
was a whole `CollisionBody`, `destroy_list`'s first push onto
`CollisionBodyList` (a node reached as the list's end, the same way)
used a head read before the write, and
`collisionbody_update_max_width` walked a broken list.

The fix:
- `smokeable.c`: the list on the stack is a whole `CollisionBody`
  (`move_to_list`, `destroy_list` take it), as the image's
  bTList<CollisionBody> is reached.
- `3DS Files/Makefile`: `-fno-strict-aliasing`, for the whole class
  (the port reaches other lists' heads through their items' types).
  A full rebuild; the ELF's producer string has the flag.
- With it, Restart Race passed on seed 0ecec47b, no unmapped reads in
  either Azahar's log. The race's CPU stages averaged 24.14 ms on A
  and 24.51 on B, against 25.21 and 25.03 under strict aliasing: no
  cost, if anything a little faster.
- On the device this should also free the race's props at every race
  end and far-away delete; before, the pool could fill and props stop
  converting. Not seen on hardware yet, nor any FPS change.

### What changed

- `netrace.c/h`: `NR_ENDED`, `round`, `saidLoaded`, `NetRaceNet.busy`,
  the hold for the next race, the reads' guards.
- `main.c`: `netrace_end`'s stage, `busy` from `netstep_ending`,
  `fedSetupNextRace`'s raced player, `netRaceGrid` after
  `raceevent_restart`, `netShownPlayer`, `lockTestFinish`.
- `configitems.c/h`: `WirelessTestFinish n` (off by default).
- `smokeable.c`, `3DS Files/Makefile`: the strict-aliasing fix.
- `tools/src/netrace_test.c`, `tools/netrace_check.py`: eight new
  scenarios, the busy period, the new and moved mutations.
- `tools/smokeable_check.py`: the list mutations' texts for the whole
  CollisionBody head.
- `tools/run_azahar_lobby.ps1`: `-Restart`, `-NextRace`, `-Finish`.
- Docs: `netrace.md`, `netstep.md`, `lobby.md`, `end-game.md`,
  `smokeable.md`, `collision-body.md`.

## Session 109 -- the second race's track, the heap's top, the driver piece

The user, on a screenshot of race 2 with the HUD and no track drawn:
"Well that's a problem". They asked that once 37f-2's fixes are done,
the icon, banner and sound become Hot Pursuit 2's before 37f-3.

### Race 2 with no track

B's log had "race: track not attached: out of memory for the tables".
Two causes:

- The race's view makes its tables in one calloc as the track's load
  ends, with the heap at its fullest, and 3.1 MB of it was the meshes'
  `GeoBatch[GEO_MAX_BATCHES]` (1,536 of a TrackSolid's 1,612 bytes, 2,048
  TrackSolids). Now a mesh's batches are in its vertex block on the
  linear heap, as many as the solid has (`geobake.c`, `geobake.h`).
  geobake_check: 44 files, 518 solids, faults 0.
- The main loop's attach ran after raceFrame's coordinator tick, which
  on Next Race runs the unload's Begin and the next load's Begin. The
  attach found the next TRACKB only begun, failed in geo_open and freed
  its 3.6 MB of tables in the middle of the load. It now waits while
  `pRaceCoordinator` is NULL, as the unload's Begin leaves it
  (`track-flow.md`, "The race's view").

### The heap's top

A run of B stopped before race 2 on `bMalloc` of
`TRACKS\TEX11LOCATION.BIN`: 21 MB of the heap free and no 5 MB of it
whole. Retail's bMalloc takes pool bit 8 from the top of its bank: a
packed copy is read there and freed once expanded below, and so are
pool 72's reads (USE_TEMPORARY_MEMORY, freed once loaded). With one
malloc heap and no top those left holes of megabytes between the blocks
kept.

- `bmem.c/h`: hooks for the top (`gBMemTopAllocFn`, `gBMemTopFreeFn`),
  for names (`gBMemNoteFn`, `gBMemForgetFn`) and for a failed bMalloc
  (`gBMemFailFn`).
- `main.c`: bMallocTop takes the top from the linear heap, never its
  last 8 MB (a block that would comes from malloc); bFreeTop knows one
  by its address. bMallocFailed writes the heap's map to stderr before
  the abort.
- `heapmap.c/h` (new): a walk of newlib's malloc heap (its free chunks,
  the runs in use between them, named when bMalloc made them) and the
  names of bMalloc's blocks of 64 KB or more. `heapmap_named` lists the
  named blocks in an address range: the race's attach logs the top's
  blocks in the linear heap and their bytes.
- That log showed the top holding 8.8 MB of the linear heap through the
  race: `TRACKS\TRACKB11.LZC`, the whole bundle. The card holds the
  tracks' TRACKB expanded, as .BUN (`bfile.c` reads a missing .LZC from
  its .BUN), so the "packed copy" is the bundle and never freed, and the
  race's prepare left out 52 to 61 textures (6 before). `bfile.c`'s
  `bFileIsExpanded` says when a .LZC is read from its .BUN, and the
  ResourceFile constructor asks for the top only when the file is
  packed on the card (`resource-file.md`). resource_check: 10
  scenarios, 0 differ (its file system holds files as named, so the
  expanded case is the port's alone); texturestream_check and
  sedwedge_check 0 differ.

### The driver piece

Run 5 split at frame 1809 in the time and players parts: slot 0 alone,
the host's car, which the AI drives after the finish
(`race_finish_car`), in every CarState piece but rel and its modes the
same. What the AI chose went into the CarState the frame it drove, so
the pieces only say when. lockhash's cars have a tenth piece, the
driver: the CarDriver's Steering to NitroFlag and its DriveTarget's

part. `run_azahar_lobby.ps1` names, for each slot that differs, the
first frame of the window where its word differed. lockhash_check:
total faults 0; `--mutate` 105, 101 caught, 4 equivalent.

## Session 110 -- Hot Pursuit 2's banner, banner sound and icon (done)

The user, at the end of Session 108: "change the icon, banner and sound

banner can be a 3D logo that spins, with any assets it needs in the

nothing with their NAND, ever: they test the CIA on their own 3DS.

### What the HOME Menu reads

bannertool's `makebanner -ci banner.cgfx -a banner.wav` makes the CBMD:
the CGFX LZ11-packed at 0x88, then a CWAV (PCM16). The HOME Menu's
rules, from 3dbrew and the banners people make:

- The model and its animation are both named `COMMON`.
- RGBA8 textures do not show, so both here are RGBA5551, ordered-dithered
  (Bayer 4x4) before the 5-bit cut.
- The whole CGFX stays under 0x80000 bytes.
- The camera is at (0, 1, 44.786) with a 30-degree field of view, which
  is 40 x 24 units at z = 0.
- The sound is about 3 s at most.

The writer follows pycgfx's layout (read in the browser only, nothing
of it run): self-relative pointers, the DATA block, each node's
children together in field order and then theirs, the string table,
and IMAG with textures 128-aligned. The DICTs are Patricia trees, and
the port of the builder matched all 8 of a template banner's.

### tools/make_banner.py

- Letters: `NFS_LOGO_ALPHA` (GLOBAL/GLOBALB.BUN), its chrome letters
  and the blue HOT PURSUIT 2 band cut from the glow around them by
  alpha, brightness and blue (15 outlines). Marched, simplified and
  extruded 1 unit deep, 30 units wide: 1,090 wall quads on a steel
  strip, shaded from the blurred alpha's gradient so the steps of the
  outline do not stripe. The front cap is the logo, the back a dark
  copy. One edge of all of them fails the inside check.
- Background: a quad behind at z = -16, a night gradient with the blue
  and red of the logo's light bar, streaks and a vignette, and the
  logo's glow with the letters filled in.
- Spin: 240 frames. The logo rests, turns once (0 to 2 pi, eased,
  frames 60 to 150) and rests again; one CANM (rot_y only, linear keys
  every 3 frames).
- Materials: each with its own hashes, so the HOME Menu's renderer does
  not skip one's state for the other; no culling; depth LESS as in the
  template.
- Sound: `CopSiren01` from SOUND/INGAME's bank, 2.9 s from its lowest

## Session 111 -- 37f-3: either player's pause, on every console

The user, on the banner: "It worked perfectly! Now go back to 37f-3 and
continue work as normal. Never stop working." TASKS 66 is done

### What 37f-3 needed

Nothing in the game. Lockstep sends each place's START in its frame
record on that place's port, so every console's player on that port
asks for the pause on the same frame. `pause_menu_enter_pause` then
gives the pause's eight screens that port (SetScreenFilterPort, through
`hookSetScreenFilterPort`), and `flowInput` and the menu filter every
other port's presses. So one player's Quit Race or Restart is
everyone's, as on retail's split screen. Places past the two players'
have no port that reaches the flow (`JOYSTICK_PORTS` is 2; they race
as the AI for now, 37d-2).

### The test

`tools/run_azahar_lobby.ps1 -PauseBy 1` (with `-Quit` or `-Restart`)
has B pause instead of the host. Before B moves, the host presses Down,
then START, on B's pause. Each press must reach every copy on port 0,
and the first flow state after it must still be the Pause Menu on
Resume Race. The verdict also wants one pause on every copy, on the
pauser's port and on the same frame, and the other copy's presses on
the same frames. With `-PauseBy 0`, the default, B presses on the
host's pause.

- `-Quit -PauseBy 1`: B paused on frame 991 (seed dbfe8ce9), port 1 on
  both copies. The host's Down on frame 1081 and START on 1229 reached
  both copies on port 0, and each left the pause on Resume Race. B's
  three Downs then went from Resume to Restart, Options and Quit Race
  (View Replay grayed, the hidden items passed over). Both stopped
  after frame 2160 and went back to the lobby, then on to Select Car
  again; all 15 logged frames' parts the same.
- `-Restart -PauseBy 1`: B paused on frame 970 (seed 3d51a052). The
  host's presses on 1058 and 1213 left the pause on Resume Race. B's
  Restart started the race again on both, still in lockstep, and both
  raced on; all 19 logged frames' parts the same.
- `-Quit` (the host pauses, B presses): the host paused on frame
  1003 (seed e5574ec8), port 0. B's presses on 1089 and 1221 left the
  pause on Resume Race, and both stopped after frame 2010.

One screenshot of A after its START shows Restart Race lit. The log

### The plan: 37g in three slices

- **37g-1 (in progress): the hold, then the CPU.** A console lost
  mid-race holds the race on every console for `WirelessHoldSeconds`
  (90 by default). A box over the top screen names the lost console
  and counts down. Then that place's live bit is dropped, and every
  console hands its car to the AI on the frame of the first record
  built without the bit.
- **37g-2: the rejoin of a console whose link alone dropped.** Its race
  is still loaded. Re-peer it while the race is held, then go on from
  its last frame. wireless.c's host ejects a lost peer
  (`peer_lost`), and alive stays 0 for good. The network is closed
  mid-race, so this needs a way back in.
- **37g-3: a restarted console rejoins by its unique ID.** It comes in
  through Local Wireless, then Join. Candidates for the ID are
  CFGU_GenHashConsoleUnique and UDS's node info, as long as two Azahar
  copies differ in it. It then catches up: the setup, the load, and
  the records run fast from frame 0, or a snapshot.

### Next: 37g-2, re-peering a console whose link alone dropped

What stands in the way in wireless.c:

- `peer_lost(p, why, eject)` marks the peer dead. The host's timeout
  path ejects it (`udsEjectClient`) and puts its node in `goneMask`,
  and read_status takes no node in goneMask until the status shows it
  gone.
- `client_came` refuses a new node while the network is closed
  (`wireless_set_open(0)` at the lobby's start), ejecting it.
- A client whose host goes quiet is WIRELESS_LOST for good.

The plan to look at: during a hold, the host keeps the lost place
(alive 0, its node and name). A node that comes back during the hold,
with the same name, or later the unique ID (37g-3), is taken back into
that place with a fresh link. netstep then sees alive(p) again, clears
`lost[p]` and resends from the client's `need`. The netstep harness
needs links that come back (g_lost cleared), and netstep needs its
"back" paths (Session 111 removed them because nothing could test
them). Check what Azahar does to a UDS node whose room member drops
and comes back. A short loss can also be faked with a config line that
stops pumping for N seconds.

## Session 112, continued -- 37g-2 done: a console back in the hold

37g-2 lets a console whose link alone dropped (out of range and back)
rejoin the race during the hold. The race goes on from the frame it
held on. The code has its own commit, before these notes.

### wireless.c

- **The host.** `wireless_set_rejoin(on, ok)` unblocks new connections
  even on a closed network (`wireless_set_open` now blocks with
  `!(W.open || W.rejoin)`). It logs "open to a console lost" and
  "closed to a console lost". client_came now fetches the node's name
  and friend code seed (`uds_friendcodeseed`) first. On a closed
  network with rejoin on, `take_back` looks for a dead peer with the
  same name, and the same seed when both are nonzero. `ok(i)` must say
  the race still holds for it. The node gets a fresh wl_link in that
  peer's slot ("node n (NAME) back in place i", i the peer index). Any
  other node is ejected as before. The peer's seed is saved at the
  first join.
- **The client.** The join saves the host's MAC
  (`scan.network.host_macaddress`) and name. `wireless_rejoin`:
  udsDisconnectNetwork and udsUnbind, then udsScanBeacons with the MAC
  filter (into `s_scanBuf`, now shared with wireless_scan), then
  udsConnectNetwork and add_peer(host). It logs "looking for NAME
  again", "back on NAME's network, try k", or the failing call.
  wireless_leave turns rejoin off.
- **The test hook.** `wireless_test_deaf(ms)`: the pump drops every
  pulled packet and send_packet sends nothing until the time is up
  ("deaf for N ms", then "hears again"). No rejoin is tried while deaf.

### netstep.c

- hostPoll: a place in `lost[]` whose peer is alive again gets the
  records again (sendFrames now skips only a place lost and not
  alive), still held for. hostRead sets `back[p]` when it takes a PADS
  message (takePads now returns whether it took it) from a place held
  for. Only then does hostPoll say "place p back at frame n, after t
  ms" and clear the loss. A place on the link again is waited for
  NETSTEP_BACK_MS past the hold, then gone, its car the CPU's.
- clientPoll: takeFrames returns whether it took a FRAMES message. A
  client lost from its host is back only when one comes ("the host
  back at frame n, after t ms"): the host's records prove it was taken
  back. A client whose link is up again but has no word waits its hold
  plus NETSTEP_BACK_MS (3000) before it goes alone, for a rejoin that
  blocks across the hold's end.
- A client's netstep_held leaves out its own place: the host's records
  hold for it until its pads come.
- **Why the host waits for pads.** The first Azahar runs passed with the
  host saying "back" as soon as the node was taken back. But a console
  that restarted and joins from the lobby would be taken back too (same
  name and seed, the place held), and it sends no pads. The race would
  have held on every console for good, its link kept up by the lobby's
  keepalives. Now that console's car goes to the CPU when the hold and
  the grace are over.

### main.c

- `lockRejoin(now)`, after lockHoldMute each lockstep pass. The host
  calls `wireless_set_rejoin(held != 0, lockRejoinOk)`. lockRejoinOk
  maps the peer to its place through netrace_race()->peer and asks
  netstep_held. A client calls wireless_rejoin every LOCK_REJOIN_MS (2
  s) while it holds for its host and wireless is WIRELESS_LOST.
- `lockTestDrop()`, after lockTestFinish: at `WirelessTestDropFrame`
  it logs "lockstep: frame n, deaf for the test" and calls
  wireless_test_deaf(`WirelessTestDropMs`, 5000). Both settings are
  new in configitems (0 and 5000).
- The stop turns rejoin off.

### The checks

- **netstep_check: 55 scenarios, faults 0.** In the harness, a cut link
  stops messages both ways. Each end finds it lost by its own timeout,
  from the other's last pump, and a lost link has no inbox. `repeer()`
  brings a link back once both ends hold for each other, tried each
  second. `repeerLate` re-peers with 2 ms of the client's hold left.
  `repeerHalf` brings back only the client's end, `repeerMute` only the
  host's (no pad ever comes). `dropAgain` cuts a link a second time once
  it is back, and "lost" and "back" must then be said twice.
  `heardHold(c,p)` models which holds a console sees when two links are
  cut. A place's "gone" is checked at the hold's end, or at the hold
  plus NETSTEP_BACK_MS when only the host's end came up. The eight new
  scenarios are listed in netstep.md.
- **`--mutate`: 190 mutants, 187 caught, 3 equivalent.** New:
  ns-back-host-clear, -pads, -heard, -reset, -grace, -grace-alive,
  -send and -after; ns-back-client-clear, -got and -lost;
  ns-back-grace and -grace-alive; ns-takeframes-taken,
  ns-takepads-taken, ns-held-client-self and -none. Old patterns moved
  with the code. The back branch once cleared `back[p]` as well as the
  loss's start; with both, removing either changed nothing, so only the
  loss's start clears it now, and the second cut catches its removal.
- netrace_check and lobby_check: faults 0. The build passed.

### Next: 37g-3, a restarted console back in the race

A console that restarted has no race: it boots, goes to Local Wireless
and Join, and must get the race again. The pieces to work out:

- **The scan.** Mid-race the network is closed and the beacon still
  says the port's version. The joiner's list must show the race held
  for it: say so in the beacon's application data, and let a closed
  network through the scan's filter while it holds.
- **Telling the two backs apart.** A restarted console comes back
  through take_back, as 37g-2's does, but sends no pads. Today the host
  holds on and then gives its car to the CPU. Any message from it that
  is not the race's reads as "gone on" (a stop), which drops the place
  at once. It needs a lobby message of its own (LOBBY_MSG_REJOIN?). The
  host must answer with the race's setup: netrace's, with the event's
  state for a race past the first. The hold must then stretch while it
  loads and catches up.
- **The catch-up.** The host keeps only NETSTEP_RING (64) records.
  Replaying from frame 0 needs every record since GO: about 8 bytes for
  each place, plus the step, a frame. That is about 0.6 MB for 5
  minutes of eight consoles, less if runs of the same pad are packed.
  The restarted console loads the race, then runs the records without
  drawing until it reaches the held frame. Every other console stays
  held, under a box that says how far it has got, with the hold
  stretched while it gains. Measure how fast the sim runs without
  drawing on a New 3DS first: at 24 ms a frame with drawing, 5 minutes
  could take minutes to run again. A snapshot of the world is the other
  way, and much harder.
- **The ID.** The match by name and friend code seed already works for
  37g-2. Azahar's copies differ in console ID, so their seeds should
  differ: log the seeds to check.

## Session 112, continued -- 37g-3 done: a restarted console back in the race

37g-3 lets a console switched off or closed mid-race come back into its
place. It boots, goes to Local Wireless, Join, and joins the racing
host. The race stays held on every console while it loads and runs the
race again from frame 0, undrawn, until it is in step. netstep's half
is 2d84039; the rest (lobby, netrace, main.c, the harnesses and the
Azahar option) is b8bace6. 37g is done with it.

### netstep.c (2d84039)

- The host keeps every record it builds from GO (`hist`), delta-coded:
  the step, the places, a bit for each pad not the last record's and
  those pads, every 64th record whole (a key). 32 KB blocks, up to 128
  (4 MB). A block it cannot get stops the history, and a rejoin is then
  refused.
- `netstep_rejoin(p, now)` takes a place held for (lost, live, not
  left) and starts its hold again for the load. Its first pads end the
  load ("place p back"). The host then sends it the records from frame
  0, NETSTEP_BURST (4) messages at a time, and builds none until it is
  caught up ("place p caught up at frame n, after t ms").
- The FRAMES header grew to 23 bytes: byte 21 is the places loading or
  catching up, byte 22 the furthest behind's percent
  (`netstep_rejoining`). `netstep_behind()` is how far this console is
  behind. WL_VERSION is 2.

### lobby.c

- Every joiner sends `LOBBY_MSG_REJOIN` (0x19) once joined. A host in
  its lobby ignores it, but takes it as BACK from a client it awaits
  after a race (one that restarted as the race ended).
- A racing host's netrace answers `LOBBY_MSG_RESUME` (0x1a): 4 bytes
  (consoles, place, game type, cops), or 1 byte for refused. The
  joiner's lobby goes to `LS_RESUMING`, `LobbyRace.resume` set, the
  wait still up, and the race starts from the lobby with no car select.
- Refused: "Could not join the race.", OK, the question, the link down.
  `lobby_resume_failed` does the same for a setup the race cannot take.

### netrace.c

- The host's `racingRead` (NR_RACING) peeks each place's link. A REJOIN
  in the event's first race that netstep lets in gets RESUME, then the
  setup again ("place p back after a restart; the setup again"). A
  later race, or one heard while the next race is set up or loads, is
  refused.
- LOADED from a place resuming gets GO to it alone on the race's seed
  ("place p loaded again; go, seed s").
- A place resuming that netstep gave up on as it loaded is sent off the
  network (`wireless_drop`), its car the CPU's.
- The console back: `netrace_begin` goes straight to NR_WAIT ("back in
  the race, place p of n; the setup next"), takes the setup with the
  lobby up, and pushes the lobby back under the load.
- From RESUME the place's link has netrace's patience (30 s,
  `setPeerPatience`), until netstep no longer has it loading or catching
  up ("place p in step; its link's own patience"). The third Azahar run
  showed why: B's first frame after GO attaches the track for 4 s with
  no pump, and the host's 3 s link timeout dropped it. A race's start
  has netrace's patience on every link for the same reason.
- `netrace_back_in()`: 1 on a console back after a restart, in the race
  it came back into.

### wireless.c

- `wireless_drop(i)` ejects a client, its place kept as a lost one's.
- `wireless_set_peer_patience(i, ms)` sets one link's timeout.
- The seed is logged at each join and each take-back: "node n (NAME)
  joined, seed s" and "node n (NAME) back in place i, seed s".

### main.c

- Past NETSTEP_BEHIND (6) records the console back runs frames undrawn
  and draws only its progress every 250 ms: "Catching up with the
  race... N%" over a black top screen. It does so from its GO too,
  until the host's first record is in (`g_lockBack`): the first
  NETSTEP_DELAY records are its own, made at GO, and say nothing of how
  far behind it is. The user asked mid-session that a console back see
  no overview before it is in the race: the grid, fly-by and countdown
  are the race's past, run on the records' presses undrawn, and it is
  straight back in the race once caught up. Its master volume is 0 until
  it is in step, then fades back in as after an applet. The log says
  "lockstep: frame n, catching up begins" and "... is over".
- Every other console shows "NAME is coming back into the race... N%"
  in the hold's box and mutes the race.
- The texts are in the six languages (`portlang.c`).

### The checks

- netstep_check: 67 scenarios, faults 0; `--mutate` 259 mutants, 253

- netrace_check: 48 scenarios, faults 0; `--mutate` 252 mutants, 236
  caught, 16 equivalent. Twelve new scenarios, a console restarted
