## Session 113 -- 37f-2: the rejoin's differences were the checksum's

The user, 2026-10-15: "Continue where you left off (read prior .claude
session file, Azahar run completed but hasn't been analyzed), finish
the task then write up HANDOFF.MD etc. and stop". Then, mid-task: "When
you're done with this task, work on career, get career 100%, and as long
as everything's fully implemented, excepting little things like working
on multiplayer, lmk if its good for a public launch and I'll launch it".

The task was 37f-2's open difference: Session 112's `-Rejoin 1` run,
where B (restarted and caught up) differed from the host from frame 450
in the players part, and the host differed from B's first run at 917.

**The draw ruled out.** `run_azahar_lobby.ps1 -Blind 1` is new
(config `WirelessTestBlindFrame` and `WirelessTestBlindFrames`, main.c's
`lockTestBlind`). It runs one copy's race frames undrawn at the race's
pace. One run (seed 4b502558, B undrawn from frame 300 to 599) kept
every part the host's. So the draw was not the difference; the
catch-up's pace was.

**The sound's word.** `sound_update` runs at the top of each main-loop
pass, at most once per 8 ms of real time. During a catch-up, frames run
back to back, so anything the sound writes into a world struct lands on
other frames than on a console racing at the race's pace.
`CarState.RedLineSyncRPM` is the engine sound's
(`playerenginesound_update_to_red_line_rpm`, enginesound.c), and no
world code reads it. lockhash's new `mixState` hashes a CarState range
without it, in the parts and in the drive piece.

**The relative matrix.** The next `-Rejoin 1` run still split: B's
players part from frame 450, and the host against B's first run at
890. A test build (not committed) logged the players' CarState bytes
every 150 frames. The host and B's first run were the same byte for
byte to frame 900. The restarted B differed in `RedLineSyncRPM` and in
the second player's `RelCoordMatrix`, by a few units in the last place,
the same stale matrix from frame 450 to 1050, while `MatrixValid` was
0 on both consoles at every frame logged.

`RelCoordMatrix` is a cache. `carstate_get_transform_matrix` builds it
from the car's velocity (its heading below walking pace) when
`MatrixValid` is 0, and sets the bit. The car's mover clears the bit in
each step: `physicscar_update_car` with the velocity it copies, and the
belt, mellow, traffic and cop movers. The car sound's
`car_world_to_car` (carsound.c, for a body within 9 m) builds the
matrix between the frames, on the sound's real-clock gate, so a console
catching up built it on other frames than the host. While the bit is
clear nothing reads the matrix. Every change to its inputs is in the
world's step and clears the bit with it, but the debug warp. So a
matrix built between the frames is the one the next frame's first
reader would build: the checksum differed, the world did not. The
matrix now counts only while `MatrixValid` is set
(`docs/formats/lockhash.md`, "The relative matrix").

**Checked:**

- lockhash_check: faults 0. `--mutate`: 114 mutations, 110 caught,
  4 equivalent. New cases: `RedLineSyncRPM` moves no part and no piece,
  and the fields either side of it move theirs. With every car's
  `MatrixValid` 0, the matrix's first and last lanes move nothing,
  while `MatrixValid` itself, `BurnOutAllow` and `DistanceMoved` move
  theirs. With it set, the matrix moves the players part and the rel
  piece. The sound's word added 4 mutants and the stale matrix 5, all
  caught.
- `-Rejoin 1` on the build (seed b2c97ed7): PASS on both. B closed at
  frame 1042, restarted, and caught up to frame 1036 undrawn in 21 s.
  Every part was the host's at every frame logged, 0 to 1500, through
  the catch-up and after it. netstep's checksums matched to 2100, and
  the host's matched B's first run too.

**Frame 1809, still open.** The split nine frames after the test's
finish in Next Race (Sessions 108 and 109) is a real one, not the
checksum's: a slot's CarState differed in every piece. The stale matrix
cannot cause it, since nothing reads the matrix while it is stale. A
`-NextRace -Drive 30` run on this build (seeds ca54f485 and f20ce80b)
passed on both: every part the host's at all 27 frames logged, past the
finish on frame 1800 to the stop on 3033, then race 2 in lockstep. It
has now split 2 runs in 8. The driver piece will say which slot's
choice went first when it splits again.

## Session 114 -- TASKS 69b to 69e: the career's "View Event Tree"

The career's screen is ported: `eventtreeview.{c,h}`, retail's
tEventTreeView (EventTreeView.obj) and its classes, with the corrections
the port found written up in `docs/formats/event-tree-view.md`, "The
port".

- **The copies.** Retail draws the tree by copying Flailer objects and
  handing the copies to RenderFlailerBitmap and RenderFlailerText each
  frame. The view does the copying, and `main.c`'s hooks send each copy
  to `uirender_queue_copy`. Up to 256 a frame are drawn in their layer
  after the screens' own objects, with their alpha and their clip
  window. `draw_bitmap` and `draw_text` are now `_clipped`: a clipped
  bitmap has its quad and UVs cut.
- **The details' description** is wrapped from the text object's top
  left (TRACK_LINE_1) to the panel's right edge, in the port's style,
  after the layers (`etvDrawText`). The first build started it at the
  box's top and drew it over "Next track:"; the user caught it.
- **The Mode Selects** never wrote Fred's game type, so the first run
  logged "etv no tree". The `setEventTree` hook (`bscreens.h`) writes it,
  with the player count and the tree type.
- **`tools/run_azahar_career.ps1`** (`-CopsOn` for Hot Pursuit, `-Back`
  for B from Select Car): PASS on both trees. It covers the tree, right,
  down, up, the details, the reward, back twice, Select Car, and back to
  the details. It ran at 59 to 60 FPS, with no unmapped accesses.

Not ported: the reward's turning model (ModelViewer.obj), the help menu
(tHelpMenu), and the parallaxer's use (it is ticked; nothing reads it).

### Career: an event raced end to end (446860c)

- **"TestFinish n"** in sdmc:/nfshp2_config.txt (`configitems.h`, off by
  default). It finishes a race on a lone console n seconds after GO
  (`raceTestFinish` in `main.c`).
  - The player's car crosses in place "TestFinishPlace p". Before it,
    p - 1 of the other cars cross, in the leadership order. Then
    `racecoordinator_the_race_has_finished` does the rest.
  - It counts frames from `StartGoTimeFrames` (60 a second). The first
    try counted from `StartTime`, which is set before the fly-by, so it
    fired at GO.
  - The race times are projected from a race of a few seconds, so the
    records on Azahar's card after a run are not real ones.
- **`run_azahar_career.ps1 -Race [-FinishSeconds 20] [-FinishPlace 1]`**
  does the following:
  - It writes the two lines for the run and takes them out after.
  - A picks the car. A goes past the Pre Race Blurb and Pre Race Stats
    until "race: rc N, stage 4".
  - It holds the gas until the test's finish.
  - It presses A every 9 s through the end screens.
- **The End Game Menu needs the user's hand.** A alone stops there. A
  single race's menu is Restart Event, View Lap Times, Return to
  Championship, and each item's popup starts on No. Return is two rows
  down, then Left for Yes, then A. The user played that part by hand and
  said it "returns fine". The script does not do it yet.
- **The log of the run:** Events Unlocked, the Reward menu, Race
  Results, Best Lap Times, Best Total Times, the End Game Menu, the
  Autosave, then View Event Tree. Events 2 and 3 were unlocked and the
  autosave was written. That was Championship event 1.

All on Azahar with `run_azahar_career.ps1 -Race`, Championship tree:

  race 3 (National Forest, "Race 3 of 3"), the standings (Player1 30

### What the script does now

- **The End Game Menu.** `main.c` (`raceTestMenuLog`, with TestFinish
  on) logs it once each time: whether Next Race is its first row, the
  rows, the row highlighted, and whether it wraps. The script takes Next
  Race (A, Left for the popup's Yes, A) while there is one, else goes to
  Quit (Up once when it wraps) and says Yes.
- **The autosave.** Its question ("overwrite?") starts on No, as
  retail's does. A alone skipped the save, so a reboot lost the
  career. The script presses Left, then A ("memcard: saved").
- **A race's start** is "flow leave Pre Race Stats" counted per race.
  The race's stage lines come every second, so race 1's counted for the
  later ones and the gas (A held) never got past race 2's blurb.
- **A resumed event** ("etv resume event") goes on without car select.
- **-Path "down,right" -Event 5** steps the tree and checks the leaf.
  From event 3, Down is 7 and 6 is left of it; from 6, Up is 3; from 2,
  Down is 4 and 5 is right of it.
- **"TestFinishTime s"** (`configitems.h`, off by default) gives the
  player's car a lap of s seconds; `-LapSeconds`.
- After a won tournament the details panel shows "Next track:" with
  race 1's track: the race index is past the last track, and the panel
  falls back to track 0. Not a fault.
- Best Total Times stays empty after a test finish: a total time is
  only recorded when every lap was completed (`highscore.c`).
